`canActAsPlatformOperator` picks the scope — and the infra *page* derives `isOperator` from the server's `scope` field rather than a client role check, which is better than what was asked for), the abstracts chair-override, MCP consent. **Flagged for an owner call, not changed:** `api-keys` + `oauth-clients` let a SUPER_ADMIN grant the `INTERNAL` rate-limit tier, org-bound so not a leak, but on the platform it lets a tenant lift its own ceiling. **The lesson, and it generalises past this repo:** `canActAsPlatformOperator` was written correctly in August with a header comment naming this exact risk — that excluding SUPER_ADMIN from `ASSIGNABLE_USER_ROLES` "is a property of one screen, not an invariant" — and then **only eight files adopted it**. *Writing the right predicate is half the job; the sweep that adopts it is the other half. A guard that exists but is never called is indistinguishable from no guard, and is worse than none, because its existence reads as coverage.* Hence a gate rather than a code review: new **[check-platform-operator.sh](scripts/check-platform-operator.sh)** (gating in CI) pins three invariants — `x-org-id` has exactly **one reader**, every listed platform surface calls the operator predicate, and no platform surface decides authorisation with a **standalone** `SUPER_ADMIN` comparison (the coarse `ADMIN || SUPER_ADMIN` pre-filter is explicitly allowed, because a rule banning the string would push authors into working around it). **All three mutation-verified**, and the second check exists only because the first version of the gate *passed* a mutation: it was per-file, so reverting one of a route's two handlers to a bare check went undetected — the same weakness `check-tenant-als.sh` had already solved with a count invariant. **Master is byte-identical**: `PLATFORM_ORG_ID` is unset there, so `canActAsPlatformOperator` reduces to the previous role test and the dashboard org switcher keeps working — asserted by a named test rather than reasoned about, and that test is mutation-verified against reverting the guard. **Also this round: the eight "unpoliced models" audit closed with zero new decisions** — five carry a required `eventId` and are therefore the **Event RLS** decision, two are `userId`-keyed and follow **item 6**, and `McpOAuthClient` is *correctly* global (a DCR registration precedes consent, so it has no org to carry). The list had **missed** `ApiKey` / `McpOAuthAccessToken` / `McpOAuthAuthCode`, which *do* carry `organizationId` and have no policy — and must not get one, because they are read on the **authentication** path, which is what *establishes* the lane; policying them would deadlock login. Recorded explicitly because to the next sweeper they look exactly like an oversight. **General rule: anything read before identity is resolved cannot be protected by identity.** +8 tests (suite 5766 → **5774**); tsc 0, eslint 0, build clean, all four tenancy gates green. Full record: [PLATFORM_DECISIONS.md](docs/PLATFORM_DECISIONS.md) § "ADMIN-gate sweep".

- **In-house visitor analytics, and the reasoning that rejected Google Analytics first (August 20, 2026)**: EA-SYS could tell you a great deal about people who **completed** something, and nothing at all about the people who did not. `Registration` has carried `utmSource`/`utmMedium`/`utmCampaign` since the tickets page grew a UTM link builder, so *"which channel produced this registration"* was already answered, first-party. **What was missing was the denominator**: 500 opened the register page, 80 registered, and the other 420 were invisible. **GA was rejected for three independent reasons, any one sufficient**, and the reasoning is preserved in [docs/ANALYTICS_PLAN.md](docs/ANALYTICS_PLAN.md) §2 so the next person to ask does not re-derive it. (a) §6 of [SECURITY_AND_PRIVACY_POSTURE.md](docs/SECURITY_AND_PRIVACY_POSTURE.md), a document given to **EHS, a UAE federal health authority**, states there is *"no third-party analytics of any kind"*, and two paragraphs earlier flags **Google Fonts** as a concern because it discloses visitor IPs to Google. Loading GA on the same pages would contradict a position taken in writing. (b) GA4's pageview sends `page_location`, the **full URL including the query**, and **eight public routes carry bearer tokens or a person's name**: `/confirmation?id=…&name=…` (a registrant's first name, minted by [checkout/route.ts:152](src/app/api/public/events/%5Bslug%5D/checkout/route.ts#L152)), `/reset-password?token=…&email=…`, `/reimbursement/{token}` (which gates passport scans and bank details), `/rsvp/{token}`, `/speaker-form/{token}`. That also breaches Google's own ToS, so the failure mode is losing the property, not only a regulator. (c) There is **no consent mechanism anywhere in `src/`**, so GA would have been non-compliant on day one under both GDPR and the UAE PDPL the speaker agreement already cites by name. **Plausible and Matomo were weighed and also rejected**: Plausible CE requires **ClickHouse** (verified against its published `compose.yml`, not assumed), which would put a new dataset on the **unencrypted root volume**, §0.2, the open gap, and outside the `pg_dump` DR stream entirely; Matomo defaults to cookies-on and IP-stored, exactly the wrong posture for a client reading the third-party table sceptically. **The principle worth carrying: for analytics the control is data minimisation, not encryption.** TLS and at-rest encryption are both fine and both irrelevant, because Google is the *intended recipient*; encryption protects data from parties who should not have it and does nothing about disclosure to the party you are deliberately sending it to. **What shipped, in five gated phases.** Identity is `HMAC(salt, siteId + ip + userAgent)` where the salt is **derived from the UTC date**, so rotation happens by construction: no cron to fail, no state to stick, and yesterday's identifier is unreachable today. `siteId` is inside the hash so one person on two tenants is two unrelated identities, which is what stops two tenants correlating a visitor between them. **There is no `ipAddress` column**, not nullable, absent, because a column that does not exist cannot be filled in later. **No cookie, no localStorage, no sessionStorage**, stricter than required and the reason no consent banner is needed; sessions are derived from a 30-minute window, which produces a boundary artifact that is accepted and documented and must not be "fixed" with client storage. Measurable paths are an **allow-list** ([path-policy.ts](src/analytics/core/path-policy.ts)), never an exclude-list, because an exclude-list fails open the next time someone adds a public route, the same inversion applied to `/uploads` the day before, and the stored path **never contains a query string**, asserted rather than assumed. Writes are **buffered** (25 hits or 2s, the `SystemLog` pattern) because one INSERT per pageview would put public traffic on the pool that serves the registration desk, which has already been exhausted once (P2024, June 10). Born tenancy-compliant: org stamped at write, **one `createMany` per organisation inside that org's lane** (one container's buffer holds hits for several tenants, so a single batch under one lane would be correctly rejected), a strict policy in [prisma/rls/analyticsevent.sql](prisma/rls/analyticsevent.sql), harness fixtures and 8 assertions, and a CI-gate entry verified to fail when the wrap is removed. The dashboard funnel is built from **route patterns rather than conversion events**, so it works from ordinary pageviews with no extra instrumentation, and its final step comes from the **`Registration` table** rather than a beacon: a conversion hit can be lost to a closed tab, and under-reporting the one number that is independently knowable would be a bad trade. Steps count **distinct visitors, not pageviews**, someone refreshing the register page five times is one person considering it. **Two bugs found by writing tests, not by reading code.** The buffer stranded a batch: when a flush was in flight and the buffer refilled to the threshold, the enqueue path returned early without scheduling a timer, so those hits sat until another happened to arrive, under a burst that ends abruptly, which is exactly what the end of a registration rush looks like, **the last batch would never have been written**. And the "no secret configured" alarm logged an error *per pageview*, in a state that is completely ordinary between deploying and configuring; latched to once per container, because the thousandth copy of a sentence adds nothing but buries `/logs` and feeds the SES alert hourly. **Verified end to end on production** after deploy: endpoint 204, row recorded, zero analytics errors. **Deliberately impossible, and stated in §3.2 of the plan so it is a knowing choice**: cross-day individual journeys, cross-device identity, *"did Dr X visit"*, and ad-platform bid optimisation. If any becomes a requirement this is the wrong design and the conversation reopens with a consent banner attached. **Deferred**: country (needs self-hosted MaxMind to avoid adding a third party), the org-level cross-event view, and publication of `core/` as a package, designed for extraction, with an eslint zone forbidding it from importing EA-SYS at all, but publishing is a maintenance commitment and a stale repo with open security issues is a *negative* trust signal on the same questionnaire. 136 analytics tests; salt rotation, tenant separation and query-string stripping mutation-verified. Suite 5605 → **5741**. **Operator note: `ANALYTICS_SALT_SECRET` must be set or nothing is recorded**, and it should be treated as permanent, changing it makes every returning visitor look new from that day.

- **A live webinar that would not join, and the three refusals that came out of it (August 19, 2026)**, Attendees hit `zoom:join-denied:unauthenticated`, a red herring twice over: both times the person signed in within 20 seconds and got through, and that line fires **by design** every time someone tests the attendee flow in a private window. The real failure was invisible: **`3712 Signature is invalid`, raised by Zoom inside the attendee's browser**, where we had no logs at all. The server minted a signature, the join route answered 200, and the truth had to be dug out of `Organization.settings` in the production database while a live test was blocked. **Every defect that day shared one shape: the wrong value was accepted everywhere it was entered, and failed only somewhere we could not see.** Three wrong values in sequence. First, `sdkKeyProd` pointed at a Meeting SDK app that **had been deleted from the Marketplace**, credentials of a non-existent app cannot validate, and nothing anywhere noticed the app was gone. Second, it was replaced with the **Server-to-Server OAuth Client ID**, a live app with no SDK capability whatsoever, which fails identically and forever. Third, the documented recovery (delete the Zoom meeting and recreate it, because `PUT .../zoom` is only a *refresh* and live streaming can be enabled at CREATE only) walks into a dropdown that defaults to **Meeting** on a WEBINAR event, silently downgrading it, breaking panelists (that route refuses `MEETING`) and every analytic (`/report/webinars/...` does not exist for meetings). **The second mistake was the UI's fault, not the operator's**, and the same trap caught a second person an hour later: the credentials card holds **three fields carrying the words "Client ID"**, and the SDK ones were labelled `SDK Key (Client ID)` with placeholder `Prod Client ID`, sitting directly beneath a Server-to-Server section whose field is called Client ID. Someone holding one Client ID does the obvious thing. So the fixes are **refusals and better labels rather than documentation**: pasting the OAuth Client ID into either SDK field is rejected at save (compared against the client id being *saved*, since one request can set both); the webinar anchor **cannot** be created as a Meeting (`WEBINAR_ANCHOR_REQUIRES_WEBINAR`, scoped to the anchor so a rehearsal meeting elsewhere still works); `defaultMeetingType` derives from `eventType` so the trap is never armed; and both SDK sections state plainly that they are **optional**, what happens if left blank, and that a Server-to-Server app has no SDK credentials. **Observability was the other half.** `zoom:signature-generated` records mode, meeting number, role and a six-char key prefix, but at INFO, and **only warn+ reaches `SystemLog` on EC2**, so that line never appears in `/logs`; the fix that mattered was threading the same prefix into the **warn-level** browser failure report (`zoom:join-failed-in-browser`, authenticated + rate-limited), the line an operator actually reads. Dev credentials on a production deployment log at **error** and page, deliberately, because signing still *succeeds* there and Zoom rejects it later in a browser, so the alarm must fire at signing time or nowhere. Credential changes are finally **audited**: before/after **fingerprints** (six chars + length) for keys, `{ rotated: true }` for secrets, never a secret and not even a prefix of one, previously the only trace was a single `configuredAt` that each save overwrote, which is exactly why "what was the SDK key before 11:50, and who changed it" had no answer. **The durable lesson: there is no server-side test for Meeting SDK credentials, because Zoom publishes no endpoint that validates them.** The Test Connection button exercises `/users/me` over OAuth, so it proves the *Server-to-Server* credentials and says nothing about the SDK ones. The only instrument that can answer "are these good?" is an attendee joining a live webinar. **Also clarified, because it drove every decision that afternoon: the Meeting SDK app is OPTIONAL.** Server-to-Server runs the webinar (create, panelists, recordings, attendance, RTMP config) and simply cannot render video; the SDK is the only way to draw it inside our own page. Leave the SDK fields blank and `generateZoomSignatureForOrg` returns null, the route falls back to `mode: "url"`, and attendees open Zoom, which works. **Wrong credentials fail worse than none, because none has a working fallback.** The third path, RTMP → MediaMTX → HLS, needs no SDK app either and was verified end to end on prod (container up, 1935 reachable from the internet, nginx proxying, HLS answering 404-not-502); its cost is that an HLS viewer is never a Zoom participant, so attendance/polls/Q&A see only host and panelists, and attendance-gated CME certificates would find an empty room. Verified in a browser against the local prod copy, **both directions**: pasting the OAuth Client ID is refused **and `configuredAt` does not move**, while a real key saves and does, a guard that blocks everything would be worse than none. Local testing also **corrected a warning I had given from code reading alone**: `defaultMeetingType` is per-EVENT, and the local event carried `WEBINAR` while the prod event being fixed carried `MEETING`, so the trap was real for that event specifically. Commits `3bf3e074` → `79aece0c`; suite 5571 → **5596**; tsc 0, eslint 0, build clean. Docs: [ZOOM_INTEGRATION.html](docs/ZOOM_INTEGRATION.html) §"Two Zoom Apps, and only one of them is required" + §"Credential failure modes", and the operational traps in [WEBINAR_EVENTS.md](docs/WEBINAR_EVENTS.md) §"Edge cases & known limitations".

- **All file handling behind one module, the `/uploads` deny-list flipped to an allow-list, and a UAE plan that AWS cancelled mid-build (August 19, 2026)** — Started as "keep sensitive data in the UAE" for an Emirates Health Services questionnaire, and the reasoning corrected the goal twice before any code was written. **First correction: moving the EC2 box to Dubai would have been the worst available option.** The app and Supabase are both in `ap-south-1`, so a database round trip is 1-2ms; Dubai is ~33ms away. **Application-to-database latency multiplies (one page view is many queries) while user-to-application latency does not (one page view is one round trip)**, so moving compute alone makes every query ~20x slower to buy a partial residency answer. **Second: the database cannot move at all** — Supabase has 16 regions and none is in the Middle East (verified against their docs), so Mumbai was already the closest reachable one. What was actually movable was object storage, which sits on no hot path, so **document residency and compute residency are separable** and only the files needed to go. **The survey then found the real problem.** [storage.ts](src/lib/storage.ts) covered photos, media, certificate PDFs and Stripe receipts only; **nine document routes hand-rolled `mkdir` + `writeFile` and a dozen read sites carried their own copy of the traversal guard — and those were exactly the sensitive ones** (passports, CVs, bank details, employer letters), including both paths a passport arrives through. A storage change would have had to be applied correctly in twenty places, where missing one leaves sensitive files behind while the change reports as done. **Phase 1 consolidated all fourteen sites behind four primitives** (`uploadFile` / `readStoredFile` / `deleteStoredFile` / `listStoredFiles`), net **88 lines removed** from the touched routes because each lost its own copy of the same logic. `requirePrefix` is a **required** argument, not optional, because it is the guard every read site re-implemented and an optional guard is one somebody eventually omits; `StorageFailureReason` keeps traversal / prefix / not-found distinguishable in `/logs` (a traversal attempt is a security event, a missing file is operational) while returning one 404 either way so no route becomes an existence oracle. **The one real security change: the `/uploads` catch-all carried a DENY-list of five private prefixes, which fails OPEN** — add a sixth and it is world-readable until someone remembers one file, with no test failing, because a test asserting the OLD prefixes are 403 stays green while a NEW one is wide open (that file's own comments described the trap). Inverted to an allow-list in [upload-prefixes.ts](src/lib/upload-prefixes.ts) the same mistake fails closed; the permitted set is byte-identical and pinned as a SET so a prefix cannot quietly join or leave it. **"Public" there means only "served to anyone who knows the URL"** — certificates are on the list because that is how they are delivered, to a recipient signed in to nothing — which is a different axis from where bytes are stored, and conflating the two is how someone later breaks certificate delivery while trying to improve privacy. **Phase 2** added a region-agnostic [S3 provider](src/lib/storage-s3.ts), dynamically imported so the AWS SDK is not loaded while the provider is `local`, credentials from the instance role so nothing enters `.env`; three guards **mutation-verified** because each fails silently — dropping `IsTruncated` pagination (the prune worker stops seeing anything past 1000 files and still reports a clean sweep), classifying `NoSuchBucket` as not-found (a wrong bucket name looks like an empty one), and skipping the prefix guard on the S3 branch (S3 has no symlinks, so the string checks are the ONLY guard there). **Then AWS cancelled the destination.** Switching to `me-central-1` returned a console notice that the region "has suffered damage as a result of the conflict in the Middle East", cannot reliably support customer applications, that customers should **migrate resources OUT and restore from remote backups**, with recovery expected to take **several months**. Provisioning identity-document storage into a region under an active evacuation notice was refused. **The owner had asked, hours earlier, how we would recover in under five minutes if a regional conflict took the UAE out for two weeks — the scenario was not hypothetical, and the answer arrived before the design did.** That question produced the rule that now holds regardless of region: **never delete the local `public/uploads/` copies** (they are the warm standby that makes failover one env var plus a ~22s redeploy) and **the provider switch must always be reversible by one env var and a redeploy** — the original plan's "remove the local copies after the bake period" step is struck permanently. Repointed to `ap-south-1` as a **durability** project (versioning, KMS encryption, 11 nines, off the unencrypted EBS root volume) and the staging ground for the UAE move; **Bahrain rejected** as a different country that does not deliver UAE residency and sits 500km away in the same theatre. **The latency gate was run for real rather than estimated**, from the box against existing buckets: Mumbai EC2 → S3 `ap-south-1` TCP connect **2.5ms**, → `ap-southeast-1` **62ms**, local disk below measurement resolution; Dubai (~1,900km) brackets between, validating the ~33ms published figure with real numbers. **In-region is cheap enough that the read-through disk cache fallback is resolved as unnecessary**, and no replication rule is needed either, because keeping the local copies means the existing hourly Singapore sync keeps working unchanged (three copies: S3 Mumbai, local disk, Singapore). `supporting-document-prune-worker` moved onto `listStoredFiles` so it works under any backing store — it briefly carried a loud non-local refusal during Phase 1, deliberately, because **a reaper that silently reaps nothing is the worst shape of failure**; the guard was deleted in Phase 2 once the gap it announced was actually closed. **Eight tests across three suites broke on the first full run, all one cause: tests asserting `fs.unlink` was called rather than that the file was gone** — fixed by completing the mocks so the real containment guard still runs, not by stubbing the storage layer out, which would have removed the coverage instead of keeping it. Also deleted `storedFileExists`, added speculatively in the first commit and called by nothing. Verified live on prod after each deploy: a real speaker photo 200 with the correct content type, `speaker-docs` / `reimbursements` / `resident-letters` all 403, both containers healthy, zero storage errors. Six commits (`cc99f773` → `83f4c49d`); suite 5523 → **5571**; tsc 0, eslint 0, build clean throughout. Plan, decision history and the Console runbook: [docs/UAE_DOCUMENT_RESIDENCY_PLAN.md](docs/UAE_DOCUMENT_RESIDENCY_PLAN.md). **Nothing is enabled: `STORAGE_PROVIDER` is unset on prod, so the S3 provider and the migration script are inert until a bucket exists and two env vars are set.**

- **Inbound contacts import from the EU mirror, and the do-not-import screen that had to be rewritten after it deleted real people (August 18, 2026)** — The `contacts_centralv1` sync had only ever run outbound. Owner asked to pull the other way: of 60,300 mirror rows, **56,950 were not in EA-SYS** (11 years of EventsAir + Mailchimp history). New [import-contacts-central.ts](scripts/import-contacts-central.ts) does it in ~24s, enrich-only (fills blanks, unions tags, never writes `eventIds` because the mirror holds event NAMES and we hold cuids), and **merges 2,756 people the mirror stores twice because its PK is case-sensitive and ours is not**. **The load-bearing lesson is about the spam screen.** The owner spotted a contact whose `firstName` was literally `Dont click me: https://racetrack.top/…` on a disposable mailbox — form spam the import had faithfully copied. A name is an **output surface** (merged into email greetings, printed on badges), so it needs input suspicion; hence [contact-import-blocklist.ts](src/lib/contact-import-blocklist.ts). **The first version was wrong in both directions and an adversarial review caught it after it had already done damage:** a bare-TLD rule applied to `organization` deleted a lab worker at "Al borg medical laboratories.com" and a pharmacist at "blue coast medical.com" (and would have deleted anyone employed at Roche.com or Sanofi.com), while missing `bit.ly`, `t.me`, `wa.me` and `spam.club` entirely. The rewrite splits by field: **NAME fields strict** (scheme, `www.`, known-abuse TLD, or a shortener host), **employer/job-title lenient** (scheme or `www.` only — a company name ending in its own domain is ordinary CRM data, and those fields never reach a greeting). **The TLD list is a treadmill and is still correct here**, because the reviewer's suggested generic `word.word` rule deletes **78 real contacts** whose names are this audience's ordinary forms: `Dr.Omar`, `Prof.DR Abdelraouf`, `Al.Rayes`, `Ma.Theresa`, `Most.Gulshan Ara`. Both directions mutation-verified. Also from the review: the quarantine file **truncated on every run**, so the only copy of what was deleted was one `writeFile` away from gone (now timestamped, `flag: "wx"`, mode 0600); the purge screened the **whole org** rather than imported rows (now scoped to the `central-import` tag, `--all-contacts` opt-in) and silently severed `CrmContact.contactId` via `SetNull` (referencing ids now captured before deleting). **Also shipped:** the contacts **tag filter** became a searchable popover with usage counts — the import took the tag vocabulary from 4 to 125 and the flat pill row became taller than the table it filtered; `GET /api/contacts/tags` stopped reading every contact into Node to compute ~120 strings; and the outbound sync now sends **`title`** (raw enum `DR`, deliberately unlike `role`'s formatted label), which needed one additive column on the target. **Known and deferred:** that tags aggregate is the first `$queryRaw` on a tenant-scoped table, and [db.ts](src/lib/db.ts) states raw ops are deliberately outside the tenant lane, so under RLS it fail-closes to an empty tag list — and because it replaced the route's only swept model read, `check-tenant-als.sh` now passes vacuously on `src/app/api/contacts`. `getTagColor` is also now a 5th copy (one already divergent). Both recorded in ROADMAP. **The blocklist is not yet wired into the public registration form**, which is the door the spam originally walked in.

- **Parallel sessions stop reading as a sequence (August 17, 2026, organizer request)** — Asked to improve the public agenda for a multi-day multi-track event. Three sessions on EHSMHC2026 run at **exactly 10:15–13:00 in three different halls**, and they rendered as three stacked cards with the time printed three times, so someone reading top to bottom takes them for a sequence. The cost of getting that wrong is walking into the wrong room. They now collapse into ONE block headed "3 parallel sessions" with a column per hall; on mobile the columns stack, each under its own hall label. **The proposal round mattered more than the build.** Reading the real data first (three events, read-only via MCP) corrected two things I would otherwise have got wrong. **(1) Grouping is on OVERLAP, not on an equal start time.** On BHS2026 a workshop runs 11:40–13:00 across Session V (11:25–12:20) and Session VI (12:20–13:15); nothing shares a start time, so an equality check finds nothing and the attendee never learns there was a choice. **(2) Columns are keyed by HALL, not by session.** That same BHS cluster is three sessions but two halls, so Plenary Hall is one column holding V then VI in time order, beside Workshop Room. Keying by session would have given three columns and presented two back-to-back talks in the same room as alternatives to each other. Both are pinned by tests **mutation-verified** to fail (`<=` on the boundary fuses every back-to-back session on a single-track day; keying by session id breaks the BHS case and the double-booked-room case). Logic lives in a pure, testable [agenda-layout.ts](src/lib/agenda-layout.ts); a cluster resolving to one hall degrades to ordinary single cards, which is also what makes the track filter behave (filtering to one hall gives the plain list, not a one-column grid). Breaks are laid out apart from the programme and merged back by start time, so a coffee break inside a long workshop cannot split the block around it. **The one real bug found in the preview was a container-query trap:** the topic run-sheet uses `sm:flex-row`, and `sm:` reads the VIEWPORT, so inside a ~300px column on a 1280px screen it still tried to lay out side by side and clipped the topic titles ("OCD/BD", "Tourette"). Columns now always stack. **Also (owner):** day tabs promoted to a primary tab strip with the date under each label, track chips demoted to a tinted strip beneath, since the day is what you pick first on a multi-day programme and the track is a refinement within it; both sat side by side as equal pills before. That also fixed a pre-existing bug where **Day 1 and All Days were both highlighted on first load**. **Owner rulings this round:** tracks ARE rooms ("actual rooms like in conference rooms or halls" — true on every event with real sessions), the label stays "Track" rather than being renamed, and the block header says just "N parallel sessions" with no "choose one". **Deliberately NOT built** (ROADMAP §"Public agenda — the rest of the multi-track proposal"): speaker de-duplication (BHS lists every speaker twice, as a session chip and again under their own topic), per-session add-to-calendar, live-now marker, sticky filters, per-session anchors, speaker search, print-as-grid, personal starred agenda. **Flagged, needs an owner call:** the public agenda is currently **404 for attendees on every event** — `settings.agendaPublished` is unset on all seven published events, so `/e/<slug>/agenda` is unreachable publicly everywhere. +17 tests (suite 5453 → **5470**). Gate: tsc 0, eslint 0, build clean.

- **Session description shows under the title, no click (August 17, 2026, organizer request)** — Organizer reported the description "not showing up on agenda". It was two different things behind one complaint. On the **public** agenda it rendered only after clicking the card to expand (the whole card was a `<button>` whose sole job was toggling it), so on a programme people read like a printed document it looked absent. On the **dashboard** agenda it rendered **nowhere at all** — `grep` found it only in the edit form and the detail sheet, so an organizer could not see a description without opening the session to edit it. Both now render directly under the session title, `whitespace-pre-line` so typed line breaks survive; the public card's expand state, chevron and print-only duplicate are deleted, and the wrapper reverts from `<button>` to `<div>` because **a card that invites a click and does nothing is worse than a plain one**. Added to the dashboard calendar tooltip too (`line-clamp-4`). **Also fixed, found while reading the save path:** the agenda form sent `description: rest.description || undefined`, so emptying the box omitted the field, the PUT read that as "unchanged", and **a description could never be cleared** — you got a success toast and the old text stayed. The service already maps `""` to null and the route's Zod takes a string but not null, so an edit now sends the raw value, empty string included; a create still omits it. Sizing checked read-only on prod first, and it reframed the report: the Hematology Summit has **15 sessions and 0 descriptions**, Middle East Heart Failure **12 and 0**, so on the events most likely being looked at there was nothing to show anywhere. **No test added for the clear-description fix, deliberately:** the service half was already correct, the defect was in the form payload, and this repo has no component tests for the agenda page — a service test would pin something that never broke (the "a test that cannot fail is not load-bearing" rule). Gate: tsc 0, eslint 0, vitest 5453, build clean.

- **Notification switches that actually switch something (August 17, 2026, organizer request)** — Owner asked for a control over the "Session Created" notification. The finding that reframed the task: the two switches **already** in Settings → General → Notifications (`notifyOnRegistration`, `notifyOnAbstractSubmission`) saved correctly and were **read by nothing** — `grep` for either key outside the settings page returned zero hits, and on prod **one event had both set to `false` and was still being notified**. Adding a third switch beside them would have shipped a third one that lies. **A flag that is displayed but not enforced is worse than no flag, because it silently spends the trust of the person who set it** (same class as the June-24 `registrationOpen` no-op and the RSVP `campaign.isActive` finding). **The gate lives inside `notifyEventAdmins`**, not at its **37 call sites**, so a new caller cannot forget it and a switch cannot end up honoured on one path and ignored on another; `settings` rides along on the `findUnique` that function already performs, so gating costs **no extra query**. Callers opt in with a `setting` key, which is destructured out before the `createMany` spread (it is a routing hint, not a column — leaking it would make Prisma reject every gated notification, pinned by test). **A caller that passes no key can never be suppressed**, which is deliberate and mutation-verified: the `⚠ Group invoice could not be created` family and every PAYMENT alert omit it, because turning off registration notices must not silence a failed invoice. Reads **fail OPEN** — only an explicit `false` suppresses, so absent keys, a corrupt blob, `0` or `""` all still send, since a missed notification is invisible to whoever needed it while an unwanted one is merely noise. Keys + UI copy live in a client-safe [notification-settings.ts](src/lib/notification-settings.ts) (the Settings page cannot import `notifications.ts`, which pulls in `db` and the push client — the "no Node imports in the client bundle" trap), and the panel now **renders from that list**, so panel and gate cannot disagree and a fourth switch is one line. Verified the event PUT takes `settings` as an open `z.record` rather than a whitelist, so the new key is not a dead write (the July-27 CME-accreditor lesson). Also fixed in passing: **"Session Created" was filed as a `REGISTRATION` notification**, which is why an agenda change arrived looking like a sign-up — `Notification.type` is a plain string column, so the correction to `SESSION` needed no migration, and the bell's icon map (already `|| Bell`-guarded) gained a calendar. Live state checked first: 19 of 20 events have both switches on, the only one off is a DRAFT test event, so enforcing them makes nothing live go quiet. +12 tests (suite 5441 → **5453**), two mutation-verified. **Deliberately not built:** switches for sessions-imported, speaker-added, event-updated, bulk-email-sent (offered, owner picked session-created only); money, check-in, review and signup notifications stay unconditional.

- **TBA on the programme, derived rather than stored (August 17, 2026, organizer request)** — A session with no speaker rendered a blank space, so an attendee could not tell an unfilled slot from a broken page. An organizer had worked around it by creating a `Speaker` literally named **`TBC TBC`**, which is the finding worth keeping: a `Speaker` row is an identity, not a label, so that one placeholder also minted companion registration **#008** (CONFIRMED, Faculty badge, **entry barcode minted**, so a badge for a non-person would print and scan) and, because `Speaker` is `@@unique([eventId, email])` and the form demands an address, it borrowed **a real doctor's personal email**, making his inbox the destination for every speaker email that event sends to "TBC". **A placeholder is safe in a presentation field and dangerous in an identity table; the tell that a workaround is fighting the schema is when it forces you to invent data the schema insists must be real.** Replaced by a derived label in [session-enums.ts](src/lib/session-enums.ts) (`TBA_LABEL`/`TBC_LABEL` + `sessionNeedsTba`/`topicNeedsTba`) that clears itself the moment a speaker is assigned, with nothing to remember to delete. **Two conditions, both established from live data rather than assumed, both mutation-verified:** (1) it delegates the type test to `isBreakSessionType` instead of comparing to `"SESSION"`, because **both genuinely-unassigned slots on prod are Symposia** and an equality check catches neither, the same trap that would have reclassified Workshop and Symposium as coffee breaks when they were added; (2) it requires no speaker **anywhere** in the session, session-level roles and topic speakers alike, because "Keynote Lecture" on EHS carries zero `SessionSpeaker` rows and names its speaker on its single topic, so a session-level-only check would print TBA directly above the keynote speaker's name. `topicNeedsTba` suppresses the row-level label when the session already reads TBA, so an empty session says it once. Applied to the public [agenda](src/app/e/%5Bslug%5D/agenda/page.tsx) and [session page](src/app/e/%5Bslug%5D/session/%5BsessionId%5D/page.tsx) **and to the `{{moderatorDetails}}` run-sheet** in [speaker-agreement.ts](src/lib/speaker-agreement.ts) (previously a bare dash in HTML and nothing at all in the plain-text mirror — that document is handed to someone running a room, where a blank cell reads as a rendering fault), from ONE helper so the email cannot drift from the web page. The organizer's own agenda deliberately gets **a chase-list count** ("2 sessions still need a speaker", naming them) rather than TBA on the cards, computed from the same predicate so it can never disagree with what attendees see. Impact verified read-only on prod before shipping: **exactly two cards change**, both Industry Symposia, and all 26 topics already carry a speaker; `agendaPublished` is false on all 7 published events, so this lands **before** first publication rather than fixing something attendees have seen. **Not in this round** (docs/SPEAKER_TBA_PLAN.md §7). **TBC is PARKED** (owner, same day — do not build without an explicit go-ahead; `TBC_LABEL` stays defined and unused because it settles the wording, not because work is imminent): TBC would cover the 29-of-34 named-but-INVITED assignments on the Hematology Summit (no public surface reads `Speaker.status`, so an invited speaker renders identically to a confirmed one); hiding the one **DECLINED** speaker still attached to a workshop, which if added later falls through to TBA on its own with no extra rule; and a "no speaker needed" tick for slots that are speakerless by design. +24 tests (suite 5417 → **5441**). Gate: tsc 0, eslint 0, build clean.

- **The 24h session timeout was never in force: one config was silent, and silence is not inheritance (August 17, 2026)**. Owner question: *"I did not login for 2 days, how come today I still logged in."* The documented answer (24h **rolling idle**, so the window slides on use) did not survive the follow-up: the laptop was **shut down all weekend**, so nothing read the session. Evidence settled it in two prod reads. `LoginEvent` showed the last actual sign-in on **Aug 7**, `User.lastSeenAt` showed activity on **Aug 17**. Ten days, two weekends, a 24h timeout. **Cause: two NextAuth instances over one cookie.** [auth.ts](src/lib/auth.ts) builds the Node instance and set `maxAge: 24h`; [proxy.ts](src/proxy.ts) builds a **second**, Edge instance for middleware RBAC from [auth.config.ts](src/lib/auth.config.ts), which had **no `session` block at all**. A silent config does not inherit its sibling; it opts into NextAuth's **default of 30 days**. Middleware runs on every dashboard route and re-issues the cookie, so the real lifetime was **30 days rolling**. Aug 7 + 30 days lands in September, which is why a shut-down weekend never touched it. **The file had already solved this exact problem once and not generalised it**: its own `mapTokenToSessionUser` comment reads *"Keep this file the single source of truth so the two call sites can't drift"* about session **claims**. Nobody carried the reasoning to session **lifetime**. **Fixed structurally, not by writing the number twice**: one exported `SESSION_CONFIG` in `auth.config.ts`, consumed by both instances, so they cannot hold different values. **Owner set 48h** (option "match the docs", then raised): 24h re-prompts staff who use this daily, a week is long for an account that moves money given we still cannot force a sign-out except by bumping `User.tokenVersion`. Flagged and accepted: **48h does not carry a weekend** (~63h Friday evening → Monday morning), so Monday is a fresh login, which is what the owner expected all along; 72h is the number if that changes. **No mass sign-out on deploy**: existing cookies keep their 30-day `exp` until the next request re-issues them at 48h. **+5 tests** ([session-config.test.ts](__tests__/lib/session-config.test.ts)), the load-bearing ones being source assertions that nobody re-inlines a `maxAge` in either file or in `proxy.ts`; mutation-verified by deleting `session: SESSION_CONFIG` from the Edge config, which is the exact regression. The guard **reads sources with comments stripped** (the `check-tenant-als.sh` precedent) after its first version failed on a comment explaining the rule (a guard that cannot tell prose from code fails on its own documentation). **Docs corrected where they were confidently wrong**: HANDOVER §4 and SESSION_ARCHITECTURE §2 both asserted a 24h bound that had never held, and SESSION_ARCHITECTURE's Aug-11 note that *"an actively-used session never expired at all"* was understated: the bound was a month, not a day. The durable lesson: **when one concern is configured in two places, the config that says nothing does not defer to the other. It silently wins with a framework default.** Gate: tsc 0, eslint 0, vitest 5429, build clean.

- **Daily digest: the email and deploy warnings were reporting stale history (August 17, 2026)**. Owner question about digest cadence surfaced a mismatch between the snapshot and the email. The digest reads the `/admin/infra` snapshot, which deliberately holds **more** history than a daily email should report: **7 days** of failed emails (`EMAIL_FAILURE_WINDOW_DAYS`) and the **last 10 workflow runs with no time bound at all**. Both were reported as-is and [any finding makes the verdict amber](src/lib/daily-digest-worker.ts), so ONE event coloured the digest every morning until it aged out of the *snapshot*: seven mornings for an email, and **indefinitely** for a deploy during a quiet week. Each morning it read like a fresh overnight problem. There was a live instance: Friday's migration-safety CI failure, fixed by the very next push, had been making the digest amber for three days because no deploy had run to push it out of the last 10. Now **2 days** for email failures and **the last 3 runs** for deploys, both named in the finding labels so amber reads as *"there is an open item"* rather than *"something broke overnight"*. **Bounded in the digest, not in the fetch**. `/admin/infra` keeps the fuller history because the dashboard is the drill-down; narrowing the fetch would have cost 3am visibility to fix a problem that only existed in the email. **Deploys stay bounded by COUNT, not time**, because they are bursty (the last 10 runs spanned 28h one week and 3 days another), so "the last 3" tracks *did the most recent work land?* better than any fixed number of hours. A failed email whose timestamp will not parse is **counted, not dropped**: this code decides whether to raise an alarm, so an unreadable date must never be the thing that hides a real failure. +7 tests, both windows mutation-verified (restoring 7 days / 10 runs fails 4, including both "must not fire" cases).

- **Customizable RSVP: one event, several independent RSVPs (August 14, 2026)** — Generalizes Dinner RSVP so an event can run a gala dinner AND a set of parallel workshops AND a site visit, each with its **own options and its own guest list**. Owner ask: *"RSVP for anything — speakers, registration, submitters."* Plan + decision record: [docs/CUSTOMIZABLE_RSVP_PLAN.md](docs/CUSTOMIZABLE_RSVP_PLAN.md); live reference: [docs/RSVP.md](docs/RSVP.md). **The audience half was already built** — `RsvpInvite` carried `registrationId?`/`speakerId?` soft refs and the import picker already read Registrations + Speakers; submitters ARE `Speaker` rows (`submitterSource`, 27 on prod), so the Submitters tab is a filter over the speakers fetch, not a second endpoint. **The work was the "several RSVPs" half, and it is not a `kind` column**: `@@unique([eventId, inviteeEmail])` meant a person held exactly ONE invite per event, so a 30-person dinner list and a 200-person workshop list could not coexist — and reusing the invite would have shown the workshop audience the VIP dinner list. New **`RsvpCampaign`** between Event and items+invites; the key moves to **`@@unique([campaignId, inviteeEmail])`**. **The simpler model was considered and rejected**: scoping invites to an ITEM (no campaign) breaks the multi-night dinner that works today — one link asking "which nights?" becomes three links. General test recorded in the plan: *if removing a layer forces you to reinvent it without a name, it was not gratuitous.* **Per-campaign config is two booleans + a mode, deliberately not a `kind` enum** — `selectionMode` SINGLE/MULTI, `allowGuests`, `collectDietary`; a site visit collects dietary but no guests, a workshop takes neither, and `kind: DINNER|WORKSHOP` makes those unrepresentable (the Aug 13 supporting-document lesson). SINGLE is **enforced server-side** (400 `SINGLE_SELECTION_ONLY`), `allowGuests:false` **ignores** a submitted count rather than persisting it, and declining everything stays valid in BOTH modes (otherwise a pick-one RSVP forces a false pick). **The campaign costs the organizer no extra step** (plan §2a): "New RSVP" is ONE form creating the campaign *and* its first option (`firstItem` on the create payload), config sits behind an **Options** disclosure defaulting to today's dinner behavior, so a single-dinner event is still New RSVP → add invitees → send. *Model the general case, present the common one* — schema shape and UI shape need not match, and assuming they must is why the flat `@@unique` existed. **Renames are Prisma-side via `@@map`**: `RsvpItem`→`RsvpDinner`, `RsvpResponse`→`RsvpDinnerResponse`, `startsAt`→`dinnerAt`, `itemId`→`dinnerId`. A real `ALTER TABLE ... RENAME` is not blue/green safe (migrations run BEFORE the container swap), so the physical table is still called `RsvpDinner` while holding workshops — documented naming debt bought at zero risk. **Migration `20260814120000` is idempotent throughout; the only statement that can change behaviour is** `DROP INDEX RsvpInvite_eventId_inviteeEmail_key` — the thing that actually permits two audiences. It only *loosens*, and was verified collision-free first (prod: **1 item, 2 invites, 0 responses** — effectively unused); precedent `20260625140000_cert_per_template_uniqueness`. At scale the principled form is **expand/contract** (ship additive, deploy, drop next deploy) and the migration header says so. Replay from empty → `prisma migrate diff` **"No difference detected"**, which also confirmed the `@@map` index names line up. Applied to the local prod-copy: 1 campaign backfilled, **zero orphans**. **The email template slug stays `dinner-rsvp-invitation`** — verified read-only on prod that **17 events already hold a materialised row** on it (the templates list GET auto-seeds system defaults), so renaming would orphan all 17 and silently fall back to the default for anyone who edited theirs; `{{dinnerWord}}` likewise kept resolvable, though the DEFAULT template moved to `{{rsvpName}}` so a **workshop** RSVP on a new event stops emailing "you're invited to the dinners". *A slug is a KEY, not a label* (the Aug 11 presenter lesson). Routes moved **under the campaign** (`/rsvp-campaigns/[campaignId]/{items,invites}`) so scoping is structural rather than a where-clause someone can forget; pages `/dinner` → `/rsvp` (list) + `/rsvp/[campaignId]` (console) with `/dinner` a permanent redirect. Shared [src/lib/rsvp/server.ts](src/lib/rsvp/server.ts) `loadRsvpEvent`/`loadRsvpCampaign` because six routes need the same two-step scope and a hand-copied check is how one ends up org-scoped-only. MCP `list_dinner_rsvps` → **`list_rsvps`**, results **grouped by campaign** (summing a 30-person dinner and a 200-person workshop briefs the caterer wrongly); **MCP clients reconnect**, pkg 0.4.29→0.4.30. `RsvpCampaign` born tenancy-compliant (org stamped at create, `runWithTenant`, [prisma/rls/rsvp.sql](prisma/rls/rsvp.sql) policy, CI-gate entry, harness assertion) in the same change. **All the July-2026 review fixes are preserved and still pinned** (M1 deadline-less item closes at start, M2 `ignoredItemIds`, M3 409 `STALE_FORM`, M6 10-min batch resume, M8 message tokens, M10 audit-with-IP, H2 roster is `denyReviewer`-guarded because the token IS an impersonation credential). **+3 mutation-verified guards**: reverting the de-dup key to `eventId` fails the "same person, two RSVPs" test; removing the SINGLE guard fails its test; passing the guest count through fails its test. **Post-ship review, 3 lenses (security/tenancy · correctness/concurrency · drift/duplication): 0 BLOCKER, 3 HIGH, 6 MED — the 6 introduced by the commit were fixed in-band** (`H1` SINGLE mode was bypassable through the ordinary UI because the guard counted only OPEN items while the replace-all preserved a CLOSED item's attendance — pick A, let it close, pick B, and the DB holds both; now counts the RESULTING state. `H2` `{{itemWord}}` was documented in four places as an alias for `{{dinnerWord}}` above two lines rendering different words, and was in neither `TEMPLATE_VARIABLES` nor the preview samples — so following the docs gave a literal token in Preview, a resolved one in the send, and silently rewrote the copy: the July-2026 preview/send divergence class, reintroduced. `H3` `list_dinner_rsvps` still named in `MCP_REFERENCE.md` and the user-guide, the latter feeding the **help-chat system prompt** so the assistant recommended a dead tool. `M-A` `campaign.isActive` was displayed, badged, settable and enforced nowhere — *a flag that is displayed but not enforced is worse than no flag*. `M-C` `CLAUDE.md` + `DOMAIN_MAP` still asserted the inverted uniqueness. `M-D` flipping `allowGuests` off left guest counts summed in the headcount tile but absent from the CSV, so the caterer got a total nobody could explain — now reconciled in the same transaction, audited). **Four findings verified as carried over from July 2026, not regressions** (replace-all destroying un-addressed fresher answers, org stamped from the host-resolved lookup, the false "was not recorded" toast, missing rate limits) — recorded in ROADMAP. Gate: tsc 0, eslint 0, vitest **5411**, build clean. **Not built** (plan §9): capacity/waitlists (the one genuinely hard piece — a contended claim needs a conditional write and collides with the replace-all submit; additive later as nullable `RsvpItem.capacity`), a hub link spanning campaigns, auto-reminder cron, campaign cloning, decline reasons.

- **Supporting document is a per-registration-type switch, not a guess at the type's NAME (August 13, 2026)** — Replaces the `/resident|trainee/i` name match the Resident letter shipped with the day before. The owner asked "what about Member?" within 24 hours, which is the signal that the *mechanism* was wrong rather than incomplete: a second hardcoded regex would have made it three. **Configuration encoded in a name is configuration nobody can see, change or audit** — renaming "Resident" to "Junior Doctor" silently switched the requirement off, with no warning and no log line, and "ask Members but not Residents" was inexpressible. Four additive `TicketType` columns ([supporting-document.ts](src/lib/supporting-document.ts)); **two booleans, deliberately not one tri-state enum**, because collapsing them makes "ask but do not block" unrepresentable and that is the default, for the real reason that a delegate filling the form at 11pm without the document should still be able to register. The organizer picks **Required / Optional** as an explicit pair rather than a "refuse without it" checkbox (owner's framing: they are choosing a policy, not opting out of one), plus their own field label and instructions, which the public form renders in place of the hardcoded Resident copy. **Registration's two columns were NOT renamed in SQL**: deploys are blue/green and migrations run BEFORE the container swap, so `ALTER ... RENAME COLUMN` would leave the still-live old container querying a column that no longer exists — Prisma `@map` gives the honest field name at zero risk, verified with `prisma migrate diff` producing no DDL. The storage prefix `/uploads/resident-letters/` and the worker's `JOB_NAME` also stay: both are KEYS, not labels (the job name is matched by `EXPECTED_JOBS` for the daily digest's cadence check and carried in `JobRun` history, so renaming would orphan history and risk a false "job not running" alarm). The event-wide `settings.residentLetter` switch is retired, its value backfilled per type. **Migration `20260813120000` is additive + gated on the first column not existing, so the backfill runs exactly once** — a bare `WHERE requiresDocument = false` would be re-runnable but would also re-enable a type an organizer had deliberately switched off, which is worse than not being idempotent. **Verified against prod read-only before shipping: 20 types keep asking (exact parity with today's name match) and the single event carrying the old switch has it `false`, so nothing starts blocking** — behaviourally a no-op. +12 tests, two mutation-verified (collapsing the booleans fails 3; failing open on `requiresDocument` fails 2); the load-bearing ones assert what the old mechanism got wrong — a rename must not change behaviour, and a suggestive name must not start asking. Gate: tsc 0, eslint 0, vitest 5350, build clean.

- **Financial-document presentation: day-first dates, and the receipt masthead that was a duplicate (August 12, 2026, organizer-reported; commit `1b71a1cd`)** Two small defects on the invoice/receipt family, both of the "renders fine, means the wrong thing" class. **(1) Dates were month-first.** `formatDateShort` in [document-layout.ts](src/lib/pdf/document-layout.ts) built `${month}/${day}/${year}`, so 9 April printed as `4/9/2026` — which a UAE or European finance team files as **4 September**. On an invoice that ambiguity lands on exactly the two fields where it costs money: the **issue date**, which starts the payment clock, and the **due date**. Now zero-padded day-first (`09/04/2026`), and the padding is part of the fix rather than decoration: unpadded `4/9` gives a reader nothing to infer the convention from, whereas fixed-width at least signals one is in force. One helper backs the invoice, quote, credit note and CRM quote, so two documents describing one transaction cannot disagree about it; the receipt's *Payment Date* deliberately stays on `formatDate` (`Apr 9, 2026`), which is unambiguous by construction and needs no convention. **(2) The receipt had no logo, and repeated the company name.** `logoPath` was simply never passed to `generateReceiptPDF` — the invoice and credit note both had it — while the top-left carried the company name at 20pt, which is a **duplicate of the FROM block directly beneath it**. So the logo replaces that copy without displacing information: logo (100pt wide) on top, "PAYMENT RECEIPT" under it, the name still in FROM. The 100 is a width; the height beside it is a **ceiling**, since pdfkit's `fit` preserves aspect ratio — a tall or square logo shrinks to stay in the box instead of growing down into the line below. Two fallbacks keep the text masthead: no logo configured, and a logo whose bytes will not decode. **The second matters more than it looks**: a receipt is proof of a payment that already happened, so failing the render over a corrupt image would withhold the artifact over the one element on it carrying no financial information; the failure logs `receipt-pdf:logo-image-decode-failed` so it stays answerable rather than silent. **The testing lesson, and it is a trap worth knowing before touching any PDF renderer:** asserting on the text of the finished document does not work. pdfkit Flate-compresses its content streams **and** subsets the font, so the words on the page are glyph indices — a `pdf.includes("PAYMENT RECEIPT")` check returns false for text that is plainly there, i.e. an assertion that can only fail, or worse, pass in the negative direction. [receipt-pdf-masthead.test.ts](__tests__/lib/receipt-pdf-masthead.test.ts) spies on `PDFDocument.prototype` `image`/`text` with **call-through** instead, so pdfkit still genuinely renders and the branch is still observable. +8 tests (4 date-format, 4 receipt-masthead; 21 total in the two touched files), both halves mutation-verified (month-first fails 4; removing the logo branch fails 2). **Doc drift corrected in passing:** PAYMENT_FLOW.md §11 claimed "the system now only emits `INVOICE`" and that `createReceipt` was a backward-compat alias — false for the single-registration path, where `issuePaidRegistrationDocuments` mints **both** an invoice and a receipt and emails one message carrying both PDFs. It is true only of the **group** path, which deliberately promotes the consolidated invoice rather than minting a second numbered document. Docs: PAYMENT_FLOW.md §11.1 (presentation rules + the testing note) and user-guide §8 "How the documents look".

- **⚠️ The Resident-letter half of this entry was SUPERSEDED Aug 13, 2026** (per-type switch — see the entry above). The name-pattern trigger and the event-wide Settings switch it describes are both retired; everything else in the entry stands. **Organizer round: the Resident official letter, a bill-to that addresses people properly, and a date token that had a clock in it (August 12, 2026; commits `911d1238` / `d210bfc8` / `7dcbcc6e` / `0a3a2fd3` / `ed0864bd`)** Four organizer reports in one arc. Three of them turned out to be two bugs stacked on each other, which is the theme worth keeping. **(1) The Resident official letter was a notice with nothing to click.** The copy shipped July 6 (`c5e205b1`) as an amber box telling residents to upload a letter from their institution, keyed on the ROLE dropdown, with no file input. The trigger moved to the **ticket type**: the letter substantiates entitlement to a discounted RATE, and the rate is the ticket type, so a resident paying the full Physician rate is claiming no discount and has nothing to prove; it also catches the variants that actually exist on prod (`Student/Resident`, `Trainee / Student`, 17 events carry a Resident type). **Whether a missing letter BLOCKS is a per-event organizer switch** (Settings → Registration), defaulting OFF so no live event changes behaviour: some events want the paperwork before holding a discounted place, others would rather take the registration and chase it than lose the delegate at the form. Note the deliberate asymmetry with the member/student evidence fields beside it, which are unconditionally required: those ask for a number someone knows by heart, this asks for a document they may not have to hand at 11pm. **The upload is the first genuinely UNAUTHENTICATED one in the system**: every other public upload is token-gated (reimbursement, speaker form) and the rest sit behind `auth()`, but a registration form has neither, so the bounds come from elsewhere: PDF/JPG/PNG by **magic bytes** (the declared Content-Type is attacker-supplied), 5MB, 10/hr/IP, and the event must exist and be public, with the event resolved BEFORE the body is read so a bad slug costs a lookup rather than 5MB of ingest. The stored path is validated **on the way in and again on the way out**: it arrives from a public form field and the staff download route later resolves it against the filesystem, so a stored `../../` would be an arbitrary-read primitive: validating once would do today, validating at both ends means the read side never has to trust the column. Letters are private (a named person, their employer, a signature and stamp), so `/uploads/resident-letters/` is blocked on the public catch-all and streams only through the authed route. That block is pinned as a **route-level test** rather than by curling a dev server, because `next dev` serves `public/` before the catch-all runs, which makes EVERY private prefix (reimbursements, speaker-docs, crm-deal-docs) readable on a developer machine; verified by checking an existing block leaks identically, so the new one is exactly as effective as the ones already relied on in prod. Nightly `resident-letter-prune` (JOB_ID 1016) collects uploads no registration ever claimed, which exist because the file necessarily precedes its owner (the form uploads, then submits): nothing else in the system has that shape. Two guards, both mutation-verified: **referenced ⇒ never deleted at any age**, and **unreferenced but younger than 24h ⇒ never deleted either**, that window being the registrant still filling in the form. **(2) The bill-to was wrong twice in one line.** It printed `Osman, DR Ahmed`: surname-first is a directory sort order rather than a form of address, AND `title` is the raw Prisma enum, so every doctor's quote said "DR". The fix could not be `formatPersonName`, because **the callers disagree on the title's shape**: the quote builder passes the enum, the invoice builder passes the already-formatted label: so mapping only the enum would have SILENTLY dropped the honorific from every invoice. New tolerant `formatRecipientName` in [document-layout.ts](src/lib/pdf/document-layout.ts) accepts both; normalising in one function beats sweeping the call sites because **a missed call site in that sweep fails silently**. Organization also joined the bill-to on its own line: `jobTitle || organization` printed whichever came first and dropped the other. **(3) "Dubai Studio City" ran on** because the whole address is one field (`508 & 509, DSC tower, Dubai Studio City,`, trailing comma included). The Settings field is already a textarea so the break was always typeable, but the header advances a fixed 11pt per entry and a newline passed through as one string draws over the line below: `toAddressLines` splits and strips a dangling separator, shared by quote, invoice, receipt and CRM quote, which each built that array inline. **The receipt also gained the payer's tax number**: quote and invoice always printed it, the receipt did not, so the one document a finance team files against a payment was the one missing the number they file it under; sourced payer-first and labelled with the payer's name when a third-party account pays, so the TRN is never misattributed to the attendee named above it. **(4) `{{eventDate}}` printed a clock, and the clock was hiding a worse bug.** A confirmation read *"held from Friday, October 2, 2026 at 04:00 AM"*. `sendRegistrationConfirmation` was the last sender formatting the date by hand and appended hour+minute: an event-level clock is meaningless on a multi-day conference (the real per-day times live on the agenda), which is why the same line was pulled from the public event pages in July. But it also passed **no `timeZone`**, so it rendered in the SERVER's zone (UTC in prod): the organizer's 08:00 Dubai start is stored `04:00Z`, hence "04:00 AM": and the same omission **silently moves the DATE**, since an event starting 02:00 Dubai on the 3rd is 22:00Z on the 2nd and the email would name the wrong day. Now anchored to the event's own timezone, the rule the agenda and deadline fields already follow. **`{{eventDateRange}}` is now provided by the send** ("October 2 – 3, 2026", collapsing on a one-day event), plus an explicit `{{eventStartDate}}` alias; it previously resolved in the template **preview and nowhere else**, so an organizer using it saw it work on screen and shipped copy that printed the raw token to every registrant. The preview additionally rendered `{{eventDate}}` as a RANGE while the send rendered the start, so previewing "October 2 – 3" produced emails saying "October 2". `{{eventDate}}` keeps its meaning deliberately (24 events hold materialised templates using it). The date logic became an exported pure `buildEventDateTokens` **because neither new value is observable through the default template**, which references only `{{eventDate}}`: a contract that cannot be asserted is a contract that drifts, which is precisely how the divergence arose. **The testing lesson of the round, learned from a mutation run:** an assertion that the email does not contain `"04:00"` **passes on a laptop set to Asia/Dubai**, because the same instant renders there as 08:00: it only catches the bug on a UTC machine. The load-bearing guards are a clock-SHAPE regex and a `Europe/London` fixture, which discriminate in any runtime zone; both are commented in the file so the weaker ones are not mistaken for guards. **A timezone test that names a specific clock string is testing your laptop, not your code.** +58 tests (suite 5248 → 5325); every guard that matters mutation-verified. Verified by rendering real quote and receipt PDFs and by driving the registration form in a browser against the local prod copy. **Owner action:** put the line break in Settings → Billing → Address; the renderer now honours it. Migration `20260812120000` (two nullable columns on Registration) is additive + idempotent + blue-green safe.

- **"Can an external AI agent talk to our system?" The MCP front door audited, and the two things the audit found (August 12, 2026; full record in [docs/MCP_SECURITY.md](docs/MCP_SECURITY.md))** Owner question ahead of the platform instance. The answer is yes and deliberately: `/api/mcp` exists so Claude, n8n and any spec-compliant client can drive EA-SYS. **Verified live against prod, read-only**: unauthenticated POST returns 401 with the RFC 6750 `WWW-Authenticate` challenge, a forged `mmg_` key returns 401, and `/api/events` + `/api/contacts` + a nested registrations route all return 401. The OAuth core held up on inspection: **PKCE S256 only** with a timing-safe compare, auth codes deleted in the same transaction that mints the token so a code cannot be replayed, tokens stored hashed and never logged raw, the grantee's role **re-resolved on every request** so a demotion bites immediately, an org-mismatch refusal, and `redirect_uri` re-validated at both the consent page and the decision endpoint. **The finding that mattered is not in any of that, it is in the one screen a human reads.** `/api/mcp/oauth/register` is unauthenticated because RFC 7591 Dynamic Client Registration is (a browser client cannot hold a pre-issued credential), which is fine on its own since a `client_id` grants nothing. But every path to data then reduces to one admin approving `/mcp-authorize`, and that screen rendered **`client_name`, free text typed by whoever registered**, while never rendering **`redirect_uri`, where the code is actually delivered**. So a client registered as "EA-SYS Official Sync" pointing at an attacker's callback was visually indistinguishable from the real Claude integration, and approving it hands over the org's whole tool set for 30 days. This is the canonical OAuth consent-phishing shape (the 2017 "Google Docs" worm was an app literally named Google Docs asking for Gmail scope), and **the durable rule is to display the field the requester cannot forge, not the one they typed**. Fixed with a new [mcp-client-trust.ts](src/lib/mcp-client-trust.ts) `describeRedirectTarget()`: the destination is now the loudest block on the page, the client name is demoted to a claim ("a client calling itself …"), an unrecognised host renders red and names the consequence, and **the safe action becomes the primary button** (Deny filled, Approve a red outline reading "Approve anyway, I recognise evil.example") because a screen that makes Approve inviting regardless of who is asking is doing the attacker's layout work. Unrecognised is **advisory, never a block**: a self-hosted n8n or a customer's own agent is legitimate and the admin is the one who knows, so it changes what the screen says, not what it allows; an approval to an unrecognised host logs at **warn** with the host so a phished grant is answerable afterwards. The trust list is deliberately **its own list, not the CORS one** in `mcp-cors.ts`: they hold the same hosts today and answer different questions ("may this origin call our API" vs "should a human be reassured"), and sharing them would let a future CORS addition silently mark a destination trusted, the same reasoning as the six deliberately-disagreeing visibility predicates. **Second finding: the CSRF protection on the grant endpoint was inherited, not written.** `/api/mcp/oauth/authorize/decision` is a cookie-authenticated POST that mints a credential, and [src/proxy.ts](src/proxy.ts) **explicitly skips its Origin/Host check for the whole `/api/mcp` prefix** so browser MCP clients are not blocked by the mobile-only CORS allow-list, which is correct for the transport endpoint (Bearer auth, not CSRF-able), wrong for this one. It was safe only because Auth.js defaults the session cookie to `SameSite=Lax`, which browsers do not attach to a cross-site POST: a real protection, but one `sameSite: "none"` away from vanishing with nothing in the repo failing. **A guarantee you did not write is a guarantee you cannot test**, so it is now written: `isSameOriginRequest()` in [security.ts](src/lib/security.ts) checks Origin against Host, falls back to Referer, treats an opaque `Origin: null` as a refusal rather than falling through to a Referer the same attacker controls, and refuses when neither header is present; the route runs it **before the session is read**, so a forged request cannot depend on who happens to be logged in. +25 tests, two **mutation-verified** (disabling the guard fails 2; a bare `endsWith` in place of the dot-anchored suffix fails the look-alike case, which pins that `notclaude.ai` and `claude.ai.evil.com` must NOT read as trusted). **Also fixed while here:** the two long-standing lint warnings were **not dead imports but a missing assertion**: `registration-rls.test.ts` and `abstract-rls.test.ts` imported the A-side fixture ids and then asserted only counts, and a count of 1 per lane also passes if the two lanes are SWAPPED, which is exactly the mis-routing an RLS suite exists to catch; both are now identity assertions (same "counts cannot reveal a wrong pick" lesson as the Aug 11 date-format echo). **Owner actions outstanding, none code-fixable** (§6 of the doc): 4 active API keys with **no expiry on any of them**, one of which is **INTERNAL tier (rate-limit exempt) and has never been used**, a `n8ntest` key idle since 2026-07-09, and 7 `McpOAuthClient` rows accumulating because the cleanup worker prunes codes and tokens but never clients. Gate: tsc 0, eslint **0 warnings and 0 errors**, vitest **5248**, build clean.

- **Presenter registration: abstract submitters pay like delegates, and the three defects only RUNNING it exposed (August 11, 2026; commits `f6e0d7d4` / `96b136c0` / `96f3a1c2` / `2cb325ae` / `4c950a2a`; plan + decisions in [docs/PRESENTER_REGISTRATION_PLAN.md](docs/PRESENTER_REGISTRATION_PLAN.md))** Organizers asked for abstract presenters to register on their own rate ladder instead of receiving an automatic free Faculty comp. Evidence first: a tier literally named `Presenter` had been auto-seeded **69 times across prod with zero registrations, ever**, because the abstract door minted a free comp and bypassed it, and on the live conference it was priced identically to Early Bird. So one dead tier became a **family** (`Presenter Early Bird` / `Presenter Standard`), matched by a single name-prefix predicate in [presenter-tiers.ts](src/lib/presenter-tiers.ts) because three places need to answer "is this a presenter tier?" (the delegate redirect that must skip them, the signup form that lists their rates, the door that picks the one on sale) and three string comparisons would drift. **Decisions:** rates are tiers **per profession**, not a separate registration type (deriving from the `role` enum was rejected: events carry `Nurse`/`Member`, which the enum cannot express, and the enum carries `Pharma`/`Academia`, which have no rate); the submitter **picks their type at signup**; **quote at submission with Pay Now OFF by default** plus a per-event organizer toggle behind a confirmation dialog, because ~1 in 20-30 presenters actually pay and the rest are settled after acceptance; and **an event with no presenter tiers keeps today's free comp**, which is what makes this safe to deploy since every existing event is in that state. Price is resolved **server-side** from a type id, so a form left open overnight cannot buy a rate that closed, and form and door share one resolver so the price shown is the price charged. **The three defects, all found by running the flow rather than reading it, each being correct code that nothing reached or two correct halves disagreeing:** **(1)** the presenter registration **claimed the ticket type's seat while the cancel path would release the presenter tier's**. The door never stamped `createdSource` (so the service derived `ADMIN_DASHBOARD` from `source: "api"`) *and* the service hardcoded a `ticketType` increment while release picks its counter with `seatCounter()`; a guarded release floors at 0, so the tier no-oped and the ticket type leaked upward forever, exactly the drift class the June 29 fix existed to kill. Both sides now derive from `seatCounter()` so they **cannot** disagree again; owner ruling, consistent with the Aug 6 group-registration decision, is that a public door **sells the tier** so a presenter tier's seat limit is real and caps, while a staff grant still claims the ticket type because a courtesy seat must not burn a paid one; pinned in both directions and mutation-verified. **(2)** a presenter received **two emails seconds apart**: the submitter welcome and then the delegate "Your registration for X" carrying the quote, which claims a settled place at an event where nothing has been accepted; owner ruling: **one email**, the fee and quote fold into the welcome via a new `suppressConfirmationEmail` service flag documented as usable ONLY where the caller sends a replacement (the `/abstract-start` sign-in door has no welcome, so it keeps the confirmation, otherwise the quote would silently never arrive). **The trap inside that fix is the reusable lesson: adding the token to the DEFAULT template reached nobody, because 24 events had already materialised their own saved `submitter-welcome` row**, so the quote would have arrived attached with nothing in the body explaining it, so the token is appended when the resolved template lacks it. The block's closing sentence and its Pay Now button are decided from **one** flag, so "payment is not required" can never print above a Pay Now button. **(3)** the welcome CTA pointed at `${appUrl}/login`, the **internal staff sign-in**, so a submitter landed in a different product with no route back; the identical defect was fixed Aug 6 for the session-proposal email and this door was missed. **Also this round:** the per-event **co-author limit was not reaching the submission form** (the form read a settings blob the org-null submitter payload deliberately strips, so it silently fell back to the default of 20 while the server enforced 5, a whitelist correct by default and wrong for one key, which is a class a test of the whitelist cannot catch, so the pin is consumer-side), and `scripts/dev-create-admin.ts` exists because the local DB is a restored copy of production where every account carries a real bcrypt hash, so there was no way to sign in at all; it is guarded harder than the feature it enables (parses the URL rather than substring-matching it, so `?host=localhost` on a remote host is refused) and deliberately has no override flag. Verified end to end against the local prod copy: rate picker renders, the registration lands on the presenter tier, the **tier's** seat is the one burned, one email arrives with the fee block and quote attached, and the CTA opens the branded event login where the submitter lands on My Details with only Bio outstanding. Gate per commit: tsc 0, eslint 0, vitest → **5200**, build clean. **Not built** (plan §8): presenter-specific invoicing, automatic action on rejection (an unpaid registration already models it), and a presenter rate on the session-proposal door, which still creates nothing by design.

- **Abstract submission limits, the datetime-local drift that had corrupted six live events, and a Settings tidy-up (August 11, 2026; commits `1d4e0954` / `901cb62a` / `6939ccf8` / `10baf6ce`)** Four organizer requests in one arc, one of which turned out to be live data corruption. **(1) The deadline drift, and the class behind it.** Organizers reported the abstract and session-proposal deadlines "changing by hours" on save. The two fields loaded with `.toISOString().slice(0, 16)` and saved with `new Date(value).toISOString()`. A `datetime-local` input carries **no timezone**, so the browser was handed the UTC wall-clock and then read that same string back as LOCAL: every save stored `instant - offset` and it **compounded**. Typing a fresh value was correct, which is exactly why it went unnoticed for months; only opening Settings and pressing Save moved it. Prod carried a clean 4-hour ladder across ten deadlines, all typed as `:59` (`19:59Z` correct, then `15:59Z`, `11:59Z`, `07:59Z`), and **Annual Benign Hematology League Summit was closing abstract submissions at 11:59 Dubai on the final day instead of midnight**. This is the **third** instance of the identical defect: the dinner console had it (Survey/RSVP review B2) and the fix from that round, [src/lib/datetime-local.ts](src/lib/datetime-local.ts), documents the exact failure in its header, but these fields were never migrated onto it, and **promo code validity windows** turned out to have it too (every edit-and-save shifted a code's window back 4 hours, so codes stop working before the organizer expects). Deadlines moved onto the **event's timezone** (`localDateTimeInTz` / new `wallTimeInTzToIso`), matching the agenda and dinner console, so a deadline means the same instant whoever edits it; both fields now name the timezone, and the proposal input's `min` was computed browser-local while its value was UTC, so those two disagreed and could reject a genuinely-future date. Promo windows moved onto the browser-local pair, which is their recorded semantics. **(2) The gate, because three is not a coincidence.** New [scripts/check-datetime-local.sh](scripts/check-datetime-local.sh) (CI, gating): a file rendering a `datetime-local` input may not also slice a date string, narrowly scoped so a rate-limit key built from `token.slice(0, 16)` never trips it. Mutation-verified both directions. **A unit suite structurally cannot catch this class**, each helper is correct in isolation and the bug is in which one a form calls, which is the same reachability lesson as the Aug 10 round; when a defect recurs across files the fix belongs where the pattern is visible, not in a fourth code review. **(3) A latent bug the new tests found on their own:** `wallTimeInTzToDate` accepted right-shaped impossible dates because `Date.UTC` rolls over silently, so `2026-02-31` became March 3 and `2026-13-01` became January 2027.
