Unreachable from a date picker but **fully reachable from the agenda CSV import**, where a spreadsheet typo would have landed a session on the wrong day and reported a clean import; the components are now read back and compared, the same rule the Freshsales importer already adopted. **(4) Repair, deliberately not automatic.** [scripts/repair-drifted-deadlines.ts](scripts/repair-drifted-deadlines.ts) reports the drift per event with a before/after diff in the event's own timezone and writes nothing without `--write`. Nothing records how many times a value was saved, so the cycle count is **inferred** by undoing until the value reads 23:59 event-local; values that never were 23:59 are reported with their candidate ladder and left for an explicit `--set` after asking the organizer. **The first draft applied the drift instead of undoing it** and would have moved every deadline a day earlier; the dry run caught it, which is the argument for reading the diff rather than trusting the count. **(5) Per-event abstract limits** (`901cb62a`), four numbers that were constants compiled into the app: title words (**new, default 30**), body words (300), co-authors (20), and **abstracts per person** (new, default unlimited). They live together in `Event.settings.abstractLimits` for the same reason `groupRegistration` does, one policy, read as a set at every enforcement point, with no migration; [readAbstractLimits](src/lib/abstract-limits.ts) is fail-safe **per field** so one bad key cannot take the other three down, and ceilings mean a typo of 30 → 3000 cannot hand the review committee a 3000-word title. Two owner rules: **format limits (title/body/co-authors) apply to drafts too**, because a draft with a 60-word title is still a 60-word title, deliberately unlike the theme and presentation-type gates, which are *completeness* checks and exempt drafts; and the **per-person cap governs the review POOL, not the archive**, drafts are free, withdrawing or being rejected returns the slot, it bites only at Submit, only for a SUBMITTER (staff adding one on someone's behalf are exempt, matching the deadline and profile gates), and the abstract being submitted is excluded from its own count. The counting statuses are an **allow-list** so a future status is excluded by default rather than silently counted. **Lowering a cap never invalidates existing work**: `exceedsAbstractLimit` takes the current value and refuses only growth, so an abstract already over a new cap stays editable and can be trimmed, the same rule the presentation-type offering uses. The body cap was **not** asked for and was folded in anyway, because leaving 300 hardcoded next to three configurable neighbours is the inconsistency an organizer hits the following week. The Zod schemas keep only absolute shape guards (title 500 chars, co-author array 50) since a static module-level schema cannot see event settings, **static validation guards the shape, the handler guards the policy**. +37 tests across a reader suite and a route suite that asserts the *query shape* of the per-person count; the per-person gate and the grandfathering rule are both mutation-verified, and the route suite caught a real off-by-one in my own work (without `id: { not: abstractId }` a cap of 1 would refuse the first resubmission). **(6) Sign-in link on both submitter doors** (`6939ccf8`): the abstract and proposal register pages already flipped to sign-in when the typed email turned out to have an account, but only if you happened to type it, someone who knows they registered for a previous event looks for a Sign in link, does not find one, and creates a second account on a different address. They now carry the same "Already have an account? Sign in" line the delegate register page has always had, reading the variant copy config's existing `loginRedirect` rather than introducing a second source; one change covers both doors since they are thin wrappers over one component. **(7) Settings tidy-up** (`10baf6ce`, organizer request, pure layout): Registration had become a junk drawer of five unrelated concerns while abstract configuration was spread across three surfaces, so no single screen answered "how is abstract submission set up for this event?". Tab bar 10 → 8: **General** gains Notifications, **Registration** keeps registration settings + tax + agenda, and a new **Abstracts** tab (existing `!isWebinar` gate) holds Submissions + Session Proposals + Themes + Review Criteria. Notifications keeps its own Save inside General rather than merging into the one above it, because those switches write the settings JSON while the fields above write event columns through a different handler, folding them would drag the `maxAttendees` recompute and the session-date range guard into an unrelated save. Suite 5057 → 5144. **Owner decision (same day): the drifted prod values are LEFT AS-IS, the repair script was not run.** Reasonable because the fix makes the drift self-evident: the field now renders real event-local time with the timezone named, so an organizer opening Settings sees `11:59` where they meant midnight and corrects it in place, and saving no longer moves it. The one dated consequence to watch is **Annual Benign Hematology League Summit closing abstract submissions at 11:59 Dubai on Sept 29** instead of 23:59. `scripts/repair-drifted-deadlines.ts` stays in the repo (writes nothing without `--write`) if that changes. **Also note (`901cb62a` CI):** its first deploy failed on a transient `next/font/google` Fraunces fetch inside the Docker build, unrelated to the change; the following push carried it through.

- **Multi-tenancy item 5: the privileged maintenance lane, and the decision it corrected (August 11, 2026; commits `2b74dee4` / `f763016c` / `fdf54c3c`)** The first of the two decisions blocking the platform instance. Owner rulings: operator = **SUPER_ADMIN** (no new role); **per-job allowlisted** worker access, **synthetic platform org** for ownerless rows (not MMG's id, because the org a row carries IS the lane that can read it, so MMG-stamping would surface system rows inside MMG's ordinary tenant lane); and **wire every surface now** rather than during platform bringup. **(1) The lane.** `dbOperator` ([src/lib/db.ts](src/lib/db.ts)) connects as the table-OWNER role on `DATABASE_URL_OPERATOR`. It needs no `BYPASSRLS` grant: the policies in `prisma/rls/*.sql` are created **without FORCE**, so the owner role is exempt already, which is the same two-role split the tenancy harness has run as the reference architecture since Phase 0. **On master it is the SAME OBJECT as `db`** (the operator URL is unset), so one client, one pool, byte-identical behaviour, pinned by test, because a second client on the same URL would quietly double the box's connection footprint and this codebase has already had a P2024 incident. It carries `audit-org-stamp` (a job writing an audit row must still stamp its org) but deliberately **NOT `tenant-set-local`**: that extension issues SET LOCAL, which would re-impose the lane the client exists to step outside of, and the failure would be silent: zero rows is not an error, so `email-log-prune` would simply stop reaping while every dashboard stayed green. Same shape as the advisory-lock bug, so it is a test rather than a comment. **(2) Two walls.** `denyNonOperator` ([src/lib/platform-operator.ts](src/lib/platform-operator.ts)) is a **new, seventh** visibility predicate, narrower than all six recorded ones, and it **refuses org API keys**. Everywhere else a key is admin-equivalent, but a key belongs to ONE tenant and that equivalence has to stop at the tenant edge. The DB lane and the RBAC check are independent; neither substitutes for the other. **(3) The gate.** The whole reason the lane is a separate export rather than a flag on `db` is that privileged access must be a **greppable import** a CI gate can pin: [check-tenant-als.sh](scripts/check-tenant-als.sh) fails on any unlisted file importing `dbOperator`, and its failure message tells you to ask whether you actually need cross-tenant data or just the RIGHT tenant's lane. Mutation-verified both directions. **(4) Eleven surfaces wired, and the shape matters more than the count:** in 8 of the 9 jobs **the privileged part is ONE statement**. The candidate scan finds work across tenants, reads the org off the row, then does the actual work inside `runWithTenant(thatOrg)` on the normal client, so every send and money-adjacent write stays under RLS. *Borrow the tenant's lane; do not stay privileged.* Two deliberate exceptions: `email-log-prune` is privileged end to end (it reaps by row AGE across every tenant plus the NULL-org pool, which has no owning org whose lane could be borrowed, and it is that pool's only reaper), and `crm-inbound-email` resolves a reply token to a thread on the lane because **which tenant an inbound reply belongs to is precisely what that lookup answers**, so it cannot be scoped by its own answer. **Deliberately NOT wired**, and the reason is recorded in the allowlist: `system-log-prune`, `log-archive`, `oauth-cleanup` and `login-event-prune` scan SystemLog / McpOAuth* / LoginEvent, none of which carry an RLS policy, so they need no exemption; when LoginEvent is swept, its prune job joins the list. **(5) `/admin/infra` became scope-aware** (owner decision) rather than operator-only: the platform operator gets totals across every tenant, a tenant's own ADMIN gets their org. The scope picks the client AND the `organizationId` filter together, so the org view is already correct on master rather than only after RLS, and the 60s cache is **keyed on the scope**, because a shared entry would serve one audience's totals to the other, which is the exact leak the scope exists to prevent. Its test asserts the ARGUMENT rather than the response body, because the body is identical either way and on master both scopes return the same numbers: that is what would make this class of mistake invisible to review and to manual testing. **(6) The §4 correction, the most useful part of the round.** The recorded decision was that the `runWithTenant(orgId ?? "")` sites should fall back to the default (operator) org id. Measuring first showed there were **45, not 16**, and that **33 are lane wraps on routes reading a TENANT's event data** (check-in, refund, credit notes, badges, invoices, clone). For those, the operator org's lane cannot read tenant ACME's registration either, so the decision swaps one dead lane for another *while looking like a fix*. The real question was never which org to stamp but **whether a platform operator with no org should act inside a tenant's event at all**; owner: no, and if they must, they get a membership there. That is also the only option adding **no** privileged surface. New `runWithTenantLane(orgId, { route, userId }, fn)` ([src/lib/tenant-lane.ts](src/lib/tenant-lane.ts)) still fails closed but logs `tenant:no-org-lane` first, so a platform 404 is traceable instead of mysterious; `route` is **required** here (unlike `denyReviewer`'s optional one) because this wrap only exists where an org-null caller is genuinely possible, so a line naming who but not what would be useless every time it fired: the Aug 10 lesson applied rather than repeated. Master behaviour unchanged (RLS off ⇒ passthrough for any value including `""`), asserted rather than assumed since otherwise this would have silently broken 33 live routes. The 15 public `tenant.orgId ?? ""` sites (host resolution, already logged by the resolver's own ramp) and the 12 `organizationId: (… ?? "")` **service arguments and Prisma predicates** (not lanes at all) are deliberately untouched. **Ten test files** needed their `@/lib/db` mock widened: they stub a single export, so `dbOperator` arrived `undefined`; they now bind both names to the same fake, which is what production does on master anyway. The CI gate also needed teaching that `runWithTenantLane(` does **not** contain the substring `runWithTenant(`. +43 tests (suite 5044 → 5095); tsc/eslint/build green per commit. **Remaining platform ops step:** provision the non-owner `app_user` role and point the two connection strings at different roles. Until then they are the same and the lane is inert. **Item 6 (identity model) is now the only open decision in [docs/PLATFORM_DECISIONS.md](docs/PLATFORM_DECISIONS.md).**

- **Warning triage → four organizer bugs, and two guarantees that were implemented but never invoked (August 10, 2026; commits `34c9c39a` / `07cf5062` / `1210ca9b` / `d4d8788c` / `007b5a48`)**. Started as *"review all the errors and warnings especially from the webinar in the last 1 hour"*. Of 51 warn lines, 9 distinct messages, most were expected (staff testing a join window, a deleted test event, a typo'd login) but three were real, and the day's theme is that **two of them were correct, fully tested code that nothing ever called**. **(1) The session optimistic lock was never engaged.** The server half of W2-F8 is complete: pass `expectedUpdatedAt` and [session-service](src/services/session-service.ts) turns the update into a conditional claim returning 409 `STALE_WRITE`, with a test pinning that a lost claim mutates nothing. The agenda dialog never sent the token, so every save was last-write-wins and the whole tested path was unreachable from the main editing surface; prod logged 4 `optimistic-lock:missing-expectedUpdatedAt` on a webinar anchor in one hour, where a lost update moves Zoom **and** reschedules the entire reminder sequence. The tell was already in the file: the error handler had a `STALE_WRITE` branch that could never fire. **A unit suite cannot catch this class: it verifies the unit works, not that anything calls it** (same shape as the `?? ""` pass and the `orgCtx` ternary). The [session detail sheet](src/components/sessions/session-detail-sheet.tsx) already did it correctly, so the fix makes agenda match the existing pattern rather than invent one, differing on recovery for a real reason: the sheet edits topics only and can discard on conflict, while the dialog holds times, roles and topics, so a conflict **keeps the operator's form** and offers an explicit "Reload session" action. Adopting the fresh token automatically was rejected, since that turns the lock back into last-write-wins with one extra click. The row-to-form mapping was extracted so open-dialog and reload-after-conflict cannot drift into two hand-written copies. **(2) Publishing a webinar silently removed the producer's ability to rehearse it.** [zoom-join](src/app/api/public/events/%5Bslug%5D/sessions/%5BsessionId%5D/zoom-join/route.ts) admits a caller when the session is LIVE, starts within 15 min, or the event is DRAFT, and it *computed* `isOrgStaff`, with a comment saying it existed **"for QA / host testing"**, then used it only to skip the registration requirement while the clock below blocked exactly the testing it named. So the only way to preview your own attendee view was to keep the event in DRAFT. Five refusals in one morning from the organizer's own account, one against a session starting the **next day**. Staff now bypass the window, logged `zoom:join-staff-preview-outside-window` so an out-of-window join stays traceable; the bypass is narrow (`isOrgStaff` needs a staff role **and** a matching org, so a foreign organizer still falls through to the registration path and then the clock). +5 tests pinning both directions, **mutation-verified, and the first draft of the log assertion PASSED with the bypass removed** (the log line sits in its own condition), so it now asserts the status too: the second time in this repo a test would have passed against the exact bug it existed to catch. **(3) Starting a webinar is two steps and only one was visible.** `Start as Host` begins the broadcast and admits **nobody**; attendees leave the waiting room only on "Open the room / Go live". Start-as-Host sat in the always-visible sticky bar while the room toggle was two cards down in Lobby (**the control that does not let anyone in was permanent, the one that does required a scroll**), and the pre-existing "room still closed" warning shows this was mitigated after the fact rather than designed out. Room state now renders beside Start as Host, and starting while closed asks whether to open it too; "Start only" stays, because rehearsing with panelists before letting the audience in is a real workflow and is what the producer got by default until now. The Zoom tab opens **synchronously in the click handler before any `await`** (a popup blocker kills a `window.open()` after one), and a failed room-open toasts "Started, but opening the room failed" rather than implying the start failed. **(4) Three organizer-reported UI bugs, one of which was two bugs.** Mobile: long country/specialty values overflowed their field. The select trigger already carried `truncate`, but **the trigger is a flex row and a flex item defaults to `min-width: auto`**, refusing to shrink below intrinsic content width, so `overflow: hidden` never fired; `min-w-0` on [searchable-select](src/components/ui/searchable-select.tsx) fixes every consumer at once (**inside a flex container, `truncate` alone is decoration**). Separately, **23 rows across the three public registration forms used a bare `grid-cols-2` with no breakpoint**, giving each field ~160px on a 360px phone, now `grid-cols-1 sm:grid-cols-2`. Confirmation page: the banner sat in a `max-w-4xl` (896px) rounded container while sign-in renders full-bleed at `max-w-[1400px]`, so a wide banner read as a boxy card, now matched (**four different banner widths across 19 public pages** recorded in ROADMAP rather than swept). Agenda: a one-day event read "August 11 – August 11, 2026" because the header hard-coded `start – end` with date-fns, i.e. in the **viewer's** timezone, while the same page grouped sessions by the **event's** local date; new shared `formatEventDateRange` in [event-time.ts](src/lib/event-time.ts) collapses to the shortest unambiguous form in the event timezone, a rule that **already existed** for the `{{eventDateRange}}` email token and was simply absent from the UI (the email keeps its own formatter deliberately, since that string is merged into the MMG agreement document where the format is a stability contract). Its tests caught a genuine bug in my first version: **`Intl.DateTimeFormat` given `{ day, year }` with no month treats it as an unusual field combination and answers with a descriptive fallback, `"2026 (day: 14)"`**, which would have shipped on every multi-day single-month event. **Investigated and NOT a bug:** the "calendar says 1 hr instead of 1.30" report. `test-webinar` is genuinely 12:00–13:00 with event, session and Zoom all agreeing, and feeding a 90-minute window through the encoder produces the correct 90 minutes. The real gap is that **there is no duration input for a webinar anywhere**; length is implied entirely by the event's start/end datetime, and we push session times *to* Zoom but never read duration *back*. Recorded in ROADMAP with an owner question, alongside an adjacent latent find: `fromDatetimeLocal` on the event-create form **hardcodes a Dubai offset** while the form also collects a timezone (inert today, a platform blocker). **Also recorded, not fixed: cloning a WEBINAR event produces a broken webinar**. Clone copies `settings` wholesale resetting only `reviewerUserIds`, so the clone inherits `webinar.sessionId`, a pointer into the *source* event's sessions; Zoom then cannot be attached to any session on the clone and the 409 names a session that does not exist there (the organizer hit it twice, then abandoned the clone and built a fresh event 11 minutes later). No live event is affected and there is **no exposure**, since every anchor lookup binds `eventId` from the July 28 sweep. But `hemophilia-awareness-series-2026-july-10` is a *series*, and cloning is how you build the next instalment. The fix is an **allow-list** of settings keys that copy, not a deny-list: a deny-list goes stale the next time someone adds a key, which is precisely what happened, and `reviewerUserIds` proves someone reasoned about this once and the reasoning did not survive. Gate per commit: tsc 0, eslint 0, vitest 5032 → **5044**, build clean.
- **WEBINARS gets MEMBER parity, and the role-scoping bypass that turned up while checking it (August 10, 2026, owner-driven; commits `1492fc4d` + `db250e45`)** — Started as *"spawn a local instance with a webinar user profile, I wanna see what they can see"*. Looking at the role in a browser produced a scope change, two nav-vs-API mismatches, and a live permission bypass in two routes. **(1) The scope change** (owner: *"webinar role can see all events completed, published and live along with webinar as they are internal users but they see limited data"*, then the sharper framing *"can webinar has member role?"* — which is exactly right and made the work small). The desk surface in [event-access.ts](src/lib/event-access.ts) went **org-wide**: WEBINARS now sees every event in its org and holds the registration desk on all of them, which is precisely MEMBER's scope. It cost one line because **the two roles' write guards were already identical** — both in `RESTRICTED_WRITE_ROLES`, both in `REGISTRATION_DESK_ALLOW`, both in `FINANCE_ROLES` — so event scope was the only thing separating them; the model is now "MEMBER + full control on webinars". **The manage surface deliberately did NOT follow**: ~55 route files sit behind `WEBINAR_STAFF_ALLOW` and lean on that `where` to keep full control off conferences, so widening the default would open all 55 on conferences **in a single edit**. A test pins it, mutation-verified against that exact change. Consequence: `Event.settings.onsiteUserIds` no longer affects this role (the Onsite Staff tab still accepts it — harmless, now redundant; ONSITE still needs it). **Full MEMBER read parity was staged, not taken**: the ~59 event GETs still resolve on the manage surface, so a conference's agenda 404s — deferred to ROADMAP §"WEBINARS MEMBER-parity read sweep" because each GET needs a per-route judgement (the webinar console, email templates, scheduled emails and the org invoice ledger must stay refused; the ledger refusal is the Aug-4 H-1 decision, *finance-capable ≠ org-ledger access*, and MEMBER parity would have quietly reversed it). **(2) The two mismatches**, both found only by looking: the events list PAGE resolved on the manage surface while `GET /api/events` passed the desk surface, so **the endpoint returned events the page rendering them did not show**; and the sidebar offered the **AI Agent**, whose API admits only SUPER_ADMIN/ADMIN/ORGANIZER/MEMBER — the page loaded in full, suggested commands and all, and 403'd on the first send. New `WEBINARS_ROLE_HIDDEN_MODULES`, kept separate from `WEBINAR_HIDDEN_MODULES` because they answer different questions (one hides Accommodation because a *webinar* has no hotel; the other hides a module the *role* may not use). Rows now resolve through one `hrefFor()` — webinars to the full event, everything else to Registrations, that role's actual landing page — because a list of links that 404 is worse than no link; that also collapsed a ternary duplicated across two cells. **(3) The bypass — the substantive find.** Probing the boundary as ONSITE showed an account assigned to ONE conference getting **200 + 3 sessions and 200 + 4 speakers WITH EMAILS** on an event it was not assigned to, while the registrations route beside it correctly 404'd. Cause, one line in each of [sessions](src/app/api/events/%5BeventId%5D/sessions/route.ts) and [speakers](src/app/api/events/%5BeventId%5D/speakers/route.ts): `orgCtx ? { id, organizationId } : buildEventAccessWhere(session.user, eventId)`. It reads as *"an API key, otherwise a person"* and that is what it was meant to say — but `getOrgContext()` returns a context for **any** caller belonging to an org, a signed-in person included, so the first branch swallowed everyone and **the role rules in the second branch never ran at all**. So a desk temp could read every other event's agenda and full faculty roster (names, emails, phones, bios); prod had 1 ONSITE + 2 WEBINARS accounts, one used 3 days earlier, so this was live and reachable, not theoretical. **Neither branch is wrong on its own** — org-scoping IS correct for a key, the role predicate IS correct for a person — **which is why reading the code never found it: the defect is in the condition, not in what the condition guards, so a review of either half passes.** It only surfaces by asking who actually lands there, which is a question you answer by running it. Fixed with **no branch at all**: `accessUserFrom` builds one access user and there is a single predicate; a key carries no userId and no role so it lands on the org-scoped default exactly as before. The registrations route was already doing this correctly by hand (hence the 404 that made the difference visible) and now shares the helper, so the three cannot drift again. Sweep bounded: every route mixing API-key and session auth was checked and **only these two** had the shape (the `contacts/*` routes also use `getOrgContext` but are org-level, where org-scoping IS the boundary, and carry their own `canViewContacts`). Effect by role: ONSITE org-wide → assignment-gated (the fix); WEBINARS narrows to its webinars until the read sweep; MEMBER/ADMIN/ORGANIZER/API keys/org-null roles unchanged. **Tests** extend the July-7 ONSITE isolation suite with the two routes plus the helper's truth table incl. the fail-CLOSED case; mutation-verified (restoring the ternary fails). **Three unrelated suites broke** because they stubbed `@/lib/event-access` with a single export and the new one came back `undefined` — they now spread the real module and override only the predicate under test, so the next export cannot break them the same way (a hand-listed mock is a trap that springs on whoever adds the next export). Gate per commit: tsc 0, eslint 0, vitest 5024 → **5032**, build clean. Verified live in a browser as real accounts, both directions: unassigned event 404/404/404, assigned 200/200/200, and WEBINARS' own webinars untouched at 200.
- **Ops monitoring arc — daily health digest, worker watchdog, and the silent job-skipping bug they uncovered (August 5–10, 2026, owner-driven)** — Began as *"I want an agent checking CPU and emailing me daily"*. Two thirds already existed (6 CloudWatch alarms → SNS → krishna+vivek; [admin-alert.ts](src/lib/admin-alert.ts) emailing on **every** `apiLogger.error()` with 1h dedupe + 30/hr ceiling), so only the third was built — and pulling that thread exposed a live defect that had been degrading every background job for months. **(1) Daily digest** ([daily-digest-worker.ts](src/lib/daily-digest-worker.ts), JOB_ID 1015, 05:30 UTC = 09:30 Dubai, deliberately after the retention sweeps): one **infrastructure-only** email a day (owner scope call — no registration/revenue numbers), reusing `getInfraSnapshot()` (the `/admin/infra` data, forced past its 60s cache) so there is ONE definition of health rather than a second that can drift from the dashboard. **The verdict is computed by a pure `assessInfra()`, never written by the model** — the AI writes 2–3 sentences ON TOP of an already-decided OK/WARN/CRITICAL and cannot change it, because the failure mode that matters in a daily email is a summary softening the one line that needed to be alarming; `buildAiSummary()` is failure-isolated by contract (no key / provider down / timeout / empty → `null`, digest still sends with the numbers and says the prose was missing). Thresholds sit deliberately **below** the CloudWatch alarms (disk 70 vs 80, mem 80 vs 85, credits 200 vs 100) so a number trending wrong shows amber a day or two before the pager fires; warn-level log lines are counted but deliberately do NOT move the verdict (routine noise colouring it amber daily would make the colour meaningless); a section that could not be **read** is reported as unchecked in plain English, never counted as healthy. **Its whole point is that it arrives whether or not anything happened** — silence from alarms is ambiguous (a healthy night and a dead alerting pipeline look identical in an inbox), so a digest that *stops* arriving is itself the signal. **(2) Worker watchdog** ([scripts/worker-watchdog.sh](scripts/worker-watchdog.sh), cron `*/2`): a crash self-heals (`restart: unless-stopped` fires on exit) but a **freeze** leaves the container `Up` and useless — Docker detects it and flips the health label, then does nothing, because plain Compose only records health while Swarm acts on it. The script is that missing action layer and nothing more: it reads the label Docker already computed from 3 probes rather than re-implementing health checking. Restarts after **3 consecutive** unhealthy checks (~6 min, so a deploy's few-second gap can never reach it — a pinned test case), uses `docker restart` **never `compose up`** (which re-resolves `EA_SYS_WORKER_IMAGE` that cron doesn't export, and could silently roll prod back to an older tag), **alerts rather than recreating** a missing container (recreation = guessing an image tag), caps at **3 restarts/hour then escalates and goes quiet** (a restart loop churning the DB is worse than being down), has an escape hatch (`touch .watchdog-disabled`), and emails on every restart *on purpose* — a watchdog that silently papers over a daily freeze is how a real problem becomes invisible. 16-case state machine tested against a **fake `docker`** ([worker-watchdog.test.sh](scripts/worker-watchdog.test.sh)) wrapped in a vitest so CI enforces it. Owner added an Uptime Robot monitor on `/worker/health`, so detection is layered: external ~2 min → watchdog ~6 min → digest as backstop. **(3) The bug the digest surfaced.** Owner asked *"we have 1,490 scheduled jobs?"* about a digest number; it was a count of **completed runs**, but the breakdown showed `scheduled-emails` had run **435 times against a schedule of 1,440**, `crm-inbound-email` 375 of 1,440, `cert-issue` 182 of 480 — while hourly and daily jobs were exact, i.e. the shortfall scaled with frequency. Diagnosis: gaps scattered all day (not downtime — that is one block), always exact multiples of the cadence (cron fired), **zero** transient-skip warnings (not connection errors), and `pg_locks` showing locks held by connections **idle for minutes**. Cause: `pg_try_advisory_lock` must be released by the connection that took it, and Prisma hands out whichever is free — the release ran on a connection that never held the lock, did nothing, and the original sat on it. Nothing ever FAILED, so every surface was green: **every health surface asked "did the last run succeed?" and none asked "did it run as often as it should?"**. Effect: nothing lost (jobs are pollers over durable state), but bulk sends promising ~90s took 5–17 min. **The first fix attempt FAILED, and is recorded because the failure is instructive**: pinning the worker to session-mode `DIRECT_URL` removed pgbouncer's per-statement reassignment, and in the 30 minutes after deploy `scheduled-emails` ran **7 of 30** — the split also happens inside **Prisma's own pool**, one layer above the pooler (probed directly: acquire pid 14731, release pid 14727, release returns `false`). **Actually fixed** by replacing the lock with an expiring **lease** ([worker/lib/job-lease.ts](worker/lib/job-lease.ts) + `JobLease`, additive migration `20260810120000`, chain replay verified): claiming is ONE atomic `INSERT … ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE … WHERE free-or-expired`, so connection identity cannot affect correctness; leases **expire**, so a killed worker frees its job rather than wedging it (the advisory lock had no story for that at all); every mutation is **owner-conditional** so a tick that overran cannot release the successor that took over — the invariant preventing a double run; a 60s heartbeat against a 5-min TTL means "expired" always signifies *the holder died*, never *the holder is slow*, and a lease lost mid-tick logs at **error**. `withJobLock(jobId, jobName, fn)` signature kept so no job file changed logic; `advisory-lock.ts` **deleted rather than left as a shim** (a file named for a mechanism it no longer uses misleads the next reader). **Tested against real Postgres** ([tests/crm-db/job-lease.db.test.ts](tests/crm-db/job-lease.db.test.ts), 14 cases: the connection-split case the lock fails, 20-way concurrent claim admitting exactly one, expiry reclaim, the owner-conditional invariant, and the *"09:41 tick still running at 09:42"* overlap the owner asked about) **because it has to be** — a mocked Prisma has one fake connection, so the bug was not *expressible* in the unit suite, which is exactly how the lock passed a year of green tests. **Verified on prod within 4 minutes of deploy: full cadence restored** (`scheduled-emails` 4 of 4 expected, `crm-inbound-email` 4 of 4, up from ~23%), every lease row released seconds after its tick. Three guards so the class cannot hide again: skip log **debug → warn** (`worker:skip-tick-leased`), the digest's **expected-vs-actual** check against a new `expectedPerDay` on `EXPECTED_JOBS` (warns below 80%; its test is pinned to the real 435-of-1,440 numbers and asserts it is NOT reported as "failing" — it wasn't, and saying so sends the reader to the wrong place; that test also caught a genuine bug in my own threshold, `floor(1*0.8)=0` letting a never-run daily job clear the bar), and `worker:lease-lost-mid-tick` at error. **Also in the arc:** the `/admin/infra` worker probe retries once before declaring failure (a deploy restart was logging a false `infra:worker-unreachable`, which would have made the digest cry wolf on its own deploys); the "within ~60s" promise on bulk-email + certificate UI became **"within about 90 seconds"** (owner's point, and correct — the poll is every 60s, so a full interval plus the send is the honest number); the worker's pool stayed at **10** after measuring prod at 24 of `max_connections=90` (I had halved it to 5 on instinct, which would have traded a fixed bug for the June `P2024` regression). **Docs:** new [docs/BACKGROUND_JOBS.md](docs/BACKGROUND_JOBS.md) is the canonical *"I clicked send, where is it?"* reference (immediate-vs-queued split, why the jobs are pollers and missed ticks are **correctly** never replayed, why nothing stampedes on recovery, what happens when a tick runs long); [AWS_OPERATIONS.md §1.7 C/D/E](docs/AWS_OPERATIONS.md) covers the digest, the watchdog, and the diagnosis method; **user-guide §20 "I clicked send — where is it?"** is the operator-facing half so the Help Assistant can answer it; `worker/README.md` corrected (it claimed "5 cron-driven jobs" with 15 registered, and still described the June dual-write window). **Owner action outstanding: the watchdog crontab line** (docs/AWS_OPERATIONS.md §1.7 D).
- **Freshsales migration — the four fixes that make a 10k-deal import safe (August 10, 2026; commits `a326f4e7` / `c414c986` / `0d46b5b6` / `09f7d5c6`)** — Follow-through on the August-7 assessment of a real Freshsales tenant (**~10,000 deals / 4,400 contacts / 230 accounts**), whose full runbook lives in [docs/CRM_FRESHSALES_MIGRATION.md](docs/CRM_FRESHSALES_MIGRATION.md). Owner picked all three recommended options (declared date format · honest banner + higher cap · comfortable 5k chunks over jobifying). **(1) Dates are DECLARED, never guessed — the one that silently corrupted data.** The importer called `new Date(cell)`, which applies V8's US-centric lenient parser: on a day-first export days 1-12 of every month parsed as the **wrong date** (`05/03` read as 3 May, not 5 March) and days 13-31 came back Invalid and were dropped to `undefined` — and a dropped close date on a won deal fell through to `?? new Date()`, **stamping the import date**, so historical wins became "won today" and a won-in-July report quietly returned zero. None of it shows in the row counts. Now the format is picked in the dialog (ISO / DD-MM / MM-DD), parsed strictly, dates anchor to **UTC midnight** (killing a second, separate off-by-one where local-midnight parsing shifted a day-precision date once serialised), rolled-over dates (`Date.UTC(2026,1,31)` cheerfully yields 3 March) and 2-digit years are refused, and a value contradicting the declared format is a **row error**. ISO is accepted under every format since it's unambiguous. **Auto-detection was considered and rejected**: scanning for a day > 12 works right up until a file where every date falls on the 1st-12th, at which point it guesses — and a guess that is usually right is exactly this failure mode. **The dry run now ECHOES the first parsed date** (`05/03/2026 → 5 Mar 2026`) because both orders parse cleanly for days 1-12, so counts alone can never reveal a wrong pick. An undated won/lost deal keeps `wonAt`/`lostAt` **NULL** and is reported — it correctly drops out of date-ranged reports rather than landing in the wrong bucket. **(2) The dropped fields.** Contacts had **no owner field in the spec at all** (4,400 would import unassigned regardless of the CSV); deals matched owners by email only, though a Freshsales list view renders *Sales Owner* as a display **name** and may offer no email column — so every deal could land unowned too. Both now use **one shared resolver** (the cross-caller-duplication rule): email wins, then an unambiguous name match; an **ambiguous** name (two "John Smith"s) assigns **nobody** and is counted separately, because picking the first would hand one rep's whole book to another and — unlike a blank owner — that is not visibly wrong. Still role-bound to `CRM_OWNER_ROLES`; on update an unmatchable owner never un-owns a live record. Also newly imported: contact `lifecycleStage` + `status` (coerced case/punctuation-insensitively; an unrecognised label stays **NULL and reported**, since defaulting every unknown to `NEW` would silently rewrite the pipeline's shape), deal `dealTypeId` by name (unknown → untyped + named in the report), deal + company `tags` through the same normalizer contacts use, company `phone`, and `dealreason`/`reasonforloss` synonyms (the API field is `deal_reason_id`, so the column may well read "Deal Reason" — without it a whole column of lost reasons imported as *unrecognized*). **Deal `pipeline` is deliberately NOT a CSV column**: `CrmDealPipeline` is our own two-value classification and a Freshsales pipeline *name* can't map onto it without a translation table nobody has, so the operator picks one **per file** in the dialog. **(3) The caps.** `/api/crm/import/*` now gets **8MB** ([body-limits.ts](src/lib/body-limits.ts), extracted from `proxy.ts` so it's unit-testable without dragging in NextAuth) — nginx already allowed 10MB, so our 1MB was the binding limit behind the 413 on an ordinary 2-3MB export; the allow-list is narrow and tested against look-alike prefixes because every entry is a path where a request can make the box buffer 8MB. And **per-row lookups became one prefetch per file** (`indexBy`): each row used to cost two reads before its write — 15,000 sequential round trips for a 5,000-row file, which is what pushed a large import past the 60s gateway timeout, and a timeout there is not a clean failure (the rows already written stay written and the operator gets a bare 504 with no report). Safe because the in-file `seenKeys` dedup already rejects a second row carrying either identity, so a prefetched map can't go stale within its own file; concurrent imports are still caught by the unique indexes. **Writes stay per-row deliberately** — `createMany` is faster but loses the per-row try/catch, and one bad row killing a 5,000-row file is a far worse trade. **(4) Honest truncation.** The deals board returned at most 1,000 rows and **said nothing about it**: a pipeline with 10,412 deals rendered as a pipeline with 1,000 deals — not a visibly broken screen, a *plausible* one, and every total read off it was wrong (contacts and companies truncated at 500 the same way). All three list routes now return the **true total** alongside the page and the UI renders "Showing 2,000 of 10,412 — narrow the filters" ([list-caps.ts](src/crm/lib/list-caps.ts) + [list-truncation-banner.tsx](src/crm/components/list-truncation-banner.tsx)). The cap is a **rendering budget**; the count is the correctness mechanism. Board capped at 2,000 deliberately — it renders every card with **no virtualisation**, so raising it trades a truthful banner for a frozen tab. `truncated` compares total against what was **returned**, not against the cap (keying on `returned === CAP` would false-positive on an org holding exactly CAP rows). The metadata rides the **same React Query cache entry** as the list via two `select`s over one `queryFn`, so the banner costs no second fetch and the 11 existing `useCrmDeals`/`Contacts`/`Companies` call sites keep returning a plain array. **+40 tests** across the four commits; three of them **mutation-verified** (restoring `?? new Date()` fails the wonAt-NULL regression; pointing the truncation count at a wider `where` fails the same-where assertion; reverting an export route to `requireCrmRead` fails the CSV-gate drift guard). Also fixed **two pre-existing tag-route tests that were passing by accident** — they mock `findMany` only, so once the routes added a `count` the `Promise.all` rejected and they were asserting against the 500 path. Suite 4933 → 4982; tsc/eslint/build green per commit. **Still outstanding: a real 5-row sample export** — it decides which further header synonyms are needed and which date format to pick, and is the only thing between here and a live migration. **Deliberately not built** (recorded in the doc §6): jobifying the import onto the worker tier (would remove the 60s ceiling and allow one file per entity, at the cost of a job table + progress + resume), batched writes, board virtualisation, and a Freshsales-pipeline→`CrmDealPipeline` mapping UI.

- **Survey share link no longer submits — it emails you your own link (B1 CLOSED, August 7, 2026)** — Closes the **last open BLOCKER** on the board, from the July-13 Survey+RSVP review. **The defect:** the share link is designed to be BROADCAST (QR on a closing slide, WhatsApp, an email signature), so it carries **no per-person identity** — one token for the whole event. The old handler took the respondent's identity as a **typed email** and submitted the survey on that basis, stamping `Registration.surveyCompletedAt`. That flag is not cosmetic: [certificates/auto-issue.ts](src/lib/certificates/auto-issue.ts) polls exactly it and mints a real, serialized, audited **CME certificate**. So anyone who knew an attendee's email (routinely public for medical faculty) could (1) issue a certificate in their name off garbage answers, (2) **permanently lock the real attendee out** — `SurveyResponse.registrationId` is `@unique`, the flag is set, and there is no organizer "reset survey" — and (3) poison the accreditation dataset. **The fix (option (a), owner-selected after tracing the alternatives):** the share page is now a **gateway, not a form**. It takes the typed email and, if it matches a non-cancelled registration, mints **the same per-registration token the bulk-email invitation path mints** (`survey:{regId}`, 256-bit `randomBytes`, stored **hashed**, single-use, TTL-bounded) and **emails it to that address**; the respondent answers via the secure `?token=` path, which derives the registration **from the token** and never from user input. Identity therefore rests on **possession of a secret delivered to the registered mailbox** instead of on an unverified assertion — a stranger typing a victim's address now merely causes the real attendee to receive their own link. **M1 (the enumeration oracle) closes in the same change:** one identical generic response for registered / unregistered / already-completed, so the endpoint can't be used to test whether a named physician attended (an already-completed person still gets a link — the token page explains it in their own inbox, keeping the HTTP response uniform). **Rate limiting re-shaped for the intended use, which is the subtle part:** the share request is dispatched **before** the submit limit (10/15min/IP, calibrated for one-submit-per-person) and carries its own — **100/15min per IP** (room-scale: a whole hall scans the QR from ONE venue-NAT egress IP; this is the same failure mode that got the `ipHash` dedup deleted in H1, where the guard fired hardest at the exact moment of intended use) plus **3/hr per email address** to stop mail-bombing one person. The per-email limit deliberately returns **the same generic 200, not a 429**, because any status that varies with the email would re-open the oracle it exists beside. **Surfaces:** [survey/route.ts](src/app/api/public/events/%5Bslug%5D/survey/route.ts) (`handleShareRequestLink` replaces `handleShareSubmit`), [public survey page](src/app/e/%5Bslug%5D/survey/page.tsx) (share mode renders the email gateway + a "Check your inbox" panel; questions and submit are not rendered at all), and the [survey builder](src/app/%28dashboard%29/events/%5BeventId%5D/survey/page.tsx) share-link card copy, which described the old trust model. **+7 tests** ([public-survey-route.test.ts](__tests__/api/public-survey-route.test.ts)) pinning: **no stamp / no `SurveyResponse` even when `answers` are supplied** (the old exploit shape, asserted dead), token mint dropping any previous one + email carrying a `?token=` (not `?share=`) link, **byte-equal non-enumeration** responses, already-completed still gets a link, invalid + expired share tokens, per-email limit → generic 200 with nothing sent, and a **dispatch-ordering regression guard** (exactly two limit checks) so the conference room can't be silently cut off again. Suite 4905 → 4912; tsc/eslint/build green. **Live state at close (verified read-only on prod):** the only share link ever generated had **expired 2026-07-18** on a COMPLETED event with **0 tokens outstanding**, so the window was never exploited — but 4 templates still had `autoIssueOnSurvey = true`, i.e. the hole would have re-armed the moment an organizer clicked *Generate*. Whole-feature usage was **2 survey responses ever**, so the change carried no migration and broke no habit. **The lesson, worth carrying beyond this feature:** the share link shipped when `surveyCompletedAt` was *just a feedback flag* — trusting a typed email was a defensible trade **at the time**. Certificate auto-issue later **promoted that flag into a credential-issuing trigger**, and its own comment even read *"the survey POST path is UNTOUCHED — it already sets surveyCompletedAt."* Nobody went back to ask who was allowed to set it. **When a field becomes a credential trigger, re-audit every writer of that field.**

- **Restricted-role read narrowing + an events/submitter polish round (August 7, 2026, organizer-reported)** — A day of small organizer reports, three of which turned out to be real exposure rather than cosmetics. **(1) Changing an existing team member's role was four roles behind.** `POST /api/organization/users` (invite) accepted all seven assignable roles while `PATCH /api/organization/users/[userId]` (change role) accepted only `["ADMIN","ORGANIZER","REVIEWER"]` — two hand-written lists, one never updated — so a person could be INVITED as Webinars but never MOVED to it, and MEMBER / ONSITE / CRM_USER were stuck the same way (organizer hit it moving a colleague to Webinars; the 400 surfaced as `organization/users:zod-validation-failed`). Both doors now derive from `ASSIGNABLE_USER_ROLES` in [auth-guards.ts](src/lib/auth-guards.ts), with a **compile-time guard** (`_AssignableCoversTeamRoles`) that breaks the build if a role joins `TEAM_ROLES` without becoming assignable; SUPER_ADMIN stays deliberately un-grantable from an ordinary admin surface. In-band hardening: the update compound-wheres `{ id, organizationId }` (the write is org-bound, not just the preceding lookup) and the audit row records `previousRole` — a privilege-change trail that said what someone IS but not what they WERE is half a trail. **(2) Honest sign-in copy on the submitter/proposer doors.** Step 1's preflight checks `User` by email, and `User.email` is unique platform-wide, so "You already have an account" fired for an account created on a DIFFERENT event and read to organizers as "this person is already registered here". Now: *"This email already has an account from another event. Sign in and we'll add you to this one, then take you to the abstract/proposal form."* Contacts are not involved and never were (a Contact has no credentials); the [check-email route](src/app/api/public/events/%5Bslug%5D/check-email/route.ts) docblock claimed cross-event accounts were deliberately NOT reported — true until `hasAccount` was added for the abstract flow, and corrected here with both scopes spelled out so nobody "fixes" the working behavior. **(3) Session-proposal description capped at 3000 chars** in a taller resizable box with a live counter — ONE constant ([session-proposal-content.ts](src/lib/session-proposal-content.ts)) backs the field's `maxLength`, the submit guard AND both write routes' Zod, so form and server cannot disagree; `maxLength` only blocks typing, so the submit path checks the VALUE (a longer description loaded into edit mode gets a clear message, not a 400). Verified read-only on prod first: 2 proposals exist, longest 21 chars, so nothing existing became unsavable. **(4) Brand — "MM Group Events", not "EventsHub"** (this silo serves MM Group only): the landing page, all four auth screens, the sidebar fallback, and — the part that mattered — the team-invitation email (HTML + text), the password-reset subject + body and the default email footer, which are what a new colleague reads before ever seeing the app. **(5) The read narrowing (the substantive half).** The events list is ONE component and ONE endpoint shared by organizers and org-null roles, queried with a bare `include` — so an abstract submitter's portal showed Registrations/Speakers headcounts AND the page shipped them the entire Event row (settings JSON, `bankDetails`, tax config, per-event sender). Sweeping the rest of their surface found two more: the event **detail** GET (deliberately serves org-null roles) returned the same full row — `settings.reviewerUserIds` (who is scoring a submitter's work), `surveyShareLink` (a live token), sponsors, webinar/group config, the internal `emailCcAddresses` — with only finance columns redacted; and **`GET .../speakers`** explicitly supported session auth for these roles and returned the **ENTIRE faculty roster** (every speaker's email, phone, bio, abstract titles) when the only reason those pages call it is to find the caller's OWN speaker row to bind as author — reachable by anyone with a self-service submitter account. All three now fetch a whitelist rather than filtering after the fact (hiding a column in CSS leaves it in the payload), and the speakers list returns own-row-only for org-null callers. **Consolidated, not accumulated** (owner pushed back mid-round on exactly this): the list select and the detail select were two hand-written lists of the same columns, and both now live in **[event-visibility.ts](src/lib/event-visibility.ts)** — sibling of `finance-`/`barcode-`/`contact-visibility`, the house convention for "which FIELDS may this role see" — with the detail view **derived** from the list view and a test asserting that derivation; [event-access.ts](src/lib/event-access.ts) goes back to answering only WHICH events a role may see. Fails closed: an unrecognised role gets the narrow shape. The settings blob is rebuilt key by key from a 2-key whitelist, so a settings key added later is invisible until someone decides otherwise. Staff payloads and the API-key path are unchanged. **(6) The account menu is trimmed for guests: the permissions checklist AND the Profile entry are staff-only.** `/profile` holds a name field plus the email signature appended to ORGANISER emails, so an org-null role could only ever store a signature that never renders; they edit their details on **My Details** (submitters) or on their **registration** (registrants). Enforced in three places, not just the menu: the item is hidden, `src/proxy.ts` redirects REVIEWER/SUBMITTER off `/profile` (REGISTRANT was already bounced from every dashboard route), and `GET`/`PATCH /api/profile` now refuse non-staff with a logged 403 — **superseding that route's original "every authenticated user edits their own signature regardless of role" rule** (key-file line above corrected). Known consequence, accepted: a REVIEWER now has no self-service page to change their own name — reviewer names are set by the admin who invited them, and password changes still go through forgot-password. The permissions checklist — a submitter/reviewer/registrant saw four rows about a system they never asked to use, two of them greyed-out crosses. The predicate could NOT come from `auth-guards` (it imports `next/server` + the Pino logger; importing that into a `"use client"` component is the silent-`undefined`-at-click class), so `TEAM_ROLES`/`isTeamRole` are now DECLARED in a dependency-free **[team-roles.ts](src/lib/team-roles.ts)** and re-exported from auth-guards — every existing import keeps working, one list, no client copy. **Tests:** +33 across the day (assignable-role matrix incl. "neither route re-declares its own list", proposal-length boundary, `event-visibility` select/derivation/fail-closed/settings-whitelist, and route-level org-null pins), suite 4855 → 4882. Two gates **mutation-verified** (removing the list gate fails 7 tests; removing the speakers gate fails 3). One existing test changed MEANING and is called out in the commit: it asserted the redactor stripped `taxRate` from a submitter payload — the row is no longer fetched, so it now asserts the SELECT, because a mock returns what it is told regardless of `select` and a body assertion would pass against a widened query. **Deliberately NOT changed** (product decisions, not defects, both recorded in ROADMAP): a reviewer still sees an abstract's author (review is single-blind), and a submitter still sees the mean score on their own abstract. **(7) Submission requirements tightened (owner):** **theme is required to submit** — but only when the event HAS themes, since themes are per-event and optional and an absolute rule would make submission impossible on an event whose organiser created none (drafts exempt, mirroring presentation type); and **bio joined the submitter profile-completeness set** ([submitter-profile-completeness.ts](src/lib/submitter-profile-completeness.ts)), which is the HARD gate on submitting an abstract or proposal — it is printed in the programme and read out at the introduction, so discovering it missing after acceptance is the expensive moment. On My Details the field also moved out from under the "Optional" heading, where it plainly read as optional. **Live impact checked read-only before shipping: 3 published events have themes (12/9/5), and ALL 12 submitter-linked speakers had no bio**, so the whole current cohort is sent to My Details before their next submission — the honest cost of "mandatory". **(8) Sub-themes under a theme** (new `AbstractSubTheme` + nullable `Abstract.subThemeId`; additive+idempotent migration `20260807120000`, replayed from empty + `migrate diff` clean): organisers add a further breakdown beneath any theme, and the submitter gets a second dropdown carrying THAT theme's children. Required only where they exist, keyed on the **chosen theme's** children rather than "does this event have sub-themes anywhere" — otherwise adding them to one theme would start demanding them on every other theme, making the feature impossible to adopt gradually. One pure helper ([abstract-theme-requirement.ts](src/lib/abstract-theme-requirement.ts)) carries both rules for the 3 submit forms + both write routes; sub-themes ride **nested in the themes GET** rather than getting a list endpoint, so the two dropdowns read one source and cannot show a theme whose children came from a stale fetch. Guards: a sub-theme from another theme is a **404, not a silent accept** (create + update); the update validates against the theme the abstract will END UP on and **clears a stale sub-theme** when the theme changes without one being restated; **delete is refused while abstracts use it** with the count (the FK is SET NULL — a delete would not error, it would quietly erase the classification); `sortOrder` computed inside the creating transaction; `@@unique([themeId, name])` → 409 not 500. **Verified in the browser on the local prod-shaped DB** (owner asked): added two sub-themes, saw the dropdown appear on selection and vanish for a theme with none, was blocked on submit without one, submitted successfully, confirmed the row + the "Theme › Sub-theme" badge, then deleted the test rows. That check also surfaced a **stale Prisma client in the running dev server** (client regenerated 13:38, server booted 09:23) returning 500 on the themes GET — a known false alarm, fixed by restarting the dev server, not a code bug. **Also this day:** `npm run uploads:refresh` ([scripts/dev-uploads-refresh.sh](scripts/dev-uploads-refresh.sh)) — `db:refresh` restores ROWS, not the FILES they point at, so a freshly refreshed local DB renders broken images everywhere (the "org logo is missing everywhere" report: row set, file 200 on prod, 24 files locally against ~500 in the bucket). Read-only S3 sync into the gitignored `public/uploads/`, counts by category, **no `--delete`** (mirroring the hourly prod sync whose non-deleting behaviour made INC-004 recoverable). Local now 514 files / 64 MB; the bucket has NO `speaker-docs/` or `reimbursements/` directory, so no passport scans or bank details have ever been uploaded on prod.

- **Group Registration Phase 2 — card payment for the whole company (August 6, 2026; plan §7 item 2)** — Phase 1 shipped pay-later only; a group can now settle by card. **ONE Stripe session for the whole group**, deliberately not N per-member sessions (the model's premise is one payer / one total / one document, and per-member charges would produce partial settlements the consolidated invoice can't represent). New **`POST /api/public/events/[slug]/group-checkout`** ([route](src/app/api/public/events/%5Bslug%5D/group-checkout/route.ts)) charges the **INVOICE's frozen snapshot**, never a fresh computation — so the card statement, the PDF and the AR ledger can't disagree after a post-issue member cancellation; descriptive per-type lines ("2 × Physician", shared with the invoice via the already-exported `buildGroupLineItems`) render only while they still sum to the invoice subtotal, else it falls back to one honest line rather than show a Stripe page whose items don't add up to its own total. 15/60s per-IP limit (corporate-NAT parity with the singles checkout), conditional member claim UNPAID/PENDING→PENDING with the just-created session **expired** on a lost race. **Webhook**: `handleGroupCheckoutCompleted` in the shared dispatcher ([stripe-webhook-handler.ts](src/lib/stripe-webhook-handler.ts)) — dispatched before the single-registration path since a group session carries no `registrationId`; charge-level idempotency (`Payment.stripePaymentId`), **ONE Payment row anchored to the group** (`registrationId` null), N members flipped in one scoped write, org-mismatch refusal on the per-org endpoint, and an already-settled group still **books the money** + alerts (duplicate-charge parity with singles) while sending no second invoice. **`issuePaidGroupDocuments`** ([invoice-service.ts](src/lib/invoice-service.ts)) **PROMOTES** the consolidated invoice rather than minting a RECEIPT — the group PDF already renders its "Payment Received" block off the linked Payment, and a second numbered document would make the org's AR ledger double-count; idempotent via a conditional `updateMany`, mints the invoice if group-create's failure-isolated attempt had failed, and `sendGroupInvoiceEmail` now derives its label from the row (`Paid Invoice` vs `Invoice`) so a settled payer never gets something reading like a request to pay. `checkout.session.expired` releases **only the members that session parked** (scoped on `stripeCheckoutSessionId`, so a second open tab's claim survives). **Refund policy — owner ruling: record + alert, never auto-reconcile.** `charge.refunded` on a group payment previously hit a fail-loud log stub; it now records the cumulative refund on the Payment row (conditional, so redelivery can't double-count) and fires a **loud admin notification naming the members still marked PAID** — but flips no registrations, because one charge covers N members and "this was refunded" doesn't say WHICH members lost their place (a company dropping 3 of 40 and a company withdrawing entirely produce the identical Stripe event; guessing would either strand paid attendees seatless or leave withdrawn ones holding badges). Full automated group refund reconciliation, incl. the common partial case, remains unbuilt. **UI**: the success card offers "Pay {total} by card" on top of the invoice — the invoice is issued either way because a coordinator often isn't the person holding the company card — plus the Stripe-return states (`payment=success` / `payment=cancelled`, the latter reassuring that the registration is safe + offering retry); page wrapped in `Suspense` for `useSearchParams` per the confirmation-page pattern. +28 tests ([stripe-group.test.ts](__tests__/api/webhooks/stripe-group.test.ts) 15: group-anchored Payment, scoped member flip, invoice promotion, charge-idempotency, duplicate-charge books-but-doesn't-email, cross-org refusal, documents-failure alert, session-scoped release, and the refund matrix incl. **never-auto-flips**; [group-checkout-route.test.ts](__tests__/api/group-checkout-route.test.ts) 13) — suite 4750 → **4778**. Both financial assertions were **mutation-verified**: recomputing from live members instead of the invoice makes two tests fail (the first draft of the headline test passed against that bug and was strengthened with a divergent fixture). **Parked by the owner mid-build:** billing accounts per-event vs org-shared (ROADMAP §"Billing accounts — per-event vs org-shared payer records").
- **Group Registration Phase 1 — coordinator registers 2–50 people, ONE payer, ONE consolidated invoice (August 6, 2026, owner go-ahead; plan docs/GROUP_REGISTRATION_PLAN.md)** — The July-30 blueprint's Phase 1, built + live-verified on the local DB (browser + API end-to-end). **Schema (migration `20260806150000`, additive+idempotent, re-run verified):** new `RegistrationGroup` anchor (event Cascade · coordinator User SetNull + name/email snapshots · required BillingAccount payer Restrict · `payerReference` PO · org scalar stamped at create); `Registration.groupId` (SetNull) + `RegistrationCreatedSource.GROUP_REGISTER`; **`Invoice.registrationId` + `Payment.registrationId` → NULLABLE** with `groupId` alternatives (app-level XOR; Cascade mirrors the registration semantics). Null-guard sweep was compiler-tight: only 3 files (charge.refunded branch fails loud on a registration-less payment — group refund reconciliation is Phase 2; `sendInvoiceEmail` refuses group invoices; org ledger bills groups to the payer name). **Service** ([group-registration-service.ts](src/services/group-registration-service.ts)): ONE `tenantTransaction` — existing-registration dup check → group row → **all-or-nothing seat claims** (per-type `claimSeats` + event-wide `claimEventSeats(n)`; SOLD_OUT/EVENT_FULL roll the whole group back) → per-member attendee+serial+qrCode+registration rows (UNPAID, payer-bound, `originalPrice` = the tier on sale NOW via `pickCurrentPricingTier` — owner: "whatever is open at submission"; `requiresApproval` → PENDING; the coordinator's own row links their account). Payer via `findOrCreateBillingAccount` (exact-name reuse, `needsReview` fuzzy flag; `CreateBillingAccountInput.userId` widened to nullable + `source: "public"`) + `EventBillingAccount` auto-attach. Post-commit failure-isolated: `createGroupInvoice` (consolidated INVOICE, groupId-anchored, Σ member `originalPrice` + event tax, house numbering; failure → admins notified "create one manually") → `sendGroupInvoiceEmail` (payer + coordinator, deduped, PDF attached; group PDF renders payer bill-to + Coordinator/Attendees meta + **derived per-type line items** "2 × Physician" via `groupLineItems` on InvoicePDFData) → member confirmations with the new `coveredByGroupPayerName` mode (**green "covered by {payer}" block REPLACES Pay Now, quote PDF suppressed — members are never dunned**) → coordinator summary via the new editable **`group-registration-confirmation`** system template (memberSummary raw-HTML table, escaped builder; preview samples + slugs mirror + drift tests updated) → per-member `syncToContact` + audit + notify + stats. **Public flow:** `POST /api/public/events/[slug]/group-register` (register-mirroring rate limits + per-coordinator-email limit; full public field-set per member incl. role/specialty; coordinator-attending⇔member-list consistency 400s; coordinator account = existing-with-password sign-in (bad creds 401, abstract-start pattern) or new REGISTRANT create mirroring ensureRegistrantAccount incl. internal-domain tiers — runs PRE-create so the group row links `coordinatorUserId`; `runWithTenant` after event resolve + check-tenant-als gate entry) + link-only page [/e/[slug]/group/register](src/app/e/%5Bslug%5D/group/register/page.tsx) (coordinator → payer → repeatable members with live tier prices → live subtotal/VAT/total → success card; "I am attending" mirrors their details into member #1). Public event API exposes the parsed `groupRegistration` settings. **Organizer:** Event Settings → Registration "Group Registration" card (enable + min/max, hard ceiling 50 clamped in [group-registration-settings.ts](src/lib/group-registration-settings.ts) — corrupt settings fail CLOSED, opt-in polarity — + copy-link button; deliberately NOT advertised on the public register page, owner decision) + a violet **Group** badge on the registrations list. **Tenancy born-compliant:** org stamping, `tenantTransaction`, `runWithTenant`, gate entry, [prisma/rls/registrationgroup.sql](prisma/rls/registrationgroup.sql) flat policy in the same change. **Live-test catch:** the coordinator email first FAILED on SES — `getEventTemplate` only returns branding when a DB template row exists and no event has one for the NEW slug, so the send fell back to the unverified env sender; fixed by threading the event's `emailFromAddress/Name` explicitly (`brandingFrom`), re-verified SENT. +37 tests (settings truth table incl. clamp/fail-closed; service gates/happy-path row contract/invoice-isolation/PENDING-parity; route consistency/credentials/mapping) — suite 4655 → 4693. **NOT in Phase 1** (per plan §7/§8): card checkout + group webhook branch, the My Group portal (add/edit members), organizer roll-up view + CSV column, MCP tools, per-company invite links. **Same-day follow-up — review M4 ruled: a group BURNS the tier's inventory.** A member priced at the live tier now claims THAT TIER's seat, exactly like an individual public registration — [registration-seat.ts](src/lib/registration-seat.ts)'s `seatCounter` routes a named `TIER_CONSUMING_SOURCES` set (`PUBLIC_REGISTER` + `GROUP_REGISTER`) with a `pricingTierId` to the tier counter, so **every release/reactivate/type-change/delete/reconcile path follows for free** (they all route through the one helper; verified each already selects `createdSource` + `pricingTierId`). The service aggregates its all-or-nothing claim **per counter** via `seatCounter` rather than re-deriving it, and a tier sell-out names the tier ("Physician — Early Bird sold out"), not just the type. Rationale: the group door is unauthenticated public self-service, so price must carry allocation — otherwise one 40-person group drains the discount budget invisibly and Early Bird never advances to Standard for individual registrants. The **staff manual-add courtesy-seat exemption is deliberately unchanged** (an organizer recording a latecomer at the Early-Bird rate still doesn't burn a real Early-Bird seat) — the asymmetry is now spelled out at both sites so it isn't "fixed" later. No behavior change on any live event until a tier actually carries a seat limit (most are unlimited), and no data repair (zero GROUP_REGISTER rows existed). +5 tests.

Shared client-safe helpers in [src/lib/submission-deadline.ts](src/lib/submission-deadline.ts) (`readSessionProposalDeadline` defensive parse + `isDeadlinePassed`; corrupt values fail OPEN — a bad setting never locks intake). **Auto-end semantics**: past the deadline the public proposer door 403s ("The session proposal deadline has passed" — server + the shared register component's client gate via a new `sessionProposalSettings` block on the public event API), and a SUBMITTER can no longer create a proposal (`DEADLINE_PASSED` 403 on the POST) or submit a draft (PUT DRAFT→SUBMITTED refused; the form hides Submit and keeps Save as Draft with an explanatory line; a fresh visit shows a "deadline has passed" card). **STAFF are exempt** (post-deadline entries on someone's behalf are deliberate — the grant-flow sales-window-override philosophy). **Extend = edit the date**: the event PUT refuses a NEW/CHANGED past value (400 `DEADLINE_IN_PAST`) but an UNCHANGED already-past value saves (the M9 lesson — unrelated settings edits never blocked); clearing to null always allowed. H2 — double-grant races: the companion helper's create-path link became a **conditional `updateMany` claim inside the tx** on `opts.expectedLink` (the RAW, possibly-CANCELLED pointer the caller read); a lost race throws the internal `CompanionLinkRaceError` sentinel (the `PromoSentinel` house pattern) rolling back attendee+registration+serial and returning the winner as `already-linked`; the payable path claims identically and a lost race **cancels the just-minted duplicate** via `payment-service.cancelRegistration(refund:false)` + 409 `GRANT_RACE_LOST` (honest note: a payment email may have gone out). **Batch 2 (MEDs + owner rulings, `d9079985`):** M2 — only a genuinely EMPTY body means comp; non-empty unparseable JSON 400s `INVALID_JSON` (was: silent free-registration mint). ""` decision item).

- **Session-proposal signups mint NO registration — per-person Grant dialog (comp OR payable) (August 5, 2026, organizer decision — REVERSES the July-30 auto-comp+revoke model)** — Organizer: "session proposal should not have a complimentary registration… most proposers are invited faculty, some must register and pay, some get comped" (last year: 14 proposers = 9 comp / 3 paid / 2 submitted-only no-shows). **(1) The doors:** both proposal doors (the `/proposal/register` signup + the sign-in shortcut) now call `ensureSpeakerCompanionRegistration(…, { linkOnly: true })` — new option in [speaker-companion.ts](src/lib/speaker-companion.ts) that still LINKS an existing same-email registration (someone who registered themselves) but never creates the comp Faculty row (`link-only-no-create`). Abstract signups unchanged (auto-comp stays). **(2) Grant is the explicit action:** [grant-companion route](src/app/api/events/%5BeventId%5D/speakers/%5BspeakerId%5D/grant-companion/route.ts) gained `mode: "comp" | "payable"` (empty body = comp, backward compat): **comp** = the historical one-click Faculty companion; **payable** = a REAL registration on an organizer-chosen ticket type (+ tier) minted from the speaker's existing details via `registration-service.createRegistration` — which owns seat claim, UNASSIGNED payment default, and the **auto confirmation email + quote PDF + Pay Now link**, so the person is asked to pay with zero re-registration; the new registration is linked as the speaker's attendee facet. Guards: live linked reg → 409 `ALREADY_HAS_REGISTRATION`; service `ALREADY_REGISTERED` → links the existing row (`linked-existing`); Faculty types refused by the service's existing guard; audited `COMPANION_GRANTED` with `mode: "payable"`. **(3) UI:** shared [GrantRegistrationDialog](src/components/speakers/grant-registration-dialog.tsx) (two option cards + type/tier pickers, faculty types filtered, no-misleading-$0 price labels, inactive tiers annotated) replaces the one-click grant buttons on the proposal detail sheet + the speaker page Registration card. **Badges:** comp → "Faculty"; payable → the badge route's existing `"DELEGATE"` fallback; per-registration override via the detail sheet as always. **Existing proposal-door comps were left untouched** — organizer reviews + revokes individually (Revoke button unchanged). +13 tests (linkOnly unit pins incl. never-touches-Faculty-type, door linkOnly wiring, payable route matrix: TICKET_TYPE_REQUIRED / mints-from-speaker-details + links + audits / 409 live-link / cancelled-link-grants / linked-existing / service-code passthrough / empty-body comp compat). User-guide Session Proposals callout rewritten ("Attendance is YOUR call, per person"). **Same-day follow-ups:** **(a) fresh proposers start as speaker status INVITED** (owner: submitting a proposal ≠ confirmed speaker; team reviews then flips to Confirmed by hand) — `EventSpeakerProfile.status` (CREATE-only; the upsert never touches an EXISTING speaker's status, so invited faculty inherit whatever the organizer set); abstract signups also flipped to INVITED the same day (owner follow-up); Option B (a dedicated PENDING enum value) noted for later if "Invited" confuses (+3 tests); **(b) Grant/Re-grant Registration button moved into the speaker page's gradient header next to Delete** (shown only when the speaker has no live registration; the Registration card keeps pointer text).

- **Submitter My Details arc — independent doors ("both"), speaker profile form, editable neutral My Details page (August 4–5, 2026, owner-driven iteration; commits `1b7c2de2` → `d98fe270` → `e8786d01` → `2105b371` → `59065664` → my-details rename)** — A multi-round rework of the submitter (abstract + session-proposal) experience. **(1) Independent doors — SUPERSEDES the July-30 "first flow wins" rule.** `Speaker.submitterSource` gained a `"both"` value (string column, no migration): a signup/sign-in door **GRANTS its surface and never removes the other** — an existing different source widens to `"both"` (sticky) at the ONE stamping choke point (`upsertEventSpeaker` in [speaker-companion.ts](src/lib/speaker-companion.ts)). Owner model confirmed: the two registers are independent; someone submitting both through their own links sees both, one account, ONE profile.
