Docs pass `a84e72f8`. **(3) Editable My Details** (`e8786d01`) — new PATCH on `abstracts/my-profile` (own-speaker by userId only, email immutable, null-clears semantics, 30/hr, self-audit with before→after, full contact sync incl. **photo + bio** which also joined the GET select + view mode); the page auto-opens the edit form when required fields are missing and an amber banner appears there AND on the abstracts/session-proposals pages ([submitter-profile-nudge.tsx](src/components/abstracts/submitter-profile-nudge.tsx)) — text simplified Aug 5 to just "Please complete your details". Session-proposal **Format field removed everywhere** (form/list/sheet/CSV; DB column + API kept). **(4) ONE neutral landing** (`2105b371` + rename) — both flows' sign-in/signup land on My Details, which moved from `/abstracts/profile` to **`/events/[eventId]/my-details`** (owner: a proposer must not see "abstracts" in the URL); old path is a permanent redirect, middleware allow-list extended, `submitterHomePath` returns it for everyone. **(5) Registration card removed from My Details** (`59065664`) — the comp/Faculty registration facet (payment/ticket/badge/check-in/survey) is organizer bookkeeping, not submitter-facing; organizer-side speaker page unchanged. +14 my-profile PATCH tests, widen-to-both stamping pins, 21+ profile-form tests. User-guide: Session Proposals callout de-Formatted + new "Submitter My Details — one profile, two independent doors" callout.

- **Webinar retime cascade + email reschedule + single-room guard/auto-heal + mobile banners (August 4, 2026, 4 organizer-reported bugs; commit `17450d25`, adversarially reviewed in-band — HIGHs + all MEDs + cheap LOWs shipped)** — **(1) Retime moves Zoom AND the reminder emails.** The one choke point [session-service.updateSession()](src/services/session-service.ts) already synced Zoom on a retime (`zoomSync`); it now ALSO reschedules the 4-phase auto email sequence when the retimed session is the webinar ANCHOR (`sequenceSync: "rescheduled" | "failed"` threaded through REST/MCP/dashboard toasts) — before this, reminder/live-now emails kept firing on the ORIGINAL schedule because the `ScheduledEmail` fire times were computed once at provisioning. New `rescheduleWebinarSequenceForEvent()` in [webinar-email-sequence.ts](src/lib/webinar-email-sequence.ts): clear + force re-enqueue at the anchor's CURRENT times, atomically inside one `tenantTransaction` holding a per-event **`pg_advisory_xact_lock`** (pooler-safe — session-scoped advisory locks are NOT safe through pgbouncer transaction mode, the P3 lesson; also serializes concurrent retimes so duplicate phase rows can't mint — `ScheduledEmail` has no unique on (eventId, emailType)). Semantics pinned by 9 new tests: SENT/PROCESSING phases never re-created (no double reminders), operator-CANCELLED phases stay cancelled (only the console's explicit Re-enqueue passes `resurrectCancelled` — which also fixed the console button silently no-op'ing when ANY phase had fired), FAILED-with-partial-deliveries keeps its resume row, manually-composed rows never touched. **(2) Event Settings date change cascades.** A WEBINAR event's Settings → General date/timezone change that moves the start instant now pre-validates the anchor fits the new window (400 `ANCHOR_OUTSIDE_NEW_DATES`, checked BEFORE the event save so the M9 out-of-range exemption can't diverge from a failed cascade), then retimes the anchor through the same service call — Zoom + emails move together; the response's `webinarTimeCascade` drives an exact Settings toast ("moved" / "zoom failed — retry from Agenda" / "could NOT be moved"). **(3) One webinar = one room.** Creating a Zoom meeting on a NON-anchor session of a webinar event is refused (409 `WEBINAR_ANCHOR_ONLY` + anchorSessionId) at BOTH doors — REST sessions/[id]/zoom POST + MCP `create_zoom_meeting` — via the shared `webinarSecondRoomViolation()` guard in [webinar.ts](src/lib/webinar.ts) (the organizer-hit bug: a new session minted a second billable webinar attendees couldn't see). Stale links self-heal: the public session detail API returns `redirectToSessionId` for non-anchor sessions (org staff exempt) and the page redirects to the room. [webinar-provisioner.ts](src/lib/webinar-provisioner.ts) re-run with an anchor missing its ZoomMeeting now RE-ATTACHES under the provisioning sentinel (P2002 on the row-create = benign lost race vs transient failure — discriminated via `Prisma.PrismaClientKnownRequestError`, remote webinar torn down either way). **(4) Mobile banners full-width.** The art-directed mobile banner (`bannerImageMobile`) now renders at natural aspect (`block w-full h-auto` — was letterboxed by `max-h-[240px] object-contain` or cropped by fixed-height `object-cover`) on login/forgot/reset/complete-registration/my-registration/presenter-agreement/speaker-agreement/rsvp/confirmation + submitter-register, and the **webinar session page + waiting room** finally use it (session hero + a new `posterMobileUrl` on [waiting-room.tsx](src/components/webinar/waiting-room.tsx) via `<picture>`). +~50 tests across 6 suites; deferred LOWs in ROADMAP §"Webinar retime / anchor round". Docs: WEBINAR_EVENTS.md "Retime cascade" + "Single-room guard" sections, user-guide §11 callouts.

- **Replies go to the Email Branding sender — NO Reply-To anywhere (August 4, 2026, owner rule; commit `cf0fa7c5`)** — Owner decision iterated to its final form: "replyto should be the same org email send address for all cases." All three Reply-To override sites (speaker single-send route, presenter-agreement route, [bulk-email.ts](src/lib/bulk-email.ts)) were REMOVED — per RFC default, replies simply go to the **From** address, which is the per-event Email Branding sender (`Event.emailFromAddress`) or the env default. Comments at the three former sites pin the rule so it isn't re-added piecemeal. Consequence for operators: the Email Branding sender must be a monitored mailbox (user-guide §9 callout). Also in the commit: the speakers table Organization column capped (`w-48 max-w-48` + truncate/title). **This supersedes the "separate speaker-communications sender" feature request — not built.**

- **Resend abstract-submission confirmation — per-abstract, from the speaker surfaces, with real-data preview (August 4, 2026, organizer request; commits `439aed98` + `c92f0225`)** — The confirmation email was fire-and-forget on submit; a bounced/lost send left the submitter with nothing and the organizer with no recovery. **(1) ONE send implementation**: new `sendAbstractSubmissionConfirmation()` in [abstract-notifications.ts](src/lib/abstract-notifications.ts) backs the create POST, the resubmit PUT, and the new manual resend — extracting it **fixed a live drift bug**: the resubmit PUT's inline copy silently dropped `presentationType`/`theme`/`authorName`/`coAuthorNames`, so those tokens rendered blank on every resubmission email. **(2) Resend route** `POST .../abstracts/[abstractId]/resend-confirmation` (reviewer resend-invitation pattern): organizer-only, 30/hr, refuses DRAFT/WITHDRAWN (`NOT_RESENDABLE` — no confirmation exists / would mislead), surfaces send failure as **502** `EMAIL_SEND_FAILED`, audited `EMAIL_SENT` + the same EmailLog slug as auto sends (shows in Email History + Activity); manual resends render the sender's saved `{{organizerSignature}}` (auto sends stay empty, July-16 rule). **(3) Surfaces**: speaker page + detail sheet Abstracts rows show the A-### serial + a per-row Resend button, AND the **Send Email dropdown gained "Abstract Confirmation"** (shown when resendable abstracts exist) with an abstract picker + **Preview**. **(4) Honest preview**: the email-preview route accepts `abstractId` (event-bound, 404 foreign) and overlays THAT abstract's real number/title/theme/type/co-authors via the same exported `buildAbstractConfirmationVars()` the send uses — preview == send by construction. +23 tests (RBAC matrix against real guards, resendability truth table, signature threading, preview overlay).

Warn-not-block (owner-shaped: desk corrections must stay possible). **(4) Speakers table "Reg #" column** — list GET includes `sourceRegistration.serialId` (serialId is NOT a credential — qrCode is never selected there) rendered as the first column via `formatSerialId`; "—" = no companion yet (Grant registration mints one). +2 serial-helper test files (upsert-shape pin + format cases) + delete-warn route pin + factory updates (`tenantTransaction: (fn) => fn(mockDb)` in abstract/proposal suites). - **Per-tenant API keys — Stripe + AI (Anthropic/OpenAI) with per-org Help-Chat provider choice (August 4, 2026, Platform decision item 7; commits `14173797..96d9436e`, 6 phases)** — Every org can now bring its **own** Stripe and AI keys, stored AES-256-GCM-encrypted in `Organization.settings.{stripe,anthropic,openai,ai}` (the Zoom/EventsAir pattern; NO schema migration), with the fallback chain **org key → env var** everywhere — master with nothing configured is byte-identical (pinned by test: an org without a key gets the IDENTICAL env client instance, so every historical PaymentIntent stays on the same account). **Stripe:** [src/lib/stripe.ts](src/lib/stripe.ts) `getStripe(organizationId?)` is now **async** (org key decrypt → env; bounded 5-min-TTL client cache + `invalidateStripeClientCache()` called from the creds PUT/DELETE — the Zoom never-invalidated-cache gotcha, avoided); all 9 SDK call sites pass their org (checkout, webhook PI/charge reads, payment-service refunds, `findStripeRefundForAttempt` gained an org param, checkout-session-cleanup; the backfill CLI stays env-only). **Webhooks = two entry points, ONE dispatcher:** the 580-line event-dispatch body moved VERBATIM to [src/lib/stripe-webhook-handler.ts](src/lib/stripe-webhook-handler.ts) `handleStripeEvent()`; the legacy `/api/webhooks/stripe` (env secret, master) and the new **`/api/webhooks/stripe/[orgId]`** (verifies against the org's encrypted `webhookSecret`; unknown-org and unconfigured return the same generic 400 — no existence oracle; metadata org mismatch warn-logs, never rejects) both delegate to it — drift structurally impossible. The publishable key proved to be **dead code** (checkout is a server-created session redirect; no Stripe.js client-side) so only secret key + webhook secret went per-org. **Direct per-tenant keys, NOT Stripe Connect** (owner decision; Connect noted as possible later evolution). **AI:** new `openai` dep + [src/lib/ai/openai.ts](src/lib/ai/openai.ts) implementing `AiProvider` (system blocks joined into one system message — OpenAI prompt-caches automatically; `include_usage` chunk → done.usage; `max_completion_tokens`); [anthropic.ts](src/lib/ai/anthropic.ts)'s singleton became the same bounded key-keyed Map (cache key IS the credential → no invalidation hook needed); `StreamChatOptions.apiKey` (server-resolved only), `getAiProvider(name)`, per-provider `getModelConfig` (OpenAI default `gpt-4o`, `HELP_CHAT_MODEL_OPENAI` override). New [src/lib/ai/credentials.ts](src/lib/ai/credentials.ts): `aiConfigFromSettings()` (pure — help-chat piggybacks its existing org lookup, ZERO new queries; a provider preference with no usable key degrades to anthropic+env with a warn, never bricks help chat; org-null roles → anthropic+env by construction) + `resolveAnthropicApiKey()` for the **Event Agent, which stays Anthropic-only this round** (tool loop + `web_search_20250305` are Anthropic-specific; a tenant's own key needs web search enabled in THAT Anthropic Console — degrades, doesn't block; porting the agent to OpenAI is a recorded follow-up in HELP_CHATBOT.md §17). **Routes** (cloned from the zoom credentials template — ADMIN|SUPER_ADMIN, 10/hr limits, every failure path logs, GET returns booleans + plain last4/keyMode, NEVER ciphertext): `/api/organization/stripe/credentials` (first-time requires the secret key; blank keeps existing; GET returns the org's webhook URL) + `stripe/test-connection` (probes `accounts.retrieve()` through the EFFECTIVE `getStripe(orgId)` chain, reports `source: org|env` so a broken org key can't hide behind a working env fallback); `/api/organization/ai/credentials` (both providers + the `helpChatProvider` preference in ONE family — selecting a provider validates a key resolves for it; DELETE clears one provider and resets a dangling preference) + `ai/test-connection` (free `models.list` probes). **UI:** Settings → Integrations gains **Stripe Payments** (masked inputs, Live/Test badge, webhook URL + copy button + Stripe-Dashboard event instructions, account-switch caution: old PIs refund only from the old account — deliberately NO silent env-key retry) and **AI Assistant** (provider Select + both keys with per-provider Test) cards, modeled on `OrgZoomCredentials`; hooks mirror the zoom section in [use-api.ts](src/hooks/use-api.ts). **Browser-verified on local:** cards render, Anthropic test-connection succeeded live (`source: "env"`), OpenAI key save → ciphertext at rest + masked `••••last4 (saved)` + badge, delete cleans the sub-key, Stripe test surfaces the honest no-key error. +56 tests (accessor chain incl. the identical-env-client existing-data guarantee / TTL / invalidation; per-org webhook route; AI credentials truth table incl. misconfigured-preference fallback; OpenAI adapter; credentials routes RBAC/masking/blank-keeps/429/DELETE) — the existing 27-test webhook suite passes UNCHANGED through the extraction (the money-path regression net). Full gate: tsc 0 · eslint 0 · vitest 4453 · build green. Docs: PAYMENT_FLOW.md (per-org keys + two-endpoint webhook section), HELP_CHATBOT.md §17 (OpenAI provider delivered), PLATFORM_DECISIONS.md §7 flipped to IMPLEMENTED. **Owner action flagged:** `.env.example` (untracked) appears to carry a REAL `sk-ant` key — rotate in the Anthropic Console + replace with a placeholder. - **Infra dashboard "Error rate" + "Abuse & auth" cards actually measure things now (August 4, 2026, owner-reported "they say 0 ALWAYS")** — Both `/admin/infra` cards read the `SystemLog` table, which on EC2 (actual prod) was **never written**: the logger's DB stream was Vercel-branch-only, so the error-trend chart and all three abuse counters were structurally zero forever. Fix: (1) the EC2/Docker logger branch now also persists **warn+error** to `SystemLog` (info stays file/stdout-only — no volume flood; both web + worker containers write, so worker errors finally surface on the dashboard); (2) new **`system-log-prune`** worker job (JOB_ID 1014, 04:45 UTC daily, [system-log-prune-worker.ts](src/lib/system-log-prune-worker.ts)) deletes rows past **30 days** — batched select-then-delete, per-tick capped with a loud `capped:true`, quiet no-op; the worker-jobs drift guard caught the unregistered job exactly as designed; (3) `fetchAbuse`'s substrings re-keyed to the REAL log taxonomy — it counted "invalid-credentials"/"forbidden", strings our messages never contain; now `rate-limited`, the three `auth:login-*` failure messages, and `-denied`/`-refused`/`forbidden` (the actual 403 suffixes). Data starts at deploy (nothing historical to backfill — the table was empty). **Needs a worker redeploy for the prune job.** +6 tests (5 prune-sweep pins + the roster entry).
- **Self-service check-in kiosk — attendee scans their emailed barcode, badge prints automatically via Chrome kiosk-printing (August 3, 2026, organizer request)** — New full-screen attendee-facing station at [/events/[eventId]/check-in/kiosk](src/app/(dashboard)/events/[eventId]/check-in/kiosk/page.tsx) (opened via a **Kiosk mode** button on the staff Check-In page): the attendee scans the barcode from their confirmation email (printed-badge `{qrCode}-{serial}` and DTCM UUID forms also work — same candidate matching), the page calls the EXISTING check-in PUT then fetches their single badge PDF (`POST .../badges {registrationIds:[id]}`) into a hidden iframe and calls `print()` — under `chrome --kiosk --kiosk-printing` that prints **silently to the default printer** (badge printer = machine default). **Zero new auth surface (owner decision):** the kiosk Chrome is signed into an **ONSITE** account, so the per-event assignment scoping, rate limits and audit attribution of the desk APIs apply unchanged; middleware already allows `check-in/*` for ONSITE. **Owner decisions:** already-checked-in scans **reprint the badge** (lost-badge self-service; "You're already checked in — printing your badge again"); payment-pending / cancelled / unknown codes show "Please visit the registration desk" — the kiosk **never** overrides the payment gate (overrides stay a deliberate audited desk action). Kiosk scans send `kiosk: true` which the PUT folds into the CHECK_IN audit row + the qr-rejected/unknown-code warn logs (non-boolean values not trusted). UX: keyboard-wedge hidden input with focus guards (incl. a forced blur→focus **frame-focus reclaim** — Chrome's PDF viewer steals browser-level frame focus from the print iframe and a plain `focus()` on an already-active element is a no-op), beeps via the new shared [src/lib/scan-feedback.ts](src/lib/scan-feedback.ts), auto-reset (8s success / 10s denied), iframe print fail-safe (never wedges), and **`--kiosk-printing` dialog detection** (print() blocking >1.5s ⇒ the flag is missing ⇒ on-screen staff note — without the flag the dialog modally eats every keystroke, proven in browser testing). **Adversarial review same day (0 BLOCKER / 3 HIGH / 4 MED / 7 LOW) — H1/H2/H3 + M1/M2/M3/M4 + L1/L2 all shipped in-band**: H1 the staff exit is **PIN-gated** (5 taps on an invisible corner target → on-screen PIN pad; PIN is MACHINE-LOCAL via [src/lib/kiosk-exit-pin.ts](src/lib/kiosk-exit-pin.ts) localStorage, set in the Kiosk-mode launch dialog — device lock, not event data, and ONSITE can't write event settings; no PIN ⇒ exit only by closing the window); H2 `printBadge` never throws, so a badge-fetch network error after a COMMITTED check-in shows the honest "checked in, badge didn't print" instead of "you were NOT checked in"; H3 401/403 → a persistent red "Kiosk needs attention" state (the 24h JWT WILL expire on day 2 — every attendee would otherwise be told their code is bad) and 429/5xx → "system busy, try again"; M1 input cleared on every early-return (debounce residue can't concatenate into the next scan); M2 busy-window scans beep instead of vanishing; M3 reprints soft-capped 3/registration/hour (kiosk-local); M4 a route test pins the ALREADY_CHECKED_IN 400 body shape (code + registration + checkedInAt) the reprint path depends on. Deferred L3–L7 + the M3 durable-cap residual in ROADMAP §"Self-service check-in kiosk review". +4 route tests. User-guide §12 gains the full kiosk-machine setup runbook (default printer, ONSITE sign-in, exit PIN, the exact `--kiosk --kiosk-printing` launch command + the dialog-detection symptom).
- **Webinar feedback batch — lobby image + non-interactive holding video with unmute + real Add-to-Calendar + mobile banners on session/confirmation (August 3, 2026, organizer feedback, 6 items)** — **(1)** Sponsor dialog button "Add to draft/Update draft" → "Add/Update". **(2) Custom waiting-room image**: new `settings.webinar.lobbyImageUrl` (JSON, no migration) with a PhotoUpload in the console's Lobby card; poster priority in [waiting-room.tsx](src/components/webinar/waiting-room.tsx) is lobby image → event banner → gradient, threaded through the webinar PUT Zod + `lobby-status` public API + session page. **(3) Holding video is fully NON-interactive**: the YouTube/Vimeo iframe is `pointer-events-none` (no pause, no title bar, no "more videos", no copy link) + `disablekb/fs=0/iv_load_policy=3` on the embed URL ([lobby-video.ts](src/lib/webinar/lobby-video.ts)). **(4) Audio via OUR one button**: browsers only allow muted autoplay, so a single overlaid Unmute/Mute control drives the player over postMessage (YouTube `enablejsapi=1` command envelope; Vimeo setMuted/setVolume). **(5) Real Add to Calendar** — key finding: EA-SYS had NO calendar feature; the "wrong date/time" chips were Gmail/Outlook auto-parsing the email's Date:/Time: text. New pure [src/lib/calendar-links.ts](src/lib/calendar-links.ts) (Google/Outlook URLs + RFC 5545 ICS, **all times UTC-encoded — timezone-proof by construction**); the confirmation page shows Google/Outlook/.ics buttons for webinars (times from the **anchor session** via a new `webinarSession` field on the public event API — the session is the authoritative clock after a console retime; conferences keep the plain tip since date-only startDate would render a misleading midnight); the webinar-confirmation email gains a `{{calendarBlock}}` token (in DEFAULT_RAW_HTML_KEYS + preview samples — drift test green) **and attaches `invite.ics`**, which gives mail clients an authoritative event to chip, overriding their own parsing (`buildWebinarCalendarEnrichment` in [bulk-email.ts](src/lib/bulk-email.ts), built once per send, attached per recipient on webinar-confirmation only). **(6) Mobile banners**: session/live page + confirmation page converted to the art-directed `EventBanner` (`bannerImageMobile` added to the session detail API select) — these were on the July 7 deferred list, which is why the mobile banner showed on sign-in but not there; survey/agreement pages remain deferred. +12 tests ([lobby-video-and-calendar-links.test.ts](__tests__/lib/lobby-video-and-calendar-links.test.ts) — embed param pins incl. enablejsapi, UTC stamps, ICS escaping/CRLF) — suite 4337.

- **Email history records attachment filenames — "payment received" now shows the invoice + receipt went out (August 3, 2026, organizer request)** — The post-payment fan-out (`issuePaidRegistrationDocuments`) sends ONE combined "Payment Confirmation" email carrying BOTH the paid-invoice and receipt PDFs, but `EmailLog` had no attachment fields — so the Activity/Email-History row gave no hint the documents were delivered, reading as if they were never sent. New **`EmailLog.attachmentNames String[] @default([])`** (additive+idempotent migration `20260803120000_add_email_log_attachment_names`) — **names only, never the bytes** (documents stay re-downloadable from their own surfaces; the email-log-prune job is untouched since names are tiny and kept with the row). **Captured at the ONE choke point**: `sendEmail` in [email.ts](src/lib/email.ts) maps `params.attachments` to filenames and passes them to all 3 `logEmail` sites (success / failure / circuit-open) — so EVERY sender is covered with zero per-caller wiring (payment invoice+receipt, registration-confirmation quote PDFs, speaker agreement .docx/PDF, certificates, bulk manual attachments), and a FAILED row still records what it TRIED to attach. **Rendered with a 📎 on all three read surfaces**: the per-person Email History card ([email-log-card.tsx](src/components/communications/email-log-card.tsx)), the registration/speaker Activity timeline ([activity-feed.ts](src/lib/activity-feed.ts) → [activity-timeline-card.tsx](src/components/activity/activity-timeline-card.tsx)), and the Communications Email Activity table ([email-activity-card.tsx](src/components/communications/email-activity-card.tsx) + its route select). **Not backfillable** — rows logged before this deploy never recorded the list (documented in the schema comment + user-guide §9 callout). +9 tests ([email-send-attachment-log.test.ts](__tests__/lib/email-send-attachment-log.test.ts) SENT/FAILED/empty passthrough with a mocked SES client + [email-log.test.ts](__tests__/lib/email-log.test.ts) persist/default/select) — suite 4330. Verified in the browser on local: a payment-confirmation row shows "INV-….pdf, REC-….pdf" in the Activity tab AND the Email Activity table.

- **DTCM QR on the badge + scannable DTCM preview on the detail sheet (August 3, 2026, organizer request)** — Until now the DTCM compliance barcode (externally-issued 36-char UUIDs, CSV-imported via Import Barcodes or hand-entered) lived only in the database — the printed badge carried ONLY the entry Code 128, so a DTCM inspector had nothing to scan. Now, on events flagged `requiresDtcmBarcode`, [the badge route](src/app/api/events/%5BeventId%5D/registrations/badges/route.ts) prints a **DTCM QR** in the badge's previously-unused bottom band (~y+172, QR right + bold "DTCM" label + the UUID in 5pt Courier left for manual verification) — **QR, not Code 128, by design**: the UUID needs ~430 Code 128 modules (~0.19mm bars at badge width — unscannable in print) while a 14mm QR holds it comfortably; new `renderQrPng()` in [src/lib/barcode.ts](src/lib/barcode.ts) (bwip-js `qrcode`, eclevel M, no new dep). **Nothing above the band moves** — non-DTCM events and rows without a code print byte-identical badges (badgeVerticalOffset calibration untouched); the flag gate is structural (flag off ⇒ the QR buffer map stays empty, so a stale value can never render). DTCM values join the bounded-concurrency pre-render pool in their own dedup map (`badges:dtcm-qr-render-failed` warn with a TRUNCATED value on a bad render — badge omits the QR, print never fails); the `BADGE_PRINTED` audit row gains **`dtcmQrCount`** and a `badges:dtcm-rendered` info line reports badges-with vs missing codes. **Check-in already accepted both codes** (`qrCode IN candidates OR dtcmBarcode = scanned`; the UUID doesn't match the serial-suffix regex so passes exactly) — verified live: scanning the sample UUID checked the right person in; +1 candidate-passthrough test pins it. **Detail sheet**: the DTCM tile now shows a scannable QR image via the barcode PNG route's new **`?code=dtcm`** param (404 `dtcm-not-flagged` / `dtcm-not-set`, both warn-logged), and the stale comment claiming that route "falls back to dtcmBarcode" was corrected (it never did). **In-band security fix**: that PNG route had NO `canViewEntryBarcode` gate — a MEMBER (or event-linked REGISTRANT) could fetch the barcode PNG directly even though the JSON payloads strip the value; now 403 + `registration-barcode:role-refused` warn, matching the July-11 barcode boundary. +9 tests ([dtcm-badge-and-barcode.test.ts](__tests__/api/dtcm-badge-and-barcode.test.ts): per-unique-value render + dedup, flag-off zero renders + audit 0, MEMBER 403, both dtcm 404s logged, entry path unchanged) — suite 4324. Verified end-to-end on local: real badge PDF rendered with the sample UUID (layout confirmed), detail-sheet QR renders, DTCM scan checks in. User-guide §12 badge-printing callout added.

- **Saved templates sendable from the per-speaker email dialog (July 31, 2026, organizer-reported gap)** — The June 16 "active custom templates are sendable" feature only reached the BULK pipeline; the single-send speaker dialog (speaker page + detail sheet) offered just the hardcoded Invitation/Agreement/Custom trio and its route's Zod was equally closed — so an organizer emailing ONE speaker never saw their saved templates. Now: [the single-send route](src/app/api/events/%5BeventId%5D/speakers/%5BspeakerId%5D/email/route.ts) accepts **`type: "template"` + `templateSlug`** — resolved via `getEventTemplate` (active-only), so a deactivated/deleted custom template **hard-400s `TEMPLATE_NOT_AVAILABLE`** (never a silent fallback to a different email — bulk semantics); system slugs keep their default fallback; the EmailLog + audit row carry the **actual slug** (Email History shows which template went). Both dialogs gained a **"Send Saved Template"** dropdown entry + an active-custom-templates picker (`isCustomTemplateSlug` filter over `useEmailTemplates` — note the hook returns `{ templates, variables }`, not a bare array; the browser check caught that), with Preview via the existing `/email-preview` + `speakerId` so it renders THIS speaker's blocks. All speaker-context machinery (presentation/moderation blocks, `{{agreementBlock}}` on-demand link mint, agreement attachment, signature) applies to template sends automatically since it runs for every type. +4 route tests ([speaker-email-template-send.test.ts](__tests__/api/speaker-email-template-send.test.ts)); verified in the browser (picker → preview renders the saved template with the real speaker + event).

- **Session Proposals v1 — abstracts-shaped submissions for proposing SESSIONS, organizer inbox only (July 30, 2026)** — Owner request: "like abstract submission but for session proposals — its own themes, no reviewer, no accepted/rejected (maybe later)." Plan + all 4 owner decisions locked in [docs/SESSION_PROPOSALS_PLAN.md](docs/SESSION_PROPOSALS_PLAN.md): **account-based access** (the existing SUBMITTER registration — one login covers abstracts + proposals), organizer side is **list/view/export only** (no review, no convert-to-session — both recorded as v2 room), **core fields only** (title, description Text, theme, `proposedFormat SessionType?` restricted to PROGRAM kinds via `SESSION_TYPE_KIND` so a future convert-to-session pre-fill is free, durationMinutes). **Deliberately a SEPARATE model family** (no kind-discriminator on Abstract — proposals must not inherit the review machinery): `SessionProposal` + `SessionProposalTheme` (mirrors AbstractTheme, `@@unique([eventId, name])`) + `SessionProposalStatus` enum (DRAFT/SUBMITTED/WITHDRAWN; UNDER_REVIEW/ACCEPTED/REJECTED are additive v2 room), both **born multi-tenant-ready** with a denormalized nullable `organizationId` stamped from the EVENT at create (LoginEvent convention; app-level org scoping = defence #1, no `runWithTenant` until the program-domain sweep). Migration `20260730150000` additive+idempotent, verified exact via `prisma migrate diff`. **RBAC mirrors abstracts with one improvement:** routes use the modern `denyReviewer(session, { allow: ["SUBMITTER"] })` form; submitter own-rows-only (404 on foreign, no existence leak), **edits only while DRAFT** (`SUBMITTED_LOCKED` 403), birth status DRAFT|SUBMITTED only (the abstracts-H2 lesson), DRAFTs invisible to organizers; the **themes GET authorizes via `buildEventAccessWhere`** (org staff OR linked submitter) instead of abstract-themes' `requireOrgId` — org-null submitters can actually read the form's theme picker (the abstracts equivalent is a noted latent gap, not fixed here). A bad `?status=` filter 400s `INVALID_FILTER` (never silently widens); `?export=csv` is org-staff-only (narrower than read) + `recordExport`-audited. **Surfaces:** dual-mode [/events/[eventId]/session-proposals](src/app/(dashboard)/events/[eventId]/session-proposals/page.tsx) (organizer: status tiles, theme/status filters, search, CSV, detail sheet with Withdraw/Reinstate/Delete, Themes manager dialog; submitter: "My Session Proposals" + submit CTA) + full-page [new](src/app/(dashboard)/events/[eventId]/session-proposals/new/page.tsx) form that doubles as the DRAFT edit surface via `?edit=` (staff get a proposer picker; submitters auto-bind to their own Speaker); sidebar entry in the Abstracts group (in the restricted-role allow-list + `WEBINAR_HIDDEN_MODULES`); middleware allow-list extended `abstracts*` → `+ session-proposals*`. **Emails:** shared [session-proposal-notify.ts](src/lib/session-proposal-notify.ts) (ONE fan-out for POST-create + PUT-resubmit — never-throws, fire-and-forget: proposer confirmation via the new editable **`session-proposal-confirmation`** system template + `notifyEventAdmins`; DRAFT saves are silent). **Deliberately NOT built** (plan §6): review workflow, convert-to-session, proposed-speakers block, MCP tools (fast-follow), dedicated public register page, theme filter parity. +20 route tests ([session-proposals-routes.test.ts](__tests__/api/session-proposals-routes.test.ts) — real `denyReviewer` + real `buildEventAccessWhere`; own-speaker binding, org-key stamping, SUBMITTED_LOCKED, draft invisibility, program-format refusal, export RBAC + audit, themes submitter-read/staff-write) — suite 4249 → 4269. tsc/eslint/vitest/build green; user-guide §7 callout added.

Written **fire-and-forget** on SSE stream completion in [POST /api/help-chat](src/app/api/help-chat/route.ts) so a write failure can never break the chat; read ONLY by SUPER_ADMIN via [GET /api/help-chat/queries](src/app/api/help-chat/queries/route.ts) (403 for anyone else incl. Migration `20260729120000_add_help_chat_query` additive+idempotent. +7 route tests (RBAC 401/403/200, escaping, paging). - **Multi-tenancy Phase 2 — Ticketing follow-on (Domain #8 carve-off) (July 30, 2026, commits: schema `4629581f` / C1+C2+C3+C4)** — Closes the seat/promo-counter RLS-backstop gap Domain #8 deferred. The **registrant promo-apply route stays unwrapped** (identity class, same as Domain #8). **C3** — [prisma/rls/ticketing.sql](prisma/rls/ticketing.sql) (5 flat policies) + an 11-assertion [ticketing-rls.test.ts](tests/tenancy/ticketing-rls.test.ts): per-lane scoping, 2-hop PricingTier lane-scoping, the SHARED promo-code string (both orgs hold `TENANCY10`, `@@unique([eventId, code])` lets them coexist) lane-scoped, fail-closed across all 5, WITH CHECK smuggle + org-re-home blocks, cross-tenant DELETE P2025, defence-#1-in-isolation on `{ id, eventId }`. Harness **174 → 185**. **C4** — [check-tenant-als.sh](scripts/check-tenant-als.sh) gained the 6 route files + `agent/tools/promo-codes.ts`; 3 route-test mocks updated (`tenantTransaction` passthrough on clone + promo-codes, `event.findUnique` on speaker-companion). - **BCC + "send me a copy" on speaker emails — single-send AND bulk (July 29, 2026, commit `929db6c6`, organizer request)** — CRM-email-dialog parity for the event side. Both single-send speaker dialogs (speaker page + detail sheet) and the shared bulk dialog gained a **BCC** field (comma-separated, client+server validated, max 10) and a **"Send me a copy (BCC)" checkbox, default ON** — so invitations land in the organizer's own inbox. **Mechanics:** the single-send route ([speakers/[speakerId]/email](src/app/api/events/%5BeventId%5D/speakers/%5BspeakerId%5D/email/route.ts)) merges manual bcc + the session user's address, dedupes, and never BCCs the speaker on their own email; for bulk, `filters.bcc` + `filters.bccSelf` ride INSIDE the filters JSON (the `surveyExpiryDays` schedule-compat pattern) so **scheduled sends reconstruct them from the persisted `ScheduledEmail.filters` with no new column and no worker change** — `bccSelf` resolves to `organizerEmail` at SEND time in [executeBulkEmail](src/lib/bulk-email.ts), and each recipient's own address is excluded per email (a bulk send BCCs the sender once PER recipient — stated in the dialog). Transport already supported bcc on all three providers and `EmailLog` records it, so Email History shows BCC automatically. MCP `send_bulk_email` deliberately unchanged. +7 tests ([bulk-email-bcc.test.ts](__tests__/lib/bulk-email-bcc.test.ts)) — suite 4239.

- **INC-004: 27 prod photo files destroyed by delete-time cleanup — root-caused, restored, guarded (July 24 incident, resolved July 29, 2026, commit `425a8bd4`)** — Organizer reported a speaker photo 404ing; forensics found **27 photo files deleted from the box on July 24 ~12:45 UTC** while surviving rows still pointed at them. **Root cause:** since March 2026 the speaker/registration/contact DELETE routes unlinked the row's photo FILE — but photo PATHS are shared by design (`syncToContact` + every import flow copies the same `/uploads/photos/...` string across rows), so a bulk cleanup of one import batch destroyed files its SIBLING rows still referenced. **Recovery:** every file was in the Singapore DR mirror (hourly, NON-deleting — the property that made this recoverable; never add `--delete` to that sync); restored via reverse `aws s3 sync` + ownership fix (the uploads tree is uid-1001/ssm-user owned — the container's write uid — so a `sudo -u ubuntu` sync gets EACCES). **Durable fix:** new [src/lib/photo-cleanup.ts](src/lib/photo-cleanup.ts) `deletePhotoIfUnreferenced()` — all three DELETE routes now count remaining references across Attendee + Speaker + Contact (the schema's three `photo` columns) and unlink only at zero; never throws; fail-safe direction (a DB blip skips the unlink — an orphan is cheap, a destroyed shared file is data loss). Full post-mortem [docs/INCIDENTS.md](docs/INCIDENTS.md) INC-004 (diagnosis trail incl. the DR-has-it-but-box-doesn't proof). **Rule: a file referenced by copied paths is shared state — no delete-time unlink until the last reference is gone.** Photo-redundancy follow-ups discussed + parked (serve-time S3 fallback + self-heal recommended over a Supabase dual-write; revisit later). +6 tests.

- **Multi-tenancy Phase 2 — Registration-core full sweep (Domain #8) — the biggest domain (July 28–29, 2026, commits `c56053a4` schema / `50c11db5` C1 / `c6271c67`+`d9929746` C2 / C3+C4)** — Second sweep from the "25 tables without an org column" set, scoped to the 5 core tables **Registration, Attendee, Payment, RefundAttempt, RegistrationSerialCounter** (TicketType/PricingTier/PromoCode deliberately carved off as a bounded follow-on — owner decision — since their seat/promo counters are id-guarded + RLS-backstopped). **Schema:** migration `20260728160000` adds a nullable denormalized `organizationId` (scalar + index, no FK) to all 5, backfilled 1/2-hop from Event. **Attendee is the hard case** — it has NO event link and no unique email, and the public-register orphan-reuse path can (a) adopt + **overwrite another org's orphaned attendee PII** and (b) under concurrency mint one row backing registrations in two orgs; so it's backfilled ONLY where all its registrations agree on one org (`COUNT(DISTINCT)=1`), orphans/conflicted stay NULL (fail-closed under RLS), and the reuse lookup is now **org-bound** (kills the PII-overwrite; a NULL-org orphan simply mints a fresh row). **RegistrationSerialCounter got a flat org column specifically** because its `INSERT…ON CONFLICT` upsert against a policy-invisible row would raise a unique violation the app misreads as "already registered" — the exact bug the counter was built to fix; the flat column sidesteps it. registration-service optimistic-lock write, and the DTCM barcode pre-check (was probing the **global** `dtcmBarcode` namespace — a cross-org existence leak) + write. **C2** — `runWithTenant` on ~28 ([certificates/auto-issue.ts](src/lib/certificates/auto-issue.ts), [refund-reconciliation.ts](src/lib/refund-reconciliation.ts), [checkout-session-cleanup.ts](src/lib/checkout-session-cleanup.ts) — org read off the row, NULL rows run unwrapped preserving master behavior). **The 7 `/api/registrant/**` self-service routes + the sign-in email auto-link sweeps are deliberately NOT wrapped** — WITH CHECK smuggle + org-re-home blocks, cross-tenant DELETE P2025, and defence-#1-in-isolation on the eventId-bound `updateMany` shape. Harness **157 → 168**. **C4** — [check-tenant-als.sh](scripts/check-tenant-als.sh) gained ~28 route files + 4 modules (verified both ways: green on HEAD, a dropped wrap fails naming the file). **Identity note (the recurring "how does a person span tenants" question):** the *rows* are org-bound (a registration belongs to an event → org); the *login account* (`User`, org-null for REGISTRANT/REVIEWER/SUBMITTER) is the one seam that spans orgs — deferred to the Phase-1 shared-`User`+`Membership` decision, and under the two-silo topology master + platform are separate DBs so a person at both literally has two accounts. - **Multi-tenancy Phase 2 — Webinar/Zoom full sweep (Domain #6) + zoom-route IDOR fixes (July 28, 2026, commits `8b488c8e` schema / `6630c72e` C1 / `6e54bf5e` C2 / C3+C4)** — The first sweep whose tables did NOT carry `organizationId`, and the first multi-table domain policy file. **Schema:** migration `20260728140000` adds a nullable denormalized `organizationId` (scalar + `@@index`, deliberately no FK) to all 6 webinar tables (`ZoomMeeting`, `ZoomAttendance`, `WebinarPresence`, `WebinarPoll`, `WebinarPollResponse`, `WebinarQuestion`), backfilled from Event in 1/2/3-hop join order — ratifying IMPACT §8.2's "columns over join-policies"; additive + idempotent + blue-green safe (nullable stays: writers stamp from this deploy on, and the 3 sync state machines **re-stamp on their update paths** so a blue-green-window NULL self-heals next tick); verified by a local replay-from-empty + `prisma migrate diff` (no difference). **C1** — every create stamps the tenant key (routes, provisioner, MCP `create_zoom_meeting`, engagement/attendance upserts, docs seed); the engagement poll find-or-create `$transaction` → `tenantTransaction` (its nullable-`zoomPollId` serialize semantics unchanged); **4 security findings fixed in-band (owner-picked "fix all")**: (a) **cross-tenant IDOR in `sessions/[sessionId]/zoom` GET/PUT/DELETE + its panelists sibling** — they resolved the ZoomMeeting by `sessionId` alone (never joined to the URL's event), so a caller owning *any* event in their org could read (`startUrl` = the Zoom **host** credential), update, or **delete another org's meeting — DB row AND the remote billable Zoom meeting** — by passing a foreign sessionId; all lookups now bind `{ sessionId, eventId }` and the mutations compound-where (`update/delete({ where: { id, eventId } })`); (b) the **public** `stream-status` route's `updateMany` had no event/org predicate (unauthenticated-reachable streamStatus flip on any row) — now event-bound; (c) `session-service.syncZoomMeetingTimes` compound-where'd `{ id, eventId }`; (d) MCP `list_zoom_meetings` pairs `ctx.eventId` with the org like every sibling executor. Every webinar-route + bulk-email anchor-meeting lookup (`findUnique({ sessionId: anchorSessionId })`) also gained the `eventId` bind so a stale/corrupted `settings.webinar.sessionId` can't reach another org's row. **C2** — **37 `runWithTenant` wraps across 22 files**: the 12 event-nested staff route files, the **5 public session routes** (`presence`/`stream-status`/`zoom-join`/`recording`/`detail` — wrap after the `publicEventWhere` event resolution; the last three read ZoomMeeting via nested selects that would **fail-closed under platform RLS** without a store), the 5 webinar MCP executors, and per-row wraps in the 3 sync fns + provisioner (org read off the row itself; the candidate sweep stays org-blind — the known worker precondition, invoice-reconciliation pattern). Inert on master (flag off = passthrough). **C3** — [prisma/rls/webinar.sql](prisma/rls/webinar.sql) (6 flat policies, one domain file) + 10-assertion [tests/tenancy/webinar-rls.test.ts](tests/tenancy/webinar-rls.test.ts): shared Zoom-meeting-number seeded in BOTH orgs proves per-lane scoping (the MediaFile shared-url pattern), 3-hop `WebinarPollResponse` invisible cross-tenant even addressed by its parent `pollId`, fail-closed across all 6 tables, WITH CHECK smuggle + org-re-home blocks, cross-tenant DELETE P2025, and **defence #1 in isolation** (owner client — the session→event compound-where alone P2025s a wrong-event update). Harness **157/157** green. **Fixture note:** the test seeds its own fixtures in `beforeAll` via the owner connection instead of `prisma/seed-tenancy.ts` — a deliberate one-off because a concurrent session held uncommitted CRM-sweep WIP in `seed-tenancy.ts` + `constants.ts` (the July-24 shared-checkout lesson); fold into the seed when the CRM sweep lands. **C4** — [check-tenant-als.sh](scripts/check-tenant-als.sh) gained 17 `SWEPT_ROUTE_FILES` + 5 `SWEPT_MODULES` entries (verified both ways: green on HEAD, a deliberately-dropped wrap fails with the file named). **Platform-only precondition (unchanged):** MediaMTX is a global singleton — before a second tenant streams an HLS-mode webinar the platform needs per-tenant publish auth or path prefixes (MULTI_TENANCY.md §13 Domain #6). Full gate green per commit: tsc/eslint/vitest 4157/build; migration-replay clean. **Remaining in the queue:** the CRM full-domain sweep (in progress in a concurrent session).

- **Sign-in activity tracking + the login rate limit that was never there (July 28, 2026)** — "who is logged in, timestamp and location". **Nothing recorded a login before this** — not a row, not a log line. `logAuthEvent()` had sat in [logger.ts](src/lib/logger.ts) since the beginning with `"login" | "failed_login"` cases and **zero call sites**; the mobile route wrote a pino line with no IP. **New `LoginEvent` table** (additive+idempotent migration `20260728100000`) — one row per sign-in **attempt**, successful or not: `userId?`/`organizationId?`/`email`/`outcome`/`surface`/`ipAddress`/`userAgent` + lazily-filled `geoCity`/`geoCountry`/`geoResolvedAt`. **Deliberately NOT AuditLog rows** even though its columns fit: failed attempts are an unauthenticated, attacker-controllable write path and would drown the business audit trail `GET /api/activity` reads; AuditLog has no prune job and its rows survive a subject-erasure request; and `entityType`/`entityId` are required and meaningless for an attempt on an address matching no user. `LoginOutcome` keeps **FAILED_UNKNOWN_EMAIL distinct from FAILED_PASSWORD** — together they separate "this account is under attack" from "someone is spraying addresses". Both attribution columns are nullable and null carries meaning: an unknown-email attempt has no org and is therefore invisible in the org-scoped view **by construction** (spray is noise; an attack on a real account resolves to a user and IS shown). **[src/lib/login-audit.ts](src/lib/login-audit.ts) is the ONE writer** for all four doors (dashboard login, event-scoped login, post-abstract-registration auto-sign-in — all three land in `authorize()` — plus the separate bcrypt path in mobile-login); contract is **never throws, never blocks**, so a DB blip can lose a row but can never lock anyone out. **The adjacent finding, fixed: the web login had no rate limit at all.** mobile-login throttled 10/15min per IP; the NextAuth credentials path that every dashboard and event login goes through had none, so passwords were brute-forceable against production unthrottled. New **[src/lib/login-throttle.ts](src/lib/login-throttle.ts)** rather than reusing `checkRateLimit`, because the semantics genuinely differ: `checkRateLimit` consumes on every call, which would **count successes** (a conference behind one venue NAT would lock its own room out) and has **no reset** (two typos then a success should leave a clean slate). So: peek before the attempt, charge only on failure, clear on success. **Per-email 10/15min** does the real work — a real person doesn't fail ten times in a quarter hour, and it catches the distributed case; **per-IP 100/15min** is loose on purpose, only there to stop a single host spraying. A success clears the email bucket but **not** the IP bucket (else an attacker holding one valid account could reset the spray counter between batches). The email bucket is charged for unknown addresses too, so being told you're throttled is **no account-existence oracle**. Throttling now `throw`s `CredentialsSignin` with `code: "RateLimited"` so a locked-out admin is told to wait rather than that their correct password is wrong. In `authorize()` the **user lookup runs first** — a blocked attack on a real account must be attributed to its org or it would be invisible in exactly the view an admin needs; bcrypt still sits behind the throttle. mobile-login also lost its **spoofable IP read** (`x-forwarded-for.split(",")[0]` — the *first*, client-supplied entry, so its limit was bypassable by forging a header) in favour of `getClientIp`. **Location is resolved lazily** ([src/lib/login-geo.ts](src/lib/login-geo.ts)) — never during login, because an outbound call between the password check and session creation makes signing in feel broken and a throwing one fails it outright. Each distinct address costs one lookup ever; the answer is written back keyed on the IP so every row sharing it fills at once, and a *failed* lookup writes nothing so it retries. Private/unroutable and malformed addresses resolve permanently to "no location" without any call. IPs are **shape-validated before being interpolated into the outbound URL** (leading-zero octets rejected — `0177.0.0.1` is octal for `127.0.0.1` in some resolvers). `LOGIN_GEO_ENABLED=false` stops all outbound IP traffic and the view degrades to raw IPs. **Visibility is its own predicate** ([src/lib/login-visibility.ts](src/lib/login-visibility.ts), SUPER_ADMIN + ADMIN, **no API-key path**) — deliberately narrower than every neighbour: `denyReviewer` is a write guard that permits ORGANIZER, `canViewFinance` includes MEMBER and ONSITE, `canExportRegistrations` includes ONSITE. This is security data about colleagues (IP, approximate location, the hours a named person was at their desk), so an organizer running one conference has no business reading it. **UI**: Settings → **Sign-in Activity** tab ([login-activity-card.tsx](src/components/settings/login-activity-card.tsx)) — outcome + window filters, paginated, exhaustive Prisma-enum-keyed badge maps (a new outcome without a presentation fails the build), and an explicit note that IP geolocation resolves to the network, not the person. **Retention**: new `login-event-prune` worker job (JOB_ID 1013, 04:15 UTC daily, offset from email-log-prune's 03:45) **deletes** rows past 180 days — unlike the email prune it doesn't keep a husk, because a sign-in record stripped of address, location and user carries nothing worth storing, and this is personal data that mustn't become a permanent movement log of the team. +106 tests across 5 files (throttle semantics incl. the NAT and no-oracle properties; the SSRF guard and never-throws contract; the writer's never-breaks-sign-in contract; the route's full RBAC matrix with ORGANIZER explicitly refused, org scoping, and geo failure-isolation; prune cutoff + no-silent-cap) — suite **4008 → 4117**. The geo test caught a real bug in my own validator (`String(n) === String(Number(part))` is a tautology, so leading-zero octets passed), and the worker drift guard caught the unregistered job. tsc/eslint/vitest/build green. **Docs:** [docs/LOGIN_ACTIVITY.md](docs/LOGIN_ACTIVITY.md) (architecture + §7 an explicit "what this does NOT do") + user-guide §14 "Sign-in Activity" (operator-facing, picked up by the help chatbot). **Deliberately NOT built** (ROADMAP §"Sign-in activity"): a per-user "your recent sign-ins" block on `/profile` (the half that catches a compromised password early — owner chose admin-only for v1), **any alerting** (nothing is pushed; an admin only sees a burst of failures if they open the tab), a session list / "sign out everywhere" (sessions are stateless JWTs — needs a token-version column), CSV export, and records for logout / password-reset / invitation-acceptance / mobile-refresh — so **an account takeover performed via password reset leaves no trace in this view**. Known limits: the throttle store is in-memory per container (resets on deploy; same limitation `checkRateLimit` carries — porting both to a shared store is ONE job), unknown-email attempts are recorded but org-null so invisible in the UI, and `surface` is client-supplied (display label only). **`.env.example` is gitignored** (`.gitignore` line 44 `.env*`), so `LOGIN_GEO_ENABLED`/`LOGIN_GEO_TOKEN` are documented in LOGIN_ACTIVITY.md §4.1 — and CLAUDE.md §10's claim that `.env.example` is in the repo is **doc drift: it has never been committed**. **Same-day follow-up — "who is logged in RIGHT NOW" (`User.lastSeenAt`):** the first cut answered "who signed in, when" but not "who is using this now", and the two are different questions — the owner asked for the second. The blocker is structural: sessions are **stateless JWTs** (`strategy: "jwt"`), so there is no server-side session record to enumerate (`AuthSession` exists from the Prisma adapter and is **completely unused**). Rather than switch to database sessions — a Postgres read on **every** authenticated request on a live system, the pooler becoming a hard dependency for reading, and everyone signed out at cutover — presence is a nullable `User.lastSeenAt` scalar (additive migration `20260728120000`) stamped from the JWT callback's **existing** 5-minute role-revalidation block, so an active person costs one extra write per 5 min, not one per request. [src/lib/active-users.ts](src/lib/active-users.ts) owns the window math + `touchLastSeen()` (never throws; **`updateMany` not `update`** — `update` throws P2025 once the row is gone, and a JWT outlives the row it names, so a deleted account would throw on every request until expiry). The online window (10 min) is deliberately **double** the stamp interval — at equal values someone actively working flickers offline between stamps; pinned by a test. Also stamped at sign-in (the JWT block's clock resets on login, so a fresh sign-in would otherwise read offline for 5 min) and on mobile-refresh (the mobile equivalent of the periodic block). Scalar on `User` rather than a side table, deliberately unlike `WebinarPresence` — that kept off the hot `Registration` row because it carries thousands of attendees heartbeating every 30s; this is a handful of staff at 5-min granularity, three orders of magnitude apart. New `GET /api/organization/active-users` (same ADMIN+ boundary + org scoping as the sign-in history beside it) + an **Active Now** card stacked above the history in the same tab. +34 tests (suite 4122 → 4156). **New [docs/SESSION_ARCHITECTURE.md](docs/SESSION_ARCHITECTURE.md)** explains stateless-JWT vs database vs Redis sessions, what each buys and costs, why EA-SYS stays stateless, and §7 the cheap `tokenVersion` path to "sign out everywhere" — because **the honest remaining gap is that nothing can sign anyone out**: a compromised account can't be revoked (a password change does NOT invalidate the existing token, and a deleted account's cookie works until it expires, up to 24h). **⚠️ That closing claim was SUPERSEDED Aug 11, 2026** — `User.tokenVersion` shipped, so revocation exists: deleting, deactivating, or bumping the counter all end a web session (immediately for staff, within 5 min for everyone else), and a password reset bumps it automatically. The mobile half was closed Aug 25, 2026 — see that entry.

- **Built-in "standard" certificate templates — clone-and-edit starters for Attendance + Appreciation (July 27, 2026)** — Creating a certificate template gave you an empty row: no background, no text boxes, and a preview that rendered an instructional placeholder. The organizer's first move was to reproduce, from nothing, a layout every certificate shares. **New: a "Use standard" button beside "+ Add" on each category card** (`POST .../certificates/templates/starter`) creates a ready-made template — generated background PDF + pre-positioned, fully tokenized text boxes — which they then edit, or **Duplicate** to spin role variants off. **(1) Modelled on the real thing, not invented.** OSH Monthly Meeting 2026 is the ONLY certificate setup configured on any event, so its geometry IS the house convention and the starter matches it: A4 portrait exported at **300 DPI** (coordinate space **2480 × 3508**, not true A4's 595 × 842), one centred column at `x=240 / width=2000`, Times-Roman/Times-Bold, navy `#1a2e5a`. Matching that scale is deliberate — designers export raster-backed PDFs at print DPI, so swapping our background for the designer's artwork keeps every box in place; a starter built at true A4 points would collapse into the top-left corner the moment 2480-wide artwork replaced it. **(2) What it fixes about that setup.** Of OSH's nine boxes only `{{recipientName}}` is a token — event name, date, accreditor, accreditation number and CME hours are **typed literals**, so each of its four role variants was made by duplicating and retyping and none of it tracks the event record. Every line in the starter is a token, and the appreciation wording uses `{{role}}` inline against a default template role of "Speaker" — duplicate, change one field, the sentence re-words itself. **(3) The tokens that didn't exist.** The cert body resolved only 9 tokens; six are new — `organizationName`, `certificateSerial`, `issuedDate`, plus `abstractTitle`/`sessionTitles` which were **threaded into the render data and referenced in code comments but never resolved** (a box using them printed blank + logged a warn), and **`accreditationName`**, the one that actually forced OSH's hardcoding: `AccreditationEntry.body` is a closed 6-value enum and `OTHER` renders the literal *"The Accrediting Body"*, so the Oman Medical Specialty Board could only be typed by hand. New optional free-text `AccreditationEntry.name` (settings JSON — no migration) + an input in the CME/CPD tab; `{{accreditationBody}}` is unchanged so existing templates keep working. All six are purely additive — no existing template references them. **(4) New [token-catalog.ts](src/lib/certificates/token-catalog.ts) as the single list.** The token list lived in two hand-maintained places that had already drifted: `resolveTokens()` (9 resolving) and the canvas editor's `AVAILABLE_TOKENS` (7 shown) — **`{{role}}` shipped in June and never reached the editor**, so the token an appreciation cert most wants was undiscoverable for a month. The catalog is client-safe (the editor renders it directly, now with a "renders as:" sample per token) and a drift test asserts `Object.keys(resolveTokens(...))` equals the catalog keys **both ways** — resolved-but-unlisted is a hidden capability, listed-but-unresolved prints blank on a real certificate. **(5) Two derived-not-duplicated invariants.** The background PDF and the text boxes are computed from the **same** layout constants — a background shipped as a binary asset would drift the first time a coordinate moved, and the rule under the recipient's name would stop being under the recipient's name with nothing failing. And every token in every starter box is checked against the catalog in CI, because that failure is silent on the page. **(6) The background carries no text** — frame and rules only, so every word is an editable text box and none of it needs a designer (a test asserts it embeds no fonts). **(7) It adapts to the event** — accreditation / CME / venue lines are OMITTED when unconfigured rather than shipping `Total Hour/s Awarded:` with nothing after the colon; the response returns `omittedSections` so the toast says what was skipped and why, and a test asserts no starter box ever ends in a dangling `:`. Auto-issue starts **off** (a starter that auto-issued on creation would mail certs to an unreviewed tag audience — same reasoning as `/duplicate`). **(8) Dedup en route:** the text-box Zod schema was about to become its **fourth** copy, so the two REST doors + the starter now share [template-box-schema.ts](src/lib/certificates/template-box-schema.ts), and the MCP validator (deliberately hand-rolled for JSON-RPC error shapes) imports the same font list. Also fixed in passing: the CME settings save mutation whitelists fields, so the new accreditor-name input would have been a **dead write** — the contacts-`additionalEmail` class. **No schema change, no migration.** +53 tests (3 files: catalog↔resolver drift both ways, starter token-validity/geometry/no-dangling-labels/no-embedded-fonts, route auth+RBAC+adaptation+storage-fails-before-row) — suite **3916 → 3969**. Verified by rendering both certificates end-to-end through the real renderer. tsc/eslint/vitest/build green.
- **Typeless imports + completion-form type self-select (July 27, 2026)** — Imported registrations no longer land on a guessed registration type; the person can state their own on the completion form. **The incident that drove it:** both importers grabbed an arbitrary type as their default (unordered `findFirst` / `findMany[0]` — heap order), which put 502 imported delegates onto a type literally named "Faculty" on a live event. **The rule now ([src/lib/import-ticket-type.ts](src/lib/import-ticket-type.ts)): never guess.** A row takes a type only when the file names one or the organizer explicitly picks a fallback in the CSV dialog (faculty types refused at every surface: fallback picker, name-matching → row error, manual-add dropdown, completion picker); otherwise `ticketTypeId` stays **null** — schema/seats/stats/UI already support it, and the import report returns an `uncategorised` count. **Free event ⇒ typeless rows owe nothing (COMPLIMENTARY/CONFIRMED). Paid event ⇒ CSV still allows typeless (amber dialog warning), and the person states their type via "Send Registration Forms"** (works for manually-added registrations too — the detail sheet + list can send the completion email to any non-cancelled, account-less registration). **The completion form** ([complete-registration](src/app/e/%5Bslug%5D/complete-registration/page.tsx) + [route](src/app/api/public/events/%5Bslug%5D/complete-registration/route.ts)) gains a type-picker section for typeless rows (previously a null type white-screened the page): price/tier resolved **entirely server-side** — the chosen type + whichever tier is on sale now (new pure [src/lib/current-pricing-tier.ts](src/lib/current-pricing-tier.ts) `pickCurrentPricingTier`; owner decision: "whatever is open when they complete") — so a crafted request can't claim a closed Early-Bird rate; seat claimed atomically (sold-out ⇒ 409 + full rollback, token survives); `originalPrice` stamped; attendee free-text category mirrored. **Review round (same day, findings picked by owner):** **M1** — an EXPLICITLY-set `paymentStatus` (CSV column / admin sheet: PAID offline, INCLUSIVE sponsor-paid) survives completion — only the typeless COMPLIMENTARY default flips to UNASSIGNED, audit records `paymentStatusPreserved` (before this, completion re-opened dunning on settled rows); **M3** — the type-set is a **conditional row claim** (`where { id, ticketTypeId: null }`) → 409 `REGISTRATION_TYPE_ALREADY_SET` when an organizer assigned a type concurrently (whole tx incl. the seat increment rolls back); **L2** — a self-selected `requiresApproval` type flips CONFIRMED → **PENDING** (public-register semantics — the person picks the type, so it enters the approval queue; only the import-default CONFIRMED flips); **L3** — hook types carry `uncategorised`. **Also fixed: event clone dropped `isFaculty` + `virtualPrice`** — every clone turned the hidden speaker-companion type into a publicly bookable "Faculty" delegate type (the incident's other half) and reset HYBRID virtual pricing. **EventsAir import** takes the same optional fallback but hard-blocks typeless rows on a priced event (`DEFAULT_TICKET_TYPE_REQUIRED`) — its dialog has no picker yet, deferred with **M2 + L1** (VIRTUAL completion seat/price) in ROADMAP §"Typeless-import + completion self-select review". +67 tests (import resolution incl. faculty-name row errors, tier picker truth table, 12 route-level completion tests, clone isFaculty/virtualPrice) — suite **4008**; e2e spec [import-completion-self-select.spec.ts](e2e/import-completion-self-select.spec.ts) (not run locally — needs the seeded test DB). tsc/eslint/vitest/build green. No schema change (`Registration.ticketTypeId` was already nullable).
- **Import/export audit trail — every bulk data movement is now recorded (July 27, 2026)** — A verification pass found audit coverage on import/export was *accidental*: **5 of 23 paths** wrote an `AuditLog` row, a handful wrote a pino line, and **the single most-used export — the registrations list CSV — left no trace of any kind** because it was built in the browser (`Blob` download, no request ever reached the server). *"Who exported our attendee list last month?"* was unanswerable. **(1) One helper, one shape** — new [src/lib/audit-data-transfer.ts](src/lib/audit-data-transfer.ts) `recordExport()` / `recordImport()`: fire-and-forget with a logged catch (**never throws** — an audit blip must not fail a file already streamed), `entityId` names the *scope* (`event:<id>` / `org:<id>`, the shape the contacts export established), and `changes` carries source/format/rowCount/role/ip + the filters that narrowed the pull, so a 12-row filtered export is distinguishable from a whole-book dump. Prisma's `Json` input rejects optional keys, so the payload is assembled as a mutable `TransferChanges` then handed over. **(2) The registrations export moved server-side** — now `?export=csv` **on the existing list route**, deliberately NOT a sibling endpoint: the query, filters, event-access gate and **both** redaction layers (`redactFinancialFields` + `redactBarcodeFields`) are already resolved there, so the CSV cannot disagree with the table or leak a field the caller's role can't see. Row logic extracted to [src/lib/registration-export.ts](src/lib/registration-export.ts) (unit-testable without a request); **redaction contract: redacted money/barcode columns render BLANK, never a wrong number, and the column count never changes** so a spreadsheet template built against one role's export still parses another's. A `q` free-text param was added so the server file matches what's on screen — merged with the tag filter into ONE nested `attendee` where, since two `attendee` keys would silently drop one (the "bad filter widens the result set" class). The client-side builder was **deleted**. **(3) Coverage.** Newly audited exports: registrations, webinar attendance, analytics (aggregate **and** the per-attendee check-in log, separate `entityType`s), reimbursements (passport + bank details), RSVP roster, survey responses, org + event invoices (all three formats — csv/quickbooks/pdf-zip), CRM deals; contacts export migrated off its inline copy. Newly audited imports: contacts CSV, contacts EventsAir, registrations CSV, abstracts CSV, DTCM barcodes, registrations-from-contacts. **`recordImport` is deliberately distinct from the per-row `CREATE` audits** some paths already write — those answer "which rows exist"; this answers "who ran an import and how much landed", **including the skipped and failed rows, which leave no per-row trace at all**. **(4) Dropped CSV columns fixed (organizer-reported).** `role` (the AttendeeRole profession category) was parsed **only** by the registrations importer — speakers and contacts silently dropped it, *and the registrations template never offered the column*, which is why it went unused. `title` was likewise dropped by the contacts importer, and `TITLE_VALUES` was hardcoded separately in two importers. Both are now single shared parsers in [src/lib/schemas.ts](src/lib/schemas.ts) — `parseAttendeeRole()` (accepts "Allied Health" / "allied-health" / `ALLIED_HEALTH`) and `parseTitle()` (accepts the UI's trailing period, "Dr." → `DR`) — used by all three importers, which also removed two inline enum-union casts. Speaker role now also flows into the org Contact store so the CRM row isn't a husk. **(5) CSV templates restructured** — `ENTITY_CONFIG` was two parallel arrays (`optional` + `sampleRow`) where inserting a column in one and not the other shifted every subsequent cell in the downloaded file; it's now **ONE ordered list per entity** carrying `{name, sample, required}` together, with required/optional/sampleRow derived — **misalignment is impossible by construction**. Person-identity columns (`title, firstName, lastName, email, phone`) are grouped first on registrations / speakers / contacts (organizer request). **Order is presentation only** — every importer resolves columns by name via `headers.indexOf`. **No schema change, no migration** (`AuditLog` already had `action`/`changes`/`ipAddress`). **Caught by post-build review (all three reviewers independently):** the first cut of the export URL **omitted the tag filter**, and because tags are applied SERVER-side on the table's own query, an organizer filtered to `committee` (12 rows on screen) would have received a CSV of the **entire attendee book** — a PII over-disclosure with no on-screen signal. The server side was correct and even had a passing test for it; the bug was in the caller, so the server test passed against it (this repo's "a test can pass against the bug it's meant to catch" lesson, re-instanced). Fixed, plus a caller-side test asserting the export URL carries every filter the table applies. **45 tests across 4 new files** (helper contract incl. never-throws; row-builder redaction/VAT/arity; the export endpoint's audit + redaction + filter-merge; both parsers; template parity + identity-grouping + no-duplicate-columns guards; and a caller-side guard that the export URL sends every filter the table applies) — suite at **3897**. tsc/eslint/vitest/build green. **Coverage, verified by grep after the review round below: `recordExport` at 12 call sites, `recordImport` at 13 (12 route files + the shared `runCrmCsvImport` wrapper, which covers all three CRM importers).** The only `*import*` routes without a call are `send-completion-emails` (sends email, imports nothing) and `import-logs` (a GET reader). **(6) Post-review round (same day).** Three independent reviewers ran over the diff. Beyond the blocker above, shipped: a **new `canExportRegistrations` / `denyRegistrationExport` boundary** ([registration-export-visibility.ts](src/lib/registration-export-visibility.ts)) — export is deliberately NARROWER than read, so MEMBER (leadership/sponsor-side) and an internal-domain REGISTRANT can page the list on screen but get 403 on the file; it is its own predicate because `canViewFinance` *includes* MEMBER and `canViewEntryBarcode` answers an unrelated question (the recurring "reaching for a close-enough predicate is the signal to write a new one" lesson). The gate + a **10/hr rate limit** run as an **export pre-flight before the query**, so a refused export never runs the unbounded `findMany` + per-row financials on the box that serves the door scanner. `%`/`_` in `q` are now **escaped** before reaching Prisma `contains` (unescaped they are ILIKE wildcards, so the FILE would match more rows than the SCREEN — the export's whole premise is that they agree). A malformed `status`/`paymentStatus` now **400s `INVALID_FILTER`** instead of silently dropping the predicate and widening the pull, matching what `parseDateRangeFilters` already did 40 lines below in the same function. **The raw search term is no longer persisted** — `AuditLog` has no prune job (unlike `EmailLog.htmlBody`) and its rows survive a subject-erasure request, so operators searching full email addresses would have re-created the PII we delete elsewhere; `changes.filters` now carries `qLength` + a truncated sha256 `qFingerprint`, which still answers "targeted or full dump?" and still correlates repeated searches. Date-range narrowing is recorded (`dateRangeAuditFilters`). **`GET /api/activity` was excluding every org-scoped audit row** — `event: { organizationId }` on a nullable relation means "event is non-null AND matches", so the contacts/invoices/CRM export audits were invisible in the only UI that reads `AuditLog`; it now matches either shape. Unrecognized `role`/`title` cells are **counted and warn-logged once per import** (previously a mis-typed column silently nulled every row while reporting a clean import — the same silent-drop class this feature exists to fix, one layer down). `logs/archive` was deliberately left unaudited: it exports SUPER_ADMIN-only *system logs*, not org business data. **Known remaining gap (unchanged):** `ImportLog` is still written only by the EventsAir importer, and the `/events/[eventId]/imports` "Import History" page that reads it **is not linked in the sidebar** — every other import now lands in `AuditLog` instead. **Deferred (ROADMAP):** `AuditLog` has no flat `organizationId` column (org id lives in `changes` JSON, which can't back an RLS policy — matters for the multi-tenancy sweep); the redactors destroy `Date`/`Decimal` instances (a **pre-existing** bug — `Object.entries(new Date())` is `[]` — so MEMBER's registrations list has rendered broken dates + `NaN` money since the July 11 barcode redaction; the fix belongs in the redactors); `recordExport`'s positional `Request` arg is unlike its single-object siblings; and `TITLE_SET` is a third in-file copy of the Title enum.

Behavior-preserving on master (policy files are never applied there).
- **Webinar deferred-findings batch — security MEDs + waiting-room UX, all shipped (July 27, 2026)** — Both deferred webinar clusters closed in one gated batch (owner: "both batches"). **Security (July 10 program/agenda review deferrals):** **M3** — the public [stream-status route](src/app/api/public/events/%5Bslug%5D/sessions/%5BsessionId%5D/stream-status/route.ts) handed `hlsUrl`/`hlsOriginUrl` **and the raw `streamKey`** to anyone — and the streamKey doubles as the RTMP **publish credential** on MediaMTX (stream-hijack, not just free viewing). `streamKey` is now never returned (the client never used it); the URL fields are gated on auth + (org staff of the event's org OR non-cancelled registration) with a 60s per-(user,event) positive micro-cache so a 5k recovery-poll storm doesn't hammer the pool; anonymous callers get the bare liveness flag. The GET's conditional `streamStatus` write stays **deliberately** (fires only on a real probe-state transition — not attacker-amplifiable). **M5** resolved via M3 + a `eventType === "WEBINAR"` 404 guard on `lobby-status` (the DRAFT residual — a liveness boolean + non-sensitive lobby copy — is required by the DRAFT-auto-open test flow, accepted). **M1** — [provisionWebinar](src/lib/webinar-provisioner.ts) (fired concurrently from event-create fire-and-forget AND the console's "Re-run provisioner") could mint **two anchor sessions + two billable Zoom webinars**; it now claims a `webinar.provisioningAt` sentinel atomically through the `updateEventSettings` row lock — contended → back off (`provision-already-in-progress`, 409 on the manual re-run), lost → one idempotent retry against the winner's session, stale (>10 min crashed claim) → reclaimable, dangling anchor pointer → recovery unaffected, sentinel released on success AND failure; the final settings write went function-form so a concurrent lobby-settings save is no longer clobbered. **M6** — retiming a session now PATCHes the linked Zoom meeting/webinar (new start + recomputed duration + event timezone) and mirrors `ZoomMeeting.duration`, from [session-service](src/services/session-service.ts) so REST + MCP both get it; failure-isolated — a Zoom outage surfaces as `zoomSync: "failed"` through the PUT + MCP `update_session` responses and a dashboard warning toast ("Zoom still shows the old time — save again to retry"), never failing the save. **Waiting-room UX (June 23 review deferrals):** the LobbyCard shows a red **"scheduled start has passed — room still closed"** alert with the live "N attendees waiting in the lobby" presence count (30s tick; hides on open/close or 30 min past end); the public lobby countdown flips to "Running a little late…" 10 min past T-0; a **DRAFT-auto-open hint** (webinar GET now returns `event.status`); **save-time HLS validation** at both doors (settings PUT rejects switching to hls without a configured live stream, 400 `HLS_STREAM_NOT_CONFIGURED`; room-open is the final gate — closing always allowed); and the public session page's **Live/Ended badge** derives from the fresh `lobby.roomOpen` poll instead of the load-time snapshot. +29 tests (8 provisioner-claim with a STATEFUL settings mock so the claim mechanics run for real, 6 stream-status gating, 9 HLS validation, 6 Zoom retime-sync; suite 3798 → 3827). No schema change, no migration. ROADMAP: M1/M3/M5/M6 + the whole waiting-room table struck (only the pre-existing shared-rate-limiter LOW remains).
- **CRM surfaced + email CC/BCC + reply-forwarding + adversarial review (July 24, 2026)** — A full CRM hardening + feature day. **(1) Sidebar (`08667e07`):** `CRM_IN_SIDEBAR` flipped `false → true` in [sidebar.tsx](src/components/layout/sidebar.tsx) — the CRM entry is now visible to roles with `canCrm` (SUPER_ADMIN / ADMIN / ORGANIZER / MEMBER / CRM_USER); a dedicated CRM_USER was always routed there. **(2) Freshsales import — downloadable sample template (`96334353`):** the import dialog (companies/contacts/deals) gained a **"Download sample template"** button; `buildSampleCsv()` in [freshsales-import.ts](src/crm/lib/freshsales-import.ts) derives the sample from curated human-readable headers that normalize to a real synonym, so a downloaded sample always imports cleanly (a drift test resolves every sample header against the field spec). **(3) CRM email CC/BCC + copy-to-me (`0aec8b9c`):** the deal Email dialog + sponsor blast gained manual **CC/BCC** fields + a **"Send a copy to me"** checkbox (default ON) that auto-BCCs the sending CRM user so every send lands in their Outlook; threaded route Zod → `sendDealEmail`/`sendSponsorProspectus` → `dispatchCrmEmail` (merges branding CC + manual; BCC = manual + sender copy). **(4) Reply-forwarding (same commit):** new `CrmEmailThread.notifyEmails` (additive migration) stores the outbound CC/BCC; when a sponsor replies, [inbound-email-worker.ts](src/crm/inbound-email-worker.ts) forward-copies it to the deal owner **+ partnerships@ (`CRM_EMAIL_FROM_ADDRESS`) + the CC/BCC watchers** (incl. the sender's own copy), deduped, never back to the replier; unverified/spoofed replies still suppress ALL forwards (anti-BEC). **(5) Adversarial CRM review — 4 angles (lifecycle · RBAC/PII/finance · concurrency · drift/logging): 0 BLOCKER / 0 HIGH.** Security (cross-org IDOR across all 38 routes + 15 services, finance redaction, inbox staff-only, reply-forward not inbound-injectable) and concurrency (conditional-claim on every transition, data-layer idempotency on both workers) verified clean. **Fixes shipped:** **M1 (`f16c8020`)** the reply-forward excluded the thread counterparty instead of the actual replier (`args.fromEmail`) — a CC'd colleague who replied got their own reply bounced back (a regression from #4); **M2 (`675708b6`)** the sponsor blast had only a 2-min in-memory dedup → replaced with a DB-backed `CrmEmailSendClaim` (additive migration, 10-min window, cross-container, atomic `@@unique([organizationId, dedupHash])` claim + stale-refresh, opportunistic prune) so a gateway-timeout-then-re-click can't re-email the audience — **owner-scoped to "persistent enqueue dedup", NOT full jobification (crash-mid-send resume out of scope)**; **LOWs (`a044bc86`)** `moveDealStage` no longer re-stamps `wonAt` on a same-outcome terminal move (e.g. "Won — Signed" → "Won — Invoiced"), the Freshsales re-import preserves the existing deal owner when the CSV owner is unmatchable (a role change must not silently un-own), import P2002 rows read "already exists — re-run to converge", and the CRM route gate logs its 401s. **Docs refreshed (`f16c8020`):** CRM_STATUS.html + `src/crm/README.md` no longer say "NOT DEPLOYED / sidebar hidden / two-way inbox out of scope" (all untrue now); the crm-inbox.tsx header comment no longer describes a reply composer (the inbox is read-only). +~20 tests across the day; every commit gated (tsc/eslint/vitest 3787/build) and **only own files** (a concurrent billing-accounts + tenancy session ran in the same tree — its WIP left untouched). **Deliberately left as-is (accepted edges, ROADMAP §"CRM review — deferred"):** quote-number gaps on render failure (atomic-counter design), the BEC same-domain residual against a DMARC-less counterparty (best-effort), the MCP-vs-REST stage-move nuance (documented), the enrich-forever externalId edge, the inbound 3-way-overlap spurious log; **M3** (silent 401s) fixed only at the CRM gate — the deeper cause is core `getOrgContext`, systemic. Also carries a **multi-tenancy note** ([MULTI_TENANCY_IMPACT.md](docs/MULTI_TENANCY_IMPACT.md) §7.1): the CRM email plumbing leans on 3 global env vars — the reply-forward to a single global partnerships mailbox would **cross-tenant-leak** on a multi-tenant silo (hard precondition before the platform onboards a 2nd tenant); harmless on single-org master.
