Frontend-only — both create backends + models already accepted every field.
  - **Public-page SEO metadata.** Public `/e/[slug]/*` pages are client components that inherited the generic root `<title>`. New **server `layout.tsx`** files now emit **per-event** OpenGraph/Twitter tags (event name, HTML-stripped description, banner as the share image) and **per-section titles** ("Register — Event", "Agenda — Event", the session's own name, …) via a shared `buildEventMetadata()` ([src/lib/public-event-metadata.ts](src/lib/public-event-metadata.ts), event lookup wrapped in React `cache`) + `metadataBase` on the root layout so the banner's relative URL resolves absolute for crawlers. **Known follow-up (tracked):** the slug lookups are org-unscoped — fine single-org; must add `organizationId` when multi-tenant lands (`docs/MULTI_TENANCY_IMPACT.md`).
  - **scheduled-email 0-recipient = benign skip.** A scheduled bulk send that resolves to **zero** recipients at fire time is now a terminal `SENT` (0 counts) logged at info — not a `FAILED` + error-level admin page. `BulkEmailError` gained `NO_RECIPIENTS_CODE` that [src/lib/scheduled-emails-worker.ts](src/lib/scheduled-emails-worker.ts) branches on; the immediate "Send now" route still returns a 400 so an operator gets feedback. Stops the auto-enqueued webinar sequence on empty/test events from paging hourly.
  - **Smaller:** removed the "Back to Event Page" button on the post-registration confirmation page ([confirmation/page.tsx](src/app/e/%5Bslug%5D/confirmation/page.tsx)); deleted the **orphaned `docker/Dockerfile`** (dead/unreferenced; `Dockerfile.dev` + root `Dockerfile`/`Dockerfile.worker` are the live ones); narrowed the dashboard sidebar `w-64 → w-56`; added `.vscode/launch.json` debug configs.

- **Billing payers — event-level inline entry with org-level consolidation (June 29, 2026)** — Previously a payer ("Charge to another account") could only be created at the **org** level (Settings → Billing), then attached to an event, then picked on the registration — a 3-step context switch. Now an organizer can add a payer **inline from the registration Charge-to picker** (the full-page Add Registration form), mirroring how Contacts work: capture in context, consolidate into one org record. New `findOrCreateBillingAccount()` ([billing-account-service.ts](src/services/billing-account-service.ts)) — **exact (case-insensitive, trimmed) name → reuse** the existing org payer (never a duplicate); a **near-duplicate name** (fuzzy: one alphanumeric key contains the other, e.g. "Cleveland Clinic" vs "Cleveland Clinic Foundation") → create + flag `needsReview` for an admin to merge later (advisory, never blocks). New event-scoped `POST /api/events/[eventId]/billing-accounts` ([route](src/app/api/events/%5BeventId%5D/billing-accounts/route.ts), `denyReviewer`+`denyFinance`) does the find-or-create at the org level **and auto-attaches** the `EventBillingAccount` junction. New reusable [AddPayerDialog](src/components/billing/add-payer-dialog.tsx) (name + type + contact/email/phone/address/city/country/tax) + `useCreateAndAttachBillingAccount` hook; wired into the full-page form ("+ Add a new payer"). The payer stays a **single shared org row** (only the per-event attachment is event-specific) — exact-name reuse does NOT clobber the existing record's details (edit those in Settings → Billing). +4 service tests (reuse / create / fuzzy-flag / NAME_REQUIRED). **Follow-ups (reusable component makes them trivial):** the registration detail-sheet reassign picker + the quick-add dialog + an admin merge UI for `needsReview` payers. tsc/eslint/vitest 1737/build green.

- **Event clone now copies custom email templates (June 29, 2026)** — Event clone already copied email **branding** (header/footer image, footer HTML, from address/name, CC) + all the HTML content fields (registration/abstract/speaker-agreement) + **survey** (`surveyConfig` + `surveyIntroHtml`, deliberately NOT the `surveyShareLink` token or responses). The one missing "communications" piece was the per-event **`EmailTemplate`** rows (the custom/edited templates under Communications → Email Templates) — they were silently dropped on clone. [clone/route.ts](src/app/api/events/%5BeventId%5D/clone/route.ts) now `include`s `emailTemplates` and `createMany`s them onto the new event inside the same transaction (slug/name/subject/htmlContent/textContent/isActive copied; no ID remap needed; the new event has no templates so the `@@unique([eventId, slug])` can't collide). **Scheduled emails are intentionally NOT cloned** (time-specific sends tied to the source event). +1 clone test (templates copied with fields + isActive preserved). tsc/eslint/vitest/build green.

- **Event.settings / Organization.settings lost-update fixed — atomic merge helper (June 29, 2026, data-loss audit #4)** — The settings JSON blob holds many features' config (reviewerUserIds, sponsors, webinar, zoom, cme, registrationOpen, …) and **every** writer did read-whole-blob → spread → `db.event.update({ data: { settings } })` **outside any transaction** — a lost-update race: two requests touching DIFFERENT keys both read the old blob, second write silently drops the first (e.g. saving sponsors wiped a concurrently-added reviewer). New [src/lib/event-settings.ts](src/lib/event-settings.ts) `updateEventSettings(eventId, patch)` + `updateOrganizationSettings(orgId, patch)`: an atomic `SELECT … FOR UPDATE` row-lock + merge + write inside `db.$transaction` (the lock holds across Prisma's interactive tx, including through the pgbouncer transaction pooler — single backend per tx). Object patch = shallow-merge (preserve unspecified keys); function patch `(cur)=>next` = full replace (for array append/remove / key delete, computed from the **locked** current). Migrated **all ~13 writers**: event PUT, org PUT, sponsors, webinar, zoom/settings, certificates/settings (cme), reviewers add (function-form append, deduped) + remove (filter), MCP `update_cme_settings`/`upsert_sponsors`, webinar-provisioner, org zoom creds (PUT + function-form DELETE), org eventsair creds. The general event PUT still strips `reviewerUserIds` from the incoming settings (helper preserves the existing list). +6 helper tests + crud settings test updated. **Adversarial review: 0 blockers/highs**; fixed MED (reviewer add same-key double-add → Set dedupe inside the lock). **Deferred (ROADMAP, low/admin-only):** cross-field atomicity in the split PUTs (settings + scalar columns are now 2 sequential writes — partial write on crash) + `settings.webinar` sub-key last-write-wins. tsc/eslint/vitest 1732/build green. **Part of a 4-fix data-loss batch** (#1 EventsAir import enrich-only `5024e42`, #2 MCP accommodation atomic re-book `b37db44`, #3 bulk-type + import-contacts oversell guards `37b0ab7`, #4 this).

- **Contact sync is now enrich-only — a sparse registration can't wipe Contact data (June 29, 2026)** — `syncToContact()` upserts the org-wide Contact (`@@unique([organizationId, email])`) from every event interaction. Its `cleanFields()` previously stripped only `undefined`, so a value of `null`/`""` **overwrote** (cleared) the Contact field — and the public new-event register passes `field || null` for blank optionals, meaning **a sparse later registration silently wiped richer data an earlier event had populated** on the same Contact (the sync is one-way event→Contact + latest-write-wins, and null counted as a write). Fix: `cleanFields()` now also skips `null` and `""` ([contact-sync.ts](src/lib/contact-sync.ts)) → the sync can **fill in or update** a field with real data but **never clears** an already-populated Contact field; the Contact accumulates the best-known value per field across events. Required name fields + `eventIds` always sync. **Behavior change (accepted):** intentionally *clearing* a field on a registration no longer propagates the clear to the Contact — to clear a Contact field you edit the Contact directly (that path doesn't go through this sync). The old comment claimed it stripped "undefined/null" but the code only stripped undefined — now they match. +5 tests ([contact-sync.test.ts](__tests__/lib/contact-sync.test.ts): null/undefined/"" skipped on update+create+upsert, real values still written, eventIds appended). tsc/eslint/vitest 1720/build green.

- **Faculty no longer shows as a "registration type" (June 26, 2026)** — Bug report: a faculty member's registration showed **"Faculty"** as the registration type, but registration type should always be a professional category (Physician / Allied Health / Nurse / Others). Root cause: a speaker's companion registration sits on the hidden **isFaculty** ticket type (needed to exclude faculty from paid capacity/revenue), the list/detail/CSV display the **ticket-type name**, and the companion's attendee row also **hardcoded** `registrationType = "Faculty"` ([speaker-companion.ts](src/lib/speaker-companion.ts)). "Faculty" is a **badge/role** (`badgeType`), not a profession. **Fix (3 parts):** (1) **Data** — `ensureSpeakerCompanionRegistration` now sets the companion attendee's `registrationType` to the **speaker's** professional category (`Speaker.registrationType`, which the Add-Speaker form already captures), blank if unrecorded — never "Faculty". Threaded `registrationType` through `CompanionSpeakerInput` + all callers (speaker-service, submitter route, batch helper). (2) **Display** — new pure `displayRegistrationType()` helper in [faculty-filter.ts](src/lib/faculty-filter.ts): for a faculty row (`ticketType.isFaculty`) it shows the profession (or "—"), **never** the literal "Faculty"; for delegates it's the ticket-type name (which IS their category). Wired into the registrations list badge, CSV export, and the detail sheet (reviewer read-only display + the editable Registration-Type cell, which for faculty becomes a read-only profession line since a faculty companion's ticket type isn't a reassignable delegate category). The list API + front-end `TicketType` type gained `isFaculty`; the list API attendee select gained `registrationType`. The Faculty status stays visible via the **Faculty badge**. (3) **Backfill** — [scripts/backfill-faculty-registration-type.ts](scripts/backfill-faculty-registration-type.ts) (dry-run default, `--write`, `--event`, idempotent) flips existing companion rows off `registrationType = "Faculty"` to the linked speaker's profession (or blank). **Operator-run AFTER deploy.** Note: someone who registered as a delegate (e.g. Physician) and was *then* made faculty already showed Physician correctly (the companion logic links their existing registration); only faculty-added-without-a-delegate-registration showed "Faculty". +8 tests (helper truth table + companion uses-profession-not-Faculty). tsc/eslint/vitest 1715/build green.

- **Reviewer-invite resend + silent-failure surfacing (June 26, 2026)** — Reviewer-audit finding: when the add-reviewer invite email fails, `findOrCreateReviewerUser` logs a warn and returns `invitationSent: false`, so the organizer can't tell a failed send from "sent, not yet accepted" — and there was no way to resend, leaving a reviewer permanently stranded with no account/link. New `POST /api/events/[eventId]/reviewers/[reviewerId]/resend-invitation` ([route](src/app/api/events/%5BeventId%5D/reviewers/%5BreviewerId%5D/resend-invitation/route.ts)): a **pending** account (`emailVerified` null) → re-mints a fresh setup token (deleteMany + create in a tx) + resends the `reviewer-invitation` setup email; an **active** account → resends the `reviewer-pool-invitation` reminder via `notifyReviewerPoolAdded`. Crucially, unlike the silent add path, a send failure **surfaces** as a 502 (`EMAIL_SEND_FAILED`) so the organizer knows it didn't go. 20/hr/user rate limit, org-scoped, `denyReviewer`-guarded, audited. UI: a "Resend" button on each **pending** reviewer row (Settings → Reviewers) next to Remove, via `useResendReviewerInvitation`; toast distinguishes setup-resend vs reminder. +4 route tests (pending→setup+token-mint, active→pool, send-fail→502, not-in-pool→404). tsc/eslint/vitest 1705/build green.

- **Conflict-of-interest enforcement on abstract review (June 26, 2026)** — Reviewer-audit finding: `AbstractReviewer.conflictFlag` was advisory only (stored + badged in the UI, never enforced) — a reviewer flagged conflicted on an abstract could still open and score it, and that review counted toward the decision. Now a conflicted reviewer is **blocked from submitting** (`403 CONFLICT_OF_INTEREST`) across all three submit paths: the REST submissions POST ([submissions/route.ts](src/app/api/events/%5BeventId%5D/abstracts/%5BabstractId%5D/submissions/route.ts)), MCP `submit_abstract_review`, and MCP `admin_submit_review_on_behalf` (which checks the **target** reviewer's flag, not the caller's) — each adds `conflictFlag` to its existing assignment lookup + a guard right after the reviewer-auth check, logged `abstract-submission:coi-blocked`. Pool reviewers with no explicit `AbstractReviewer` row carry no flag (unaffected). They can still *read* the abstract (GET) — hard-gating read is a possible follow-up. +3 route tests (conflicted→403+no-upsert, non-conflicted→submits, pool-reviewer→submits). No MCP version bump (tool params/schema unchanged). tsc/eslint/vitest 1701/build green.

- **Draft-abstract save no longer emails "submitted" (June 26, 2026)** — Reviewer/submitter audit finding. The abstract create POST ([abstracts/route.ts](src/app/api/events/%5BeventId%5D/abstracts/route.ts)) fired the `abstract-submission-confirmation` email **and** the "New Abstract Submitted" admin notification for both `SUBMITTED` and `DRAFT` — so saving a work-in-progress draft told the author they were done and pinged organizers about a non-submission. Both are now gated on `status === "SUBMITTED"`; a draft save is silent (it isn't submitted and is invisible to reviewers). `refreshEventStats` stays unconditional. Two-line behavioral gate (no test added — a predicate test would just re-implement the condition; the full suite confirms nothing relied on the old behavior). tsc/eslint/vitest 1698/build green.

- **Reviewer pool-add notification (June 26, 2026)** — Continuation of the reviewer "operational closure" cluster. Adding a reviewer to an event's pool (Settings → Reviewers, `POST .../events/[id]/reviewers`) told a **pre-existing** account nothing — only brand-new accounts got the account-setup invite (`reviewer-invitation`); an already-existing REVIEWER (or a speaker already linked to a User) was added silently. Now a pre-existing account gets a `reviewer-pool-invitation` email ("you've been added as a reviewer for {event}", link to `/my-reviews`) via a new `notifyReviewerPoolAdded` helper ([src/lib/abstract-reviewer-notify.ts](src/lib/abstract-reviewer-notify.ts)). The "pre-existing vs new" distinction is a real `existed` flag threaded out of `findOrCreateReviewerUser` (+ the speaker-with-userId path) — NOT the ambiguous `invitationSent` (which is also false when a new account's setup email *fails*, and that account can't log in yet so a "go review" email would be useless). New accounts still get only the setup invite (no double-email). New `reviewer-pool-invitation` system template (DEFAULT_TEMPLATES + TEMPLATE_VARIABLES + SYSTEM_TEMPLATE_SLUGS — drift test green); failure-isolated; logged to `EmailLog` as `entityType: USER`. +3 tests. **Still open in the cluster:** the per-abstract reviewers card omitting pool members, the reminder mechanism, COI enforcement, reviewer-invite resend/silent-failure. tsc/eslint/vitest 1698/build green.

- **Per-abstract reviewer-assignment notification (June 26, 2026)** — Follow-up to the reviewer/submitter audit. Assigning a reviewer to a *specific* abstract previously wrote the `AbstractReviewer` row and told the reviewer **nothing** — via REST (`POST .../abstracts/[id]/reviewers`) or the MCP `assign_reviewer_to_abstract` agent tool. Now both call a shared `notifyReviewerAssigned` helper ([src/lib/abstract-reviewer-notify.ts](src/lib/abstract-reviewer-notify.ts)) on a **new** assignment (NOT on idempotent re-assigns or role/COI flips), emailing the reviewer the abstract title + their role (Primary/Secondary/Consulting label) + a link to `/my-reviews`. New `reviewer-assignment` system email template (added to `DEFAULT_TEMPLATES` + `TEMPLATE_VARIABLES` + `SYSTEM_TEMPLATE_SLUGS` — drift test green). Fully failure-isolated (the helper never throws — a send failure logs but never breaks the assignment). Logged to `EmailLog` as `entityType: USER`. +5 tests (role-label mapping, name fallback, failure-isolation, no-template skip). No MCP version bump — the tool's name/params/schema are unchanged, only the executor's side-effect. Remaining reviewer "operational closure" items (pool-add notify, reminder mechanism, COI enforcement, invite-resend) still open in [docs/ROADMAP.md](docs/ROADMAP.md). tsc/eslint/vitest 1695/build green.

- **Reviewer/submitter lifecycle audit + 2 production-breaking fixes (June 26, 2026)** — A 3-agent end-to-end trace of the reviewer + submitter (+ the submitter→speaker→attendee crossover) flows. The core model is sound (per-reviewer scored submissions preserved on unassign, ACCEPTED/REJECTED both email + portal-surface, survey correctly optional-per-event, cross-org reviewer scoping leak-free), but surfaced two **live-impacting** gaps, both now fixed. **Fix #1 — self-registered submitter-speakers got NO companion registration → no badge / entry barcode / check-in / survey / attendance cert.** The public submitter route ([submitter/route.ts](src/app/api/public/events/%5Bslug%5D/submitter/route.ts)) created the Speaker with a raw `tx.speaker.create` and never called `ensureSpeakerCompanionRegistration` — unlike every other speaker-add path (createSpeaker service, CSV import, import-contacts, bulk). Since check-in/survey/cert all hang off the companion `Registration`, a faculty member who entered as an abstract submitter literally couldn't be scanned in. Now mints the companion after the account create (failure-isolated, mirrors createSpeaker; the existing backfill script recovers already-affected rows). **Fix #2 — resubmit-after-revision was silent.** The abstract PUT path's `isSubmission` gate was `status==="SUBMITTED" && existing==="DRAFT"`, so a `REVISION_REQUESTED → SUBMITTED` resubmit didn't re-stamp `submittedAt`, sent no confirmation to the author, and never told reviewers/organizers the revised abstract was back ([abstracts/[abstractId]/route.ts](src/app/api/events/%5BeventId%5D/abstracts/%5BabstractId%5D/route.ts)). Broadened to "INTO SUBMITTED from any non-SUBMITTED state" + added the confirmation email + `notifyEventAdmins` (labelled "Abstract Resubmitted" for the revision case), mirroring the create POST. +7 tests (2 route-level for the companion call incl. failure-isolation, 5 for the resubmission predicate). The **remaining audit findings** (reviewer per-abstract notify + reminder mechanism, COI not enforced, reviewer-invite silent-failure + no resend, accepted→present handoff is manual, draft-save emails "submitted", feedbackOnly dead code, mean-score visible to submitters) are catalogued in [docs/ROADMAP.md](docs/ROADMAP.md) "Reviewer/submitter lifecycle audit" for scheduling. tsc/eslint/vitest 1690/build green.

- **Hybrid attendance mode-change — seat-accounting unification + lazy barcode (June 26, 2026, pkg 0.4.12)** — Closed "the one real hybrid gap": switching a registration **virtual→in-person** left `qrCode` null (un-scannable) and — discovered mid-build — the update paths **mis-handled `soldCount`** for virtual regs entirely (a virtual reg never consumed a venue seat, but cancel/reactivate/type-change still moved the counter, since the old logic keyed off `status` alone). Fixed by introducing a **single seat-accounting model** in [src/lib/registration-seat.ts](src/lib/registration-seat.ts): `holdsSeat(status, mode)` (a reg holds a seat iff `status≠CANCELLED && IN_PERSON`), `planSeatTransition(prev, next)` → `{ release, claim }` ticket-type ids, and `needsQrCode`. Both update paths — REST PUT [registrations/[registrationId]/route.ts](src/app/api/events/%5BeventId%5D/registrations/%5BregistrationId%5D/route.ts) and MCP `update_registration` ([tools/registrations.ts](src/lib/agent/tools/registrations.ts)) — now **route every `TicketType.soldCount` delta through `planSeatTransition`** (replacing the ad-hoc status/type branches; preserves the existing cancel/reactivate/type-change behavior exactly for non-virtual + fixes virtual) and **lazily mint a barcode** on virtual→in-person (in-person→virtual releases the seat, keeps the barcode for audit). Capacity-guarded via the atomic `soldCount < quantity` claim predicate — a sold-out virtual→in-person hard-fails `CAPACITY_EXCEEDED` and the reg stays virtual (a valid state, nobody stranded). New **Attendance** Select on the registration detail sheet ([registration-detail-sheet.tsx](src/app/(dashboard)/events/%5BeventId%5D/registrations/registration-detail-sheet.tsx), HYBRID events + `!isReviewer`, via `useEvent`); MCP `update_registration` gained an `attendanceMode` param (pkg 0.4.11→0.4.12 + lockfile). Tests: 15 unit (the pure model — every transition incl. the latent virtual bugs) + 3 integration (the MCP executor actually moves `soldCount` + mints/keeps the barcode + CAPACITY_EXCEEDED). **Adversarial review = no blockers**; in-band it also closed a pre-existing REST IDOR (the request-supplied `ticketTypeId` is now event-scoped before the tx, parity with MCP) + added `attendanceMode`/`qrCodeMinted` to the MCP audit + documented the no-reprice boundary. New `src/lib/can-write.ts` `canWrite(role)` helper (added in the same session for the abstracts MEMBER-gate) is unrelated to this toggle (the toggle uses `!isReviewer` to match the PUT's `REGISTRATION_DESK_ALLOW`). **Deferred (review-flagged, in ROADMAP):** mode change does NOT recompute price/amount-owed (`virtualPrice` vs in-person — documented in the toggle + MCP description, matches the deferred "tier-windowed virtual pricing"); the detail-sheet inline-Select TOCTOU (quick-actions don't send `expectedUpdatedAt` → two concurrent seat-moving edits can double-release) is pre-existing + folds into the P1.1 `soldCount` reconciliation pass. tsc/eslint/vitest 1683/build green.

- **Correctness batch — auto-issue stall-reclaim + frontend silent-failure surfacing (June 26, 2026)** — Three backlog correctness fixes from [docs/ROADMAP.md](docs/ROADMAP.md), each gated + atomic. **(1) Cert auto-issue Phase-2 H2 — `reclaimStalledRuns` is now `autoIssue`-aware** (`f1ca449`, [src/lib/certificates/issue-worker.ts](src/lib/certificates/issue-worker.ts)). The worker's stall detector demoted any stalled `SENDING` run → `AWAITING_REVIEW`; correct for **manual** runs (operator re-confirms via Send) but a **survey-gated auto run has no operator**, so if its email phase stalled >10 min (SES outage / container restart mid-send) it sat in `AWAITING_REVIEW` un-emailed forever — and the registration is already terminally stamped, so the sweep won't re-enqueue → **silent cert non-delivery**. Now the SENDING reclaim partitions: manual (`autoIssue: false`) → `AWAITING_REVIEW`; auto (`autoIssue: true`) → **stay `SENDING`**, just refresh `lastTickAt` so the next tick re-drains the remaining `emailedAt`-null items (send phase is re-entrant; per-item failures already marked + excluded). Exported `reclaimStalledRuns` + 2 unit tests (the worker's render/send mechanics had no prior unit coverage). **(2) Registrant portal no longer silently shows "not registered" on a failed fetch** (`3fd6ca1`, [src/app/e/[slug]/my-registration/page.tsx](src/app/e/%5Bslug%5D/my-registration/page.tsx)). It ignored React Query's `isError`, so a failed `/api/registrant/registrations` fetch fell through to the "Not registered yet" empty state — a paying registrant would think their registration vanished. Now branches on `isError` → a red "Couldn't load your registration — your registration is safe, please try again" card with a Try-again (`refetch`) button, and logs to console/Sentry; the `queryFn` error carries the HTTP status. (Loading was already an early-return; the global `/my-registration` gateway is a server component that throws to the error boundary, so neither needed changing.) **(3) Bulk-tag failure now toasts** (`a1d4559`, [src/components/bulk-tag-dialog.tsx](src/components/bulk-tag-dialog.tsx)). `handleSubmit` awaited the caller's `onSubmit` and on a thrown mutation surfaced nothing (the caller's success toast is skipped by the throw); now it catches → `toast.error` + `console.error` and keeps the dialog open for retry — covers both the registrations + speakers callers (DRY, in the shared dialog). All verified tsc/eslint/vitest 1662/build green; ROADMAP rows updated (H2 shipped; "Frontend silent failures" now partial — MEMBER `canWrite(role)` gate + GET-load `!res.ok` swallows still open).

- **Simple-backlog cleanup batch (June 26, 2026)** — Six small, isolated, no-migration backlog items from [docs/ROADMAP.md](docs/ROADMAP.md) (deferred review findings), each gated + committed atomically: **(1)** `IssuedCertificatesCard` dev-only "pass registrationId OR speakerId" sentinel no longer renders in prod (returns null outside development) — `47c7fea`. **(2)** registration `recipientLabel` in the cert resend dialog now includes `title`, matching the speaker variant — `5f0c3f0`. **(3)** `AutoIssueAnalyticsCard` polls every 60s instead of 20s (staleTime 30s) — cuts post-event analytics load 3× — `2405a84` (ROADMAP M1 poll half; the covering-index half stays deferred). **(4)** CLAUDE.md doc-drift fix: the 4 current-description lines now reference `src/proxy.ts` (Next 16.1 rename of `middleware.ts`) + corrected the stale "stdio MCP drifts" note (both transports share `registerAllMcpTools()`) — `d5ba791`. **(5)** `handleNudgeY` + `pushUndoSnapshot` in the cert canvas editor read `textBoxes` from a latest-value ref (dropped from deps), so holding an arrow key no longer re-allocates those closures ~30×/s; undo/redo untouched (their pure-updater shape is the H3 StrictMode fix) — `94048f6`. **(6)** `LivePlayer` reads `onStreamStatusChange` from a latest-value ref + dropped from the init-effect deps, so a non-memoized handler can't tear down/recreate the HLS player + 10s poll — `d1999d9`. All verified tsc/eslint/vitest 1660/build green; ROADMAP rows struck through as shipped.

- **Linked registration ("attendee facet") on speaker detail (June 25, 2026, commit `2bd30ae`)** — A speaker's companion registration (the row that backs their badge / entry barcode / check-in / survey) was invisible on the speaker surfaces. Now `GET /api/events/[eventId]/speakers/[speakerId]` includes the `sourceRegistration` relation (`serialId`, `status`, `paymentStatus`, `attendanceMode`, `badgeType`, `qrCode`, `checkedInAt`, `surveyCompletedAt`, `createdSource`, `ticketType{name,isFaculty}`), and **both** speaker-detail views render it: the **speaker page** ([speakers/[speakerId]/page.tsx](src/app/(dashboard)/events/%5BeventId%5D/speakers/%5BspeakerId%5D/page.tsx)) gets a sidebar **"Registration" card** (Registration #, ticket type w/ Faculty pill, status, payment, badge, attendance, entry-barcode issued, checked-in date, survey status, a companion-vs-linked note, + a link to Registrations; empty state for an un-backfilled older speaker), and the **quick-view sheet** ([speaker-detail-sheet.tsx](src/components/speakers/speaker-detail-sheet.tsx)) gets a compact Registration block between Speaker Information and Sessions. Read-only/additive (no schema, no migration). Resolves the speaker via the existing `Speaker.sourceRegistration` FK. **Deferred nicety:** the "View in Registrations" link goes to the list (no per-registration deep-link URL exists yet — the registration detail is a slide-out sheet); a `?registrationId=` deep-link is a possible follow-up. tsc/eslint/vitest 1651/build green.

- **Survey-gated certificate auto-issue — Phase 2 (June 25, 2026, pkg 0.4.10→0.4.11)** — Completing the event survey now **auto-issues** every cert template flagged for it that the person qualifies for — **fully automatic** (rendered + emailed, no operator click; confirmed decision). The survey POST path is **untouched** (it already sets `surveyCompletedAt`); the cert worker drives off it. **Config (per template):** `CertificateTemplate.autoIssueOnSurvey` + `autoIssueTag` (editor toggle + tag input; REST POST/PATCH + MCP `create_/update_certificate_template`). A tag is **required** to match anyone (we refuse to mass-issue to everyone who surveyed); a flagged-but-tagless template is flagged in the analytics card + a `cert-auto-issue:template-missing-tag` warn. **Trigger = worker sweep** (no inline enqueue): new nullable `Registration.certAutoIssueCheckedAt` + a **partial index** (`WHERE certAutoIssueCheckedAt IS NULL AND surveyCompletedAt IS NOT NULL`); [src/lib/certificates/auto-issue.ts](src/lib/certificates/auto-issue.ts) `runAutoIssueSweep()` scans survey-completed-but-unchecked rows past their backoff gate. **Routing (constraint C):** attendee tags → **ATTENDANCE** templates → cert on `registrationId`; the linked speaker's tags (companion `sourceRegistrationId` reverse, else read-time email match) → **APPRECIATION** → cert on `speakerId` — a speaker who surveys via their companion gets **both**. Pure `selectAutoIssueTargets` (unit-tested). **Delivery reuses `CertificateIssueRun`** — each (template, recipient) → a 1-item run with a new `autoIssue` flag + **null operator** (nullable `CertificateIssueRun.triggeredByUserId` + `IssuedCertificate.issuedByUserId`); auto runs **skip the AWAITING_REVIEW gate** ([issue-worker.ts](src/lib/certificates/issue-worker.ts) render → SENDING directly). Whole per-registration resolve+enqueue+stamp is one transaction (crash-safe). **Idempotency:** per-template `IssuedCertificate` uniqueness **+** a pre-create guard (skip if a cert OR an auto-run item already covers (event, template, recipient)) — re-sweeps / crash-retries / manual-first can't duplicate or double-email. **Retry + backoff (operator-requested):** a transient per-reg failure bumps `certAutoIssueAttempts`, records `certAutoIssueError`, defers via `certAutoIssueNextAttemptAt = now + backoff` (1/5/15/60/180 min — never head-of-line-blocks the queue); after **5** attempts gives up terminally (manual Issue is the backstop). **Analytics (operator-requested):** every sweep logs `cert-auto-issue:sweep` with counts; `GET .../certificates/auto-issue/analytics` (registration state pending/retrying/resolved/gaveUp + auto-run delivery by status + certs-auto-issued + recent errors + tagless flag) surfaced as [AutoIssueAnalyticsCard](src/components/certificates/auto-issue-analytics-card.tsx) on the certificates page "Issue" tab (polls 20s). Sweep is folded into the **cert-issue** worker job (every 3 min: sweep → enqueue → `tickAllRuns()` drains) + mirrored on the legacy `/api/cron/certificate-issues` route. Migration `20260625160000_cert_survey_auto_issue` (all additive/nullable/idempotent — two NOT-NULL drops on issuer cols are blue-green safe). **Known limit:** a registration is swept once (`certAutoIssueCheckedAt` stamp); flagging a template auto-issue **after** someone surveyed needs **manual Issue** to cover them — flag before surveys go out. +12 tests (suite 1651). **Verify on prod:** flag a template + tag, complete a test survey for a tagged reg, confirm the cert renders+emails within minutes + the card reflects it.

- **Speaker-as-Attendee: companion registration (Phase 0) + certs-in-activity + faculty stats sweep (June 25, 2026)** — Foundational work so a speaker (organizer-added faculty) receives **everything a registration receives** — badge, entry barcode, **DTCM barcode**, **check-in**, **survey** — and (the motivating goal) can later hold **multiple role-specific CME certificates**. Plan: [docs/SPEAKER_AS_ATTENDEE_PLAN.md](docs/SPEAKER_AS_ATTENDEE_PLAN.md). **The model:** a speaker gets a **companion Registration** (the "attendee facet"), reusing the existing attendee machinery rather than duplicating it onto Speaker. Decided after the owner clarified speakers DO attend (earlier "speakers are independent of registrations" held only for the *entry path*, not the facilities). **Phase 0 (commit `20b0e4f`):** additive migration `20260625120000_add_tickettype_isfaculty` — `TicketType.isFaculty` (hidden from public registration + excluded from paid capacity) + `RegistrationCreatedSource.SPEAKER_COMPANION`. New [src/lib/speaker-companion.ts](src/lib/speaker-companion.ts): `ensureFacultyTicketType` (find-or-create a hidden comp/uncapped "Faculty" type) + `ensureSpeakerCompanionRegistration` (**idempotent**: already-linked → link a same-email registration → else **create** a Faculty companion with `qrCode` minted, `COMPLIMENTARY`, `CONFIRMED`, `badgeType:"Faculty"`, **no `soldCount` increment**) + a batch helper. Wired into **every** speaker-add path: `createSpeaker` service (REST POST + MCP `create_speaker`), CSV import, import-contacts, MCP `create_speakers_bulk`; `import-registrations` already links (the registration IS the companion). All **failure-isolated** (a hiccup never fails the speaker create). The link reuses `Speaker.sourceRegistrationId`. [scripts/backfill-speaker-companion-registrations.ts](scripts/backfill-speaker-companion-registrations.ts) (dry-run default, `--write`, idempotent) backfills existing speakers — **operator-run after deploy**. **Faculty stats sweep (Phase 0e, commit `c988e64`):** new [src/lib/faculty-filter.ts](src/lib/faculty-filter.ts) `EXCLUDE_FACULTY_WHERE` (keyed on `ticketType.isFaculty` via `NOT`, so a speaker who is ALSO a real delegate still counts) applied to **all delegate-focused counts**: cached `EventStats`, the dashboard "Registrations" tile (filtered relation `_count`), `event-analytics.ts`, MCP `get_event_dashboard`/`get_event_stats` + the registrations-summary resource, the webinar "registered" KPI, and the org-wide dashboard count. Revenue was already faculty-safe (faculty have no PAID payments); the tier breakdown already excludes them (null `pricingTierId`); **badge/check-in/survey/DTCM keep faculty** (the whole point). The registrations list API now exposes `ticketType.isFaculty` so the UI can badge/filter. **Certs-in-activity (commit `db79542`):** issued certificates now appear in the unified **Activity timeline** (Award icon, "Certificate of Appreciation/Attendance issued", serial, **Open** link → PDF in a new tab; Revoked badge when revoked) — consistent across the **speaker page AND the registration detail sheet's Activity tab** via a shared builder ([src/lib/activity-feed.ts](src/lib/activity-feed.ts)) that resolves the speaker↔registration counterpart, so a person who is BOTH sees one feed ("From speaker"/"From registration" badges). `SpeakerActivityCard` → generic [`ActivityTimelineCard`](src/components/activity/activity-timeline-card.tsx) + a new `GET .../registrations/[id]/activity`. **Open Phase-0 follow-ups (deferred):** a "Faculty vs delegate" split tile + a faculty filter toggle in the registrations list UI; speaker→companion name/profile edit sync. **Phase 1 SHIPPED (multi-role certs):** **1a** (commit `bc09c0c`, migration `20260625140000_cert_per_template_uniqueness`) — `IssuedCertificate` uniqueness swapped per-type → **per-template** (`@@unique([eventId, certificateTemplateId, registrationId|speakerId])`; the one non-additive but **verified-collision-free** migration), so **one person can hold several role-specific certs** (Speaker + Moderator + Organizing Committee); eligibility + worker dup-recovery re-keyed to `certificateTemplateId`. **1b** (commit `de008b3`, package 0.4.9→0.4.10) — additive `CertificateTemplate.role` + `cmeHours`; `resolveTokens` resolves `{{cmeHours}}` from `template.cmeHours ?? event.cmeHours` (per-template override) + a new `{{role}}` token; REST POST/PATCH + MCP `create_/update_certificate_template` accept `role`/`cmeHours`; Role + CME-hours inputs in the template editor (CME hours entered manually per template; issuance stays tag-driven). **Phases 2–3 (planned):** survey-completion auto-issue (enqueue → existing cert worker; works for speakers now via their companion), manual override (mostly exists). All verified tsc/eslint/vitest 1638/build green.

- **Speaker Activity timeline + pointer to source registration; speaker audit-gap closure; P1 backlog batch (June 24–25, 2026)** — A speaker-focused review ("what activity is recorded vs not") plus follow-on work. **(1) Speaker audit gaps closed** (commit `8892903`) — 6 speaker mutations were writing no `AuditLog` row; added fire-and-forget audit entries (matching the existing speaker shape + `ipAddress`): public agreement **acceptance** (token-based, `SPEAKER_AGREEMENT_ACCEPTED`, `actor:"SPEAKER"`, `userId:null`, IP captured — the legally meaningful event, previously only the row timestamp + a pino line), **bulk tags** (one `UPDATE`/op with mode/tags/ids — tags drive email cohorts + cert eligibility), the **3 speaker imports** (CSV / from-contacts / from-registrations → bulk `CREATE`), and **panelist sync-speakers** (`PANELIST_SYNC` on the ZoomMeeting). The organizer agreement PATCH already audited (an earlier review miscounted it — the fire-and-forget `db.auditLog`↵`.create()` spans two lines, so a one-line grep missed it). **(2) Speaker ↔ Registration link + unified Activity timeline** (commit `5b62671`, **includes an additive migration**) — speakers stay **first-class + independent** (a sponsor/society-suggested speaker need not be a registrant — many are manually added and never register), but when a speaker *did* come from a registration the two are now linked **pointed, not duplicated**: new nullable `Speaker.sourceRegistrationId` FK (`SetNull` on delete, set on the import-registrations path; migration `20260624140000_add_speaker_source_registration`, additive/idempotent/blue-green-safe). New `GET /api/events/[eventId]/speakers/[speakerId]/activity` merges (newest-first) the speaker's own `AuditLog` + `EmailLog` **and** — if linked — the registration's `AuditLog` + `EmailLog`. The link resolves by the pointer, else a **read-time email match** (covers speakers imported before the column + any speaker who's also a registrant). New [`SpeakerActivityCard`](src/components/speakers/speaker-activity-card.tsx) on the speaker page (replaces the email-only `EmailLogCard` it subsumes) renders the timeline with per-event icons, Sent/Failed badges, and a **"From registration"** badge on linked-registration items. **Roadmap** scopes the future **Person/Contact identity hub** (Option B) with the hard constraint that it must be `Speaker → Person?` (optional), never `Speaker → Attendee` (required), so independent speakers never break. **(3) P1 correctness backlog batch** — **P1.2** (commit `0786480`) HTML-escape `{{abstractTitle}}` in the cert cover-email HTML body (stored-XSS: speaker-authored title was interpolated raw; new `escapeDynamic` flag escapes the resolver-internal abstractTitle that the caller's pre-escaping couldn't reach; +2 tests). **P1.4** (commit `7081533`) payment-confirmation email breakdown vars now come from the canonical `computeRegistrationFinancials` (the inline `basePrice*taxRate` ignored the promo discount + skipped round2; the default template renders `{{amount}}` so the default email is unchanged — only custom-template breakdown vars are corrected, + a `discountBlock` row). **P1.1** (`PricingTier.soldCount` double-leak) was investigated + **deferred** — it's a multi-file live-capacity routing fix (the register increment routes to tier-vs-ticketType but cancel/delete/type-change/bulk-type/MCP unconditionally decrement the ticketType → tier leaks up + ticketType leaks down); full analysis + fix plan + a one-time reconciliation-script follow-up are in [docs/ROADMAP.md](docs/ROADMAP.md) "P1.1 detail". Also shipped this session: the **survey-completed checkbox + timestamp** on the registration detail sheet (commit `5aaffa7`) and the **cert Issue → template-email** switch (commit `f3f2728`). All batches verified tsc/eslint/vitest 1632/build green. **`AuditLog` still has no global UI reader** — the speaker Activity card is the first surface to read it; a broader audit viewer remains a follow-up.

- **Registration "open/closed" master toggle now enforced + branded closed page (June 24, 2026)** — The Settings → Registration **"Registration Open"** switch (`Event.settings.registrationOpen`) already existed and saved, but was a **no-op** — nothing on the public side read it. Now it's a real master close-registration control (mirrors Publish Agenda / Allow Abstract Submissions): when **off**, the whole public register flow shows "Registration Closed" **regardless of which pricing tiers (Early Bird/Standard/Onsite) are active** — the master switch wins. Wiring: the public event API ([public/events/[slug]/route.ts](src/app/api/public/events/%5Bslug%5D/route.ts)) now exposes `registrationOpen` (default **true** when the field is absent, so existing events aren't accidentally closed); the smart-redirect page ([e/[slug]/register/page.tsx](src/app/e/%5Bslug%5D/register/page.tsx)) skips the tier redirect and renders the **branded** "Registration Closed" page (event banner + info strip + a disabled "Registration Closed" CTA — previously this closed state was an unbranded bare card); the category page ([e/[slug]/register/[category]/page.tsx](src/app/e/%5Bslug%5D/register/%5Bcategory%5D/page.tsx)) folds the switch into `isClosed` (closed card + disabled CTA). **Server-side enforcement (defense in depth):** `POST /api/public/events/[slug]/register` now returns **403 `REGISTRATION_CLOSED`** when the switch is off, so a direct POST can't bypass the closed UI; the event `select` adds `settings`, the guard logs `public/register:registration-closed`. **Admin "Add Registration" (dashboard) is unaffected** — staff can still register people while public registration is closed (the switch governs only the public self-service flow). User-guide §14 (Event Settings → Registration) documents it. tsc/eslint/vitest 1630/build green.

- **Zoom embed React-19 crash fixed via CDN loader (June 23, 2026, producer-reported)** — A live webinar showed *"Couldn't load the embedded meeting / Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'ReactCurrentOwner')"*. **Root cause:** `@zoom/meetingsdk@6.0.0`'s `/embedded` UMD does **not** inline React — it externalizes `require("react")`/`require("react-dom")` and reads React-18's internal `ReactCurrentOwner`, which **React 19 removed**. The bundler resolved those externals to the app's React 19 → crash. (The long-standing note claiming "the SDK's bundled React 18 is isolated" was **wrong** for this version; corrected in memory.) **Fix:** new [src/lib/zoom/load-embedded-sdk.ts](src/lib/zoom/load-embedded-sdk.ts) `loadZoomMtgEmbedded()` loads the SDK + its **own React 18** from `source.zoom.us` (CDN) as isolated browser globals (`window.React`=18, `window.ZoomMtgEmbedded`) — Zoom's documented React-app integration, not a hack. The Next app keeps importing React 19 via the module graph, so they never collide. [ZoomWebEmbed](src/components/zoom/zoom-web-embed.tsx) now calls the loader at both mount + cleanup (same `ZoomMtgEmbedded` API, lifecycle unchanged). **Switchable** via `NEXT_PUBLIC_ZOOM_EMBED_LOADER`: `"cdn"` (default, works under React 19) vs `"npm"` (the bundled `import "@zoom/meetingsdk/embedded"` path — kept so we can flip back with **one env var, no code change** the moment Zoom ships a React-19-compatible SDK). CDN v6.0.0 URLs (react/react-dom/redux/redux-thunk/lodash vendor scripts + `zoom-meeting-embedded-6.0.0.min.js`) verified 200 + React 18.2.0. No app-level CSP blocks them (only `frame-ancestors 'self'`). tsc/eslint/vitest 1618/build green — **runtime join is best verified on prod after deploy** (a real meeting + signature is needed). Client View remains unsupported.

- **Webinar attendee join-flow fixes + waiting-room poster fallback (June 23, 2026, producer-reported)** — Two live-webinar bugs a producer hit on "Webinar 1", plus a lobby polish. Pushed `4b29784` (fixes) + `2c53ca4` (poster); tsc/eslint/vitest 1618/build green; **takes effect on web deploy.** **(1) Attendee "Join Webinar" email CTA went straight to Zoom** — bypassing our gated session page + producer-controlled waiting room. Root cause: `executeBulkEmail` set the `{{joinUrl}}` template var to `zoomMeeting.joinUrl`. Now `${appUrl}/e/{slug}/session/{anchorSessionId}` ([bulk-email.ts](src/lib/bulk-email.ts)) — fixes the immediate confirmation (`sendWebinarConfirmationForRegistration`) AND the scheduled reminder/live-now emails (all route through `executeBulkEmail`; URL is built at fire time). The **panelist email** ([webinar-panelist-email.ts](src/lib/webinar-panelist-email.ts)) is unchanged — panelists/hosts correctly join Zoom directly. Note: already-delivered emails can't be changed; the fix applies to sends after deploy. **(2) Post-login redirect dumped attendees on `/my-registration`** — clicking Join while signed out → event login → after sign-in they landed on the registration portal, not the session page. Root cause: [e/[slug]/login/page.tsx](src/app/e/%5Bslug%5D/login/page.tsx) only recognized the literal `redirect` values `"registration"`/`"abstracts"`; the session page passes a full path (`/e/{slug}/session/{id}`) which fell through to `/dashboard` → role-middleware bounced the REGISTRANT to `/my-registration`. The login now honors a **safe same-origin path** redirect (single leading `/`, open-redirect guarded). **(3) Waiting-room poster fallback** ([waiting-room.tsx](src/components/webinar/waiting-room.tsx)) — three-tier lobby visual so there's never a blank/broken state: valid YouTube/Vimeo `lobbyVideoUrl` → embedded looped player; else event banner as a dimmed poster (`posterUrl={event.bannerImage}`, no new field) behind a "Waiting for the session to begin…" overlay; else dark gradient + spinner. Countdown + lobby message always render below. Docs: [docs/WEBINAR_EVENTS.md](docs/WEBINAR_EVENTS.md) (email join-URL note, attendee join path, three-tier lobby fallback).

- **Multi-tenant readiness audit (Round 2) + remediation (June 23, 2026)** — Ahead of white-label/multi-tenant work, a 3-agent adversarial audit (lenses: cross-tenant IDOR/org-scoping · RBAC/finance/auth · data-integrity/races/silent-failures) swept the API surface; findings logged as **Round 2** in [docs/PRODUCTION_AUDIT.md](docs/PRODUCTION_AUDIT.md) (#55–68: 0 BLOCKER, 5 HIGH, 5 MED, 4 LOW). All remediated in **3 verified batches** (each tsc/eslint/vitest/build clean), pushed to `main`: **batch 1 HIGH `bfc7596`**, **batch 2 MED/LOW `ce8737b`**, **batch 3 DATA-5 `09dab42`**, doc `a769238`. **Fixes:** **IDOR-1** promo-code GET ([promo-codes/[promoCodeId]/route.ts](src/app/api/events/%5BeventId%5D/promo-codes/%5BpromoCodeId%5D/route.ts)) now org-binds the event before exposing config + redemption PII (the PUT/DELETE already did). **RBAC-1** both `bulk-tags` PATCH routes (registrations + speakers) now call `denyReviewer` — they were the **only** event-scoped admin writes missing it (restricted roles could rewrite tags, which drive email cohorts + cert eligibility). **DATA-1** promo `usedCount` is released on registration cancel/delete (REST PUT+DELETE, MCP `update_registration` + `bulk_update_registration_status`) so a limited-use code isn't permanently exhausted after cancellations. **DATA-2/3/4** overbooking + reactivate/type-change oversell + CSV/EventsAir import races all converted from read-then-write to **atomic `updateMany` predicate guards** (`bookedRooms < totalRooms` / `soldCount < quantity`, `count===0 → error`) — the pattern `soldCount` create paths already used; the false-"atomic" comment in [accommodation-service.ts](src/services/accommodation-service.ts) is gone. **DATA-6** registration DELETE guards a possibly-shared Attendee with a sibling-count check before deleting. **DATA-5** new **`invoice-reconciliation`** worker job ([src/lib/invoice-reconciliation-worker.ts](src/lib/invoice-reconciliation-worker.ts), 10-min, advisory-lock 1006, +5 tests) recovers PAID registrations whose post-payment invoice the Stripe webhook's detached block dropped (PAID + PAID `Payment` + no `INVOICE` → re-run `createPaidInvoice`+`sendInvoiceEmail`; idempotent, 25/tick, 14-day look-back) — **needs worker redeploy to run**. **FIN-1** added `totalPrice` to `FINANCIAL_KEYS` + accommodation/hotel GET redact prices for non-finance roles (defense-in-depth — moot under the June-17 finance model where MEMBER/ONSITE are finance-capable and other roles are org-null, but future-proofs the new-roles direction). Two LOW catches now log instead of swallowing. **Two findings were FALSE POSITIVES** (verified against source, recorded in the doc): #56 IDOR-2 accommodation roomType wasn't exploitable (pre-tx validation already binds the event — hardened anyway), and #66 import-contacts already increments soldCount. Verified each batch: tsc 0, eslint 0, vitest 1618, build 0. **Code-only — not yet deployed.**

- **Webinar waiting room — producer-gated admission, holding video, per-event viewing mode, real-time presence, 5k CDN wiring (June 23, 2026)** — The webinar attendee live-day flow is now producer-controlled and watched **on our gated session page** (no BigMarker). **Phases 1–4 + a two-agent adversarial review** (commits `9229409`, `89d9c83`, then review fixes `ebf766b` / `9cdac92` / `517e1d4`; docs `f09fe30`). **(1) Lobby config + producer "Open the room"** — `WebinarSettings` ([src/lib/webinar.ts](src/lib/webinar.ts)) gained `viewingMode` (`"zoom"` embed vs `"hls"` custom stream), `lobbyVideoUrl` (YouTube/Vimeo holding video — host-allowlisted by [src/lib/webinar/lobby-video.ts](src/lib/webinar/lobby-video.ts), only `youtube-nocookie.com`/`player.vimeo.com` embeds, no arbitrary iframe), `lobbyMessage`; all in `Event.settings.webinar` JSON (no schema change). New **`POST /api/events/[eventId]/webinar/room`** `{open}` sets the **anchor `EventSession.status`** → `LIVE`/`COMPLETED` (the room-open source of truth — re-openable). Console **LobbyCard** ([webinar/page.tsx](src/app/(dashboard)/events/%5BeventId%5D/webinar/page.tsx)) has the mode toggle, video URL, message, and the **"Open the room / Go live" ↔ "Close the room"** button + `Room OPEN/closed` badge. **(2) Waiting room** — new [src/components/webinar/waiting-room.tsx](src/components/webinar/waiting-room.tsx) (countdown + looped holding video + message), shown when `eventType===WEBINAR` + a confirmed registrant + room not open + `!isPast`. New **public, cached** `GET .../sessions/[sessionId]/lobby-status` (single query session→event, **3s per-container micro-cache** so 5k pollers collapse to ~1 DB hit/3s; DRAFT events auto-open). The session page ([e/[slug]/session/[sessionId]/page.tsx](src/app/e/%5Bslug%5D/session/%5BsessionId%5D/page.tsx)) polls it (~15–20s jittered) and on `roomOpen` **re-mints** join creds (a page-load signature is likely expired after a long lobby wait) then auto-mounts the embed (`zoom`) or `LivePlayer` (`hls`), with a "Join now" CTA fallback; the admit latch resets on close (re-open re-admits) and on failed re-fetch (retry); the HLS view stays mounted past the scheduled end while the room is open (overrun). **(3) Real-time presence** — new **`WebinarPresence`** table (migration `20260623000000_add_webinar_presence`, additive/blue-green-safe) + write-once `Registration.webinarFirstJoinedAt`. **`POST .../sessions/[sessionId]/presence`** heartbeat (auth + registration-gated, org staff skipped) is an **`upsert`** (INSERT…ON CONFLICT, NO interactive transaction — two-tab first-beats can't P2002, no held connection at 5k), escalate-lobby→joined-only; client beats ~30–40s, paused when hidden. **`GET /api/events/[eventId]/webinar/presence`** (org-scoped) → who's present in the last 60s split lobby/joined → console **"Live now"** card; **"Joined"** badge on the registrations list. This is OUR-page presence, **distinct from post-event `ZoomAttendance`**. **(4) 5k stream** — HLS playback is CDN-aware via `HLS_CDN_BASE` (CloudFront) with app-origin fallback (in `stream-status` + `zoom-join`); `stream-status` keeps probing the MediaMTX origin (cached 3s so 5k pollers share one probe); `LivePlayer` fails over CDN→origin once then resumes the recovery poll (auto-reconnect, not a dead-end); nginx `/stream/` origin proxy committed to [deploy/nginx.conf](deploy/nginx.conf); operator-run CloudFront + Singapore-DR failover steps in [docs/LIVE_STREAMING.md §13](docs/LIVE_STREAMING.md). Docs: [docs/WEBINAR_EVENTS.md](docs/WEBINAR_EVENTS.md) "Waiting room…" section + user-guide S11 live-day flow. **Deferred (in [docs/ROADMAP.md](docs/ROADMAP.md) backlog):** never-opened-room warning (decision: keep manual-open), operator visibility (DRAFT auto-open vs PUBLISHED), save-time hls/stream validation, `lobby-status` eventType gate, stale-badge, Redis rate limiter. **Operator prerequisites:** Zoom **Active SDK Mode dev→Production** + add the prod domain to the Marketplace embed allowlist (for the embed mode); verify the box's nginx `/stream/`; provision CloudFront+DR before a real 5k stream. The session page ([e/[slug]/session/[sessionId]/page.tsx](src/app/e/%5Bslug%5D/session/%5BsessionId%5D/page.tsx)) polls it (~15–20s jittered) and on `roomOpen` **re-mints** join creds (a page-load signature is likely expired after a long lobby wait) then auto-mounts the embed (`zoom`) or `LivePlayer` (`hls`), with a "Join now" CTA fallback; the admit latch resets on close (re-open re-admits) and on failed re-fetch (retry); the HLS view stays mounted past the scheduled end while the room is open (overrun). **(3) Real-time presence** — new **`WebinarPresence`** table (migration `20260623000000_add_webinar_presence`, additive/blue-green-safe) + write-once `Registration.webinarFirstJoinedAt`. **`POST .../sessions/[sessionId]/presence`** heartbeat (auth + registration-gated, org staff skipped) is an **`upsert`** (INSERT…ON CONFLICT, NO interactive transaction — two-tab first-beats can't P2002, no held connection at 5k), escalate-lobby→joined-only; client beats ~30–40s, paused when hidden. **`GET /api/events/[eventId]/webinar/presence`** (org-scoped) → who's present in the last 60s split lobby/joined → console **"Live now"** card; **"Joined"** badge on the registrations list. This is OUR-page presence, **distinct from post-event `ZoomAttendance`**. **(4) 5k stream** — HLS playback is CDN-aware via `HLS_CDN_BASE` (CloudFront) with app-origin fallback (in `stream-status` + `zoom-join`); `stream-status` keeps probing the MediaMTX origin (cached 3s so 5k pollers share one probe); `LivePlayer` fails over CDN→origin once then resumes the recovery poll (auto-reconnect, not a dead-end); nginx `/stream/` origin proxy committed to [deploy/nginx.conf](deploy/nginx.conf); operator-run CloudFront + Singapore-DR failover steps in [docs/LIVE_STREAMING.md §13](docs/LIVE_STREAMING.md). Docs: [docs/WEBINAR_EVENTS.md](docs/WEBINAR_EVENTS.md) "Waiting room…" section + user-guide S11 live-day flow. **Deferred (in [docs/ROADMAP.md](docs/ROADMAP.md) backlog):** never-opened-room warning (decision: keep manual-open), operator visibility (DRAFT auto-open vs PUBLISHED), save-time hls/stream validation, `lobby-status` eventType gate, stale-badge, Redis rate limiter. **Operator prerequisites:** Zoom **Active SDK Mode dev→Production** + add the prod domain to the Marketplace embed allowlist (for the embed mode); verify the box's nginx `/stream/`; provision CloudFront+DR before a real 5k stream. Verified each step: tsc 0, eslint 0, vitest 1613, build 0.

The invite dialog now offers two **Account setup** modes (new users only): **(a) Send email invite** — unchanged; **(b) Set password now** — the admin types a password; the account is created **active + `emailVerified`** with that password and **NO email/token**, and the admin hands over the email+password for immediate sign-in. **Backend** ([organization/users/route.ts](src/app/api/organization/users/route.ts)): `POST` accepts an optional `password` (min 8); when present **and the email is new** (the promote branch still wins for an existing account) it creates the user directly (bcrypt hash, `emailVerified: now`), audits `CREATE_USER` with `mode: "password"`, logs `organization/users:created-with-password`, and returns `passwordSet: true` (201). - **ONSITE registration-desk role + internal-domain org membership + promote-on-invite (June 16, 2026)** — A new org-bound **Onsite Staff** role for the registration desk, plus the identity-model changes that make it usable for internal people who first signed up as attendees. **(1) ONSITE role** (`2dbe811`) — see the RBAC section above for the full enforcement matrix. Org-bound; can ONLY add a registration, check attendees in (~~+undo~~ — **undo was never implemented**, see the RBAC section), view the registrations list, and print badges; money hidden (like MEMBER — **also since corrected: MEMBER/ONSITE are finance-capable**). `denyReviewer` gained an `{ allow }` list so the create/check-in/badge routes opt ONSITE back in while the other 27 write routes block it; middleware ([src/proxy.ts](src/proxy.ts)) confines ONSITE to `/events` + an event's `/registrations*`+`/check-in*`; sidebar/header/list/detail-sheet all gate accordingly. Additive enum migration `20260616120000_add_onsite_role`. **(2) Invite "already exists" no longer silent** (`257c5fa`) — `POST /api/organization/users` returned a bare 400 with no log when the email matched a non-team account; it now logs `organization/users:invite-email-in-use` and returns a 409 that names the case. - **Communications bulk-email filter correctness pass (June 16, 2026)** — Two rounds fixing the registrations/Communications bulk-email filters. **Round 1 — payment filter was silently dropped on "Email All" (`26f8c50`).** The registrations list applies its **Payment Status** filter to the visible rows + the recipient count, but the `BulkEmailDialog` mount passed `statusFilter` + `ticketTypeFilter` and **omitted `paymentStatusFilter`** — so the dialog's payment control defaulted to "all" and an "Email All" send went to every registration matching status/ticket, ignoring payment entirely (backend filtering was always correct; this was a UI wiring gap). [registrations/page.tsx](src/app/%28dashboard%29/events/%5BeventId%5D/registrations/page.tsx) now passes `paymentStatusFilter={paymentFilter}`, and [bulk-email-dialog.tsx](src/components/bulk-email-dialog.tsx) re-seeds its `localPaymentFilter` from the prop on every closed→open transition (it previously seeded only on first mount, so reopening after changing the list filter used a stale value). **Round 2 — review of the remaining filter findings (`50e27b6`).** A review of the whole chain (page filters → tiles → dialog payload → backend `where`) surfaced four issues, all on the display/wiring side (backend application was correct + zod-validated): **(#1+#4) misleading recipient count** — the dialog showed the page's *advanced-filter* total even when a workflow tile or the in-dialog payment dropdown targeted a different cohort (*"Send to all 200"* while a tile sent to 30). Fixed with a new optional **`recipientCountFor(filters)`** callback on the dialog: each page hands it a **pure count function over its already-loaded rows**, so "all"-mode sends always show the true number for the current effective filters (`BulkEmailEffectiveFilters` = status/paymentStatus/ticketTypeId/agreementSigned/hasSession/sessionRole). Wired on Communications (registrations + speakers), the registrations list, and the speakers list; selected-mode count unchanged. The list-page count **mirrors SEND semantics** (status+payment+ticket) and deliberately **excludes the free-text search box** (the backend can't filter on it, so counting it would over-report vs the actual send). **(#2) "Welcome Paid" tile silently narrowed** — its badge counted PAID+COMPLIMENTARY+INCLUSIVE but the send was `paymentStatus: "PAID"` only. `paymentStatus` now accepts a **comma-separated multi-value list** → `parsePaymentStatusFilter()` in [bulk-email.ts](src/lib/bulk-email.ts) resolves it to a Prisma `IN`; the tile sends `PAID,COMPLIMENTARY,INCLUSIVE` so **count == send**. The dialog renders a **synthetic Select option** for a multi-value (so the trigger isn't blank); picking a single status overrides it. **(#3) payment dropdowns are enum-driven** — the Communications advanced dropdown + the dialog's both build from `PAYMENT_STATUS_DISPLAY_ORDER` / `PAYMENT_STATUS_LABELS` (from [registration-enums.ts](src/app/%28dashboard%29/events/%5BeventId%5D/registrations/registration-enums.ts)), so UNASSIGNED/PENDING/INCLUSIVE/REFUNDED/FAILED are now selectable (were hardcoded to PAID/UNPAID/COMPLIMENTARY; INCLUSIVE was absent from both). **Tests** +6 (`parsePaymentStatusFilter` single/multi/trim+drop-invalid/empty; schema accepts a comma list; payment-filter prop pass-through). Verified across both rounds: tsc 0, eslint 0, vitest 1570/1570, build 0. Commits `26f8c50` + `50e27b6`.

- **Active custom email templates are now sendable + test-email `{{registrationId}}` is real (June 16, 2026)** — Two bundled fixes to the Communications email flow. **(1) Custom templates were orphaned.** An organizer could create + activate a custom template under Communications → Email Templates, but it never appeared as a sendable option anywhere: the bulk-email dialog and Communications tiles offered a **hardcoded** list of built-in types, and [executeBulkEmail](src/lib/bulk-email.ts)'s `slugMap` threw *"…is not supported"* for any non-default slug. Now a new **`emailType: "template"`** carries the saved template's slug in **`filters.templateSlug`** — riding inside `filters` (the same round-trip trick as `surveyExpiryDays`) so **scheduled** sends reconstruct it from the persisted `ScheduledEmail.filters` JSON with **NO new column and NO worker change**. The shared `bulkEmailSchema` gained a `superRefine` requiring `templateSlug` when `emailType === "template"`, so both the immediate ([emails/bulk](src/app/api/events/%5BeventId%5D/emails/bulk/route.ts)) and schedule ([emails/schedule](src/app/api/events/%5BeventId%5D/emails/schedule/route.ts)) routes reject a malformed payload before persisting a row. Resolution uses `getEventTemplate(eventId, slug)` which returns the row **only when active** — an inactive/missing custom slug **hard-fails with a clear 400** (no system default to fall back to) instead of blasting a batch with an empty body; system slugs keep their default fallback. Renders with the same per-recipient variables as the built-in sends. **UI:** [bulk-email-dialog.tsx](src/components/bulk-email-dialog.tsx) fetches the event's active templates (via `useEmailTemplates`) and adds each custom one as a selectable **"Your saved template"** option (`value = template:<slug>`) for **every** recipient type — so it surfaces in the **Email All** flow on registrations + speakers AND in Communications (the shared dialog). [communications/page.tsx](src/app/%28dashboard%29/events/%5BeventId%5D/communications/page.tsx) also surfaces them as one-click **"Your templates"** tiles under the Registrations + Speakers cards. New **client-safe** [src/lib/email-template-slugs.ts](src/lib/email-template-slugs.ts) classifies system-vs-custom slugs without importing the server-only `email.ts` (a drift vitest asserts the mirror == `DEFAULT_TEMPLATES`). `useBulkEmail`'s stale `emailType`/`filters` types were widened. **(2) Test/preview `{{registrationId}}`** now pulls the most-recent real registration's confirmation number (padded serial, e.g. `007`, else last-8 of the id), **falling back to the static `"9999"`** when the event has no registrations — matching how `eventName`/dates/venue already render real event data via [buildEventPreviewVariables](src/lib/email.ts) (pure-sample `getSamplePreviewVariables` still uses `ABCD1234`). Both the template test/preview POST and the email-preview route now `select` one registration (`id` + `serialId`, most recent). **Tests:** +11 (template-slug drift + classification; `bulkEmailSchema` template-send contract; registrationId real-serial / serial-less / no-registration "9999"). Verified: tsc 0, eslint 0, vitest 1565/1565, build 0. Commits `0dbfc77` (custom-template sendable) + `7300ed4` (registrationId).

Auth documented as the `mmg_`-prefixed org key via `x-api-key` **or** `Authorization: Bearer`. **Creates** for events/speakers/registrations are **session-only** (dashboard) or via **MCP** (JSON-RPC, see [docs/MCP_REFERENCE.md](docs/MCP_REFERENCE.md)) — only contacts is REST-writable, so the doc is read + contacts-CRUD and cross-links MCP for the rest. **Enabling change:** `GET /api/events/[eventId]/sessions` was **session-only**; added API-key (`getOrgContext`) auth so the program is fetchable programmatically (same trust level as the existing speakers/registrations key GETs — org-scoped, admin-issued key, the org's own data). The docs *page* is public to view (sharing is the point); a key is still required to *call* anything. - **Hybrid events: in-person vs virtual attendance choice (June 12, 2026)** — On `eventType === "HYBRID"` events, registrants choose to attend **at the venue or online**. In-person is unchanged (entry barcode + badge + check-in). **Virtual gets NO barcode/badge**, is **uncapped** (doesn't consume the ticket-type `soldCount`, so a sold-out venue still takes virtual signups), is priced via a **flat per-ticket `virtualPrice`** (`null` ⇒ falls back to the in-person price; pricing tiers apply to in-person only in v1), and its **confirmation email replaces the barcode block with a "joining instructions will be sent" message** (the barcode also self-skips on the null qrCode). **Settled product decisions:** choice shown on HYBRID only; virtual uncapped; virtual priced separately (flat); joining instructions sent **manually via Communications** in v1 (the email just promises them — no automated sender yet). **Schema** (additive migration `20260612000000_add_attendance_mode`, blue-green safe): `enum AttendanceMode { IN_PERSON, VIRTUAL }`, `Registration.attendanceMode` (default IN_PERSON, `@@index([eventId, attendanceMode])`), `TicketType.virtualPrice Decimal?`. **Core logic in [registration-service.ts](src/services/registration-service.ts)** (backs admin REST + MCP): qrCode minted only for in-person; soldCount increment + sold-out guard skipped for virtual; effective price = `virtualPrice ?? price` for virtual; virtual **always** sends the confirmation (even free) so the joining message lands; free-virtual defaults COMPLIMENTARY. **Public path**: the register route ([register/route.ts](src/app/api/public/events/%5Bslug%5D/register/route.ts)) mirrors the same qrCode/soldCount/price logic + skips the sold-out gate for virtual; the public event API exposes `eventType` + `virtualPrice`; the **register form** ([register/[category]/page.tsx](src/app/e/%5Bslug%5D/register/%5Bcategory%5D/page.tsx)) shows an In-Person/Virtual selector (HYBRID only) with mode-aware pricing. **Email** ([email.ts](src/lib/email.ts)): `attendanceMode` param drives the virtual joining-instructions block. **Admin/reporting**: REST POST accepts `attendanceMode`→service; badge generation **excludes virtual** registrations; the registrations list shows a **Virtual** badge. **Tests**: +6 service cases. Verified tsc/eslint/vitest 1546/build all clean. **Follow-on (`957abab`, bump 0.4.9):** wired `attendanceMode` through the three remaining create paths — the **admin full-page Add Registration form** (In-Person/Virtual picker shown only on HYBRID events), **MCP `create_registration`** (validated `attendanceMode` param on executor + tool defs), and **CSV import** (optional `attendanceMode` column; VIRTUAL rows skip capacity/soldCount + get no qrCode; template/hint updated). +2 MCP parity tests (suite 1548). **Still deferred** (tracked in [docs/ROADMAP.md](docs/ROADMAP.md) "Hybrid attendance follow-ups"): the notable one is **admin mode-change qrCode minting** (switching a reg virtual→in-person must lazily mint a qrCode — the one correctness gap); also the quick-add dialog picker, check-in UI hiding, dashboard in/virtual split, registrant-portal mode display, tier-windowed virtual pricing, and gating virtual attendance certificates on Zoom attendance.

- **DDoS/bot hardening: WAF audit + live nginx rate limiting (June 10, 2026)** — Follow-on to the Cloudflare removal. **WAF audit (read-only):** confirmed there is **no AWS WAF** anywhere in the account (`803726282629`) — empty across WAFv2 Regional (ap-south-1 + ap-southeast-1), WAFv2 CloudFront scope, and WAF Classic — and **no ALB/CloudFront** for one to attach to (AWS WAF can't bind to a bare EC2). On-box check (via SSM) found **no ModSecurity** (nginx not built with it), **fail2ban with only an `sshd` jail** (SSH brute-force; does NOT watch HTTP), and **ufw active but open on 22/80/443**. So the prior belief that "a WAF is set up on the EC2" was a mix-up with fail2ban/ufw. **Shipped: nginx per-IP rate limiting** ([deploy/nginx.conf](deploy/nginx.conf), commits `958139c`+`0a6283f`, **applied live on the box**) — `limit_req_zone`/`limit_conn_zone` keyed on `$binary_remote_addr` (the true client IP, since no proxy is in front): `rate=100r/s burst=200 nodelay` on `location /`, `burst=50` on `/api/mcp`, `limit_conn 100` per IP, 429 on exceed; `/_next/static/` + `/stream/` HLS deliberately un-limited. Runs **before** Node and **survives app restarts** (the in-app `checkRateLimit` is in-memory + per-container). Thresholds tuned for the **shared-NAT** case (event attendees behind one venue-WiFi IP) — raise for very large single-NAT crowds. **Note:** the live `/etc/nginx/sites-available/ea-sys` is a stripped Certbot-managed file that has **diverged from the committed `deploy/nginx.conf`** — the box is the source of truth for nginx config; the git file is a reference. **fail2ban nginx jail** ([infra/fail2ban/](infra/fail2ban/README.md), filter + jail + idempotent `setup.sh`) — bans IPs that repeatedly trip the nginx 429 limit (default 100+ in 120s → 30-min ban); complements the existing `sshd` jail; thresholds tuned high for the shared-NAT case; **applied + verified live on the box** (status shows `File list: /var/log/nginx/error.log`). **Gotcha fixed during rollout:** the box's `/etc/fail2ban/jail.d/defaults-debian.conf` sets `backend = systemd` globally, so the jail first read the journal and ignored the nginx file — the jail now forces `backend = auto` to watch `/var/log/nginx/error.log`. Operator office egress IP whitelisted in `ignoreip`. Installer is `bash infra/fail2ban/setup.sh` (not auto-deployed; applied manually via SSM). **Docs:** new [docs/AWS_OPERATIONS.md](docs/AWS_OPERATIONS.md) §4 "Security — DDoS/bot posture" documents the full verified inventory + live nginx limiting (§4.1) + the fail2ban jail (§4.2) + a complete **"adding Cloudflare later"** playbook (§4.3 — the nginx `real_ip` / `set_real_ip_from` approach needs **zero app-code changes**; the SG-lock-must-come-after-proxy ordering; the full change checklist). Also reflected in [docs/HANDOVER.md](docs/HANDOVER.md) (Rate Limiting + Recent Additions) and [docs/SUPPORT_AND_MAINTENANCE.md](docs/SUPPORT_AND_MAINTENANCE.md) §7. Deferred follow-ups: Turnstile on public forms, Redis-backed shared rate limiter.

- **Cloudflare removed everywhere + `getClientIp` spoofing fix (June 10, 2026)** — Decision: **EA-SYS does not use Cloudflare or any CDN/proxy**, for prod *or* the Singapore DR box. DNS points the A record directly at the box's Elastic IP; the origin is directly exposed (nginx → Docker). **Security fix (the important part):** [src/lib/security.ts](src/lib/security.ts) `getClientIp()` previously trusted `CF-Connecting-IP` first, then the **first** `X-Forwarded-For` entry — both **client-spoofable on a directly-exposed origin**, so an attacker could send a forged header to get a different rate-limit key per request and **bypass IP rate limiting entirely**. Now it prefers nginx's `X-Real-IP` (set to `$remote_addr`, the real socket peer, overwriting any client value), falls back to the **last** `X-Forwarded-For` entry (nginx appends the real peer via `$proxy_add_x_forwarded_for`; earlier entries are client-controlled), and **never** trusts `CF-Connecting-IP`. Tests assert the secure precedence + two explicit anti-spoofing cases ([__tests__/lib/security.test.ts](__tests__/lib/security.test.ts)). **Docs/infra swept:** [infra/dr](infra/dr) terraform + README reworded (DR SG opens 80/443 via `http_allow_cidrs` default-wide-open, direct DNS, no Cloudflare references); [docs/EC2_HARDENING.html](docs/EC2_HARDENING.html) got a top decision banner + Step 2 marked DROPPED + Step 5 marked REVERTED (the `CF-Connecting-IP` patch it claimed "Done" is exactly what this reverts) + comparison-table rows corrected; minor mentions in `scripts/switch-region.sh` + `docs/MUMBAI_SETUP.md` cleaned. Current DDoS/bot posture (in-app IP rate limiting + fail2ban + nginx, no CDN) lives in [docs/AWS_OPERATIONS.md](docs/AWS_OPERATIONS.md). Verified: tsc 0, eslint 0, vitest 1540/1540, build 0.

- **Abstracts/Reviewers consistency pass + per-abstract reviewer assignment UI (June 10, 2026)** — A cross-surface review of the abstracts/reviewers area (REST vs MCP vs in-app agent vs dashboard vs public) found the core flow already sound (the status-transition gate, reviewer auth, and SUBMITTER IDOR checks are centralized + consistent) but several edge inconsistencies, fixed across two commits. **Consistency fixes (`9794bf3`, bump 0.4.7):** (1) MCP `create_review_criterion` accepted only weight 1-10 while REST allows 1-100 (weights are meant to sum to 100) — harmonized to 1-100 in create + the new update. (2) The REST `GET /abstracts` list had **no pagination cap** (returned all); added a `limit` (default 200, max 500) mirroring the MCP `list_abstracts` cap. (3) The REST list + MCP `list_abstracts` each inlined their own mean-score math; both now use a new shared `meanOverallScore()` in [src/lib/abstract-review.ts](src/lib/abstract-review.ts) (same rounding as `computeSubmissionAggregates`, operates on already-fetched scores so no N+1). (4) The submitter inline edit dialog offered only ORAL/POSTER while the full pages offered all four presentation types — now consistent via the new shared [abstract-enums.ts](src/app/%28dashboard%29/events/%5BeventId%5D/abstracts/abstract-enums.ts) (status colours, label, presentation-type options — exhaustive Prisma-enum-keyed Records). The list + edit + new pages all import it (fixes the yellow-vs-amber status-colour drift too). (5) Added the optional `additionalEmail` field to `/e/[slug]/submitAbstract` so it matches `/e/[slug]/abstract/register` (was one-way data loss by entry point). (6) Added MCP `update_review_criterion` + `delete_review_criterion` (REST had PUT/DELETE; MCP had neither) — org-scoped, weight 1-100. **Per-abstract reviewer assignment UI (`b88f243`, bump 0.4.8):** the `AbstractReviewer` table + routes + MCP tools existed but had **no dashboard UI** — organizers could only add reviewers to the event-wide pool (which sees every abstract), never assign a specific reviewer to a specific abstract with a role / COI flag. Now wired up: **backend** — `POST .../abstracts/[id]/reviewers` now **upserts** (updates role/conflictFlag on an existing assignment instead of no-opping, so the UI can flip role / toggle COI without unassign+reassign; same upsert applied to the MCP `assign_reviewer_to_abstract` executor; both audit-logged). The REST abstracts list returns `assignedReviewerCount` for a row badge. **UI** — new [AbstractReviewersCard](src/components/abstracts/abstract-reviewers-card.tsx) (admin/organizer only — self-hides for submitters via `useSession`): merges the event reviewer pool with this abstract's assignments (and surfaces reviewers explicitly assigned but NOT in the pool), with assign/unassign, a role `Select` (Primary/Secondary/Consulting), a COI `Switch`, and a submission-status badge (score / Submitted / Pending). Mounted on the abstract edit page sidebar AND in a dialog opened from a new "Reviewers" row action (with count badge) on the abstracts list. New hooks `useAbstractReviewers` / `useAssignAbstractReviewer` / `useUnassignAbstractReviewer` in `src/hooks/use-api.ts`. ~~**The COI flag is advisory in v1**~~ **⚠️ SUPERSEDED June 26, 2026:** the COI flag is now **enforcement** — a conflicted reviewer is blocked from submitting (403 `CONFLICT_OF_INTEREST`) on all three submit paths (REST submissions POST, MCP `submit_abstract_review`, MCP `admin_submit_review_on_behalf`); their review can't count toward the decision. (It still doesn't hard-gate *read* access.) **Tests:** shared `meanOverallScore` round-trip + the assign-schema + upsert-decision (no-op vs update) contract in [__tests__/lib/reviewer-access.test.ts](__tests__/lib/reviewer-access.test.ts). Suite 1532 → 1538. Both commits verified: tsc 0, eslint 0, vitest green, `npm run build` 0. MCP tool surface changed (new criteria CRUD + assign upsert) → connected MCP clients should reconnect.

- **Worker connection-pool fix: bigger pool + slower cert poller + P2024 classified (June 10, 2026)** — A 06:05 prod alert (`worker:tick-wrapper-uncaught` + connector `Prisma error`) was a Prisma **P2024** — *"Timed out fetching a new connection from the connection pool (connection limit: 3, timeout: 10s)"* — on `cert-issue`'s advisory-lock acquire `$queryRaw`. **Root cause**: the worker's Prisma pool defaults to `physical_cores × 2 + 1 = 3` (the `t3.large` is 1 physical core × 2 threads; `nproc` reports 2 but Prisma counts *physical*; `DATABASE_URL` set no explicit `connection_limit`), and at the top of a minute several jobs tick **concurrently** on that shared 3-connection pool — `cert-issue` (`* * * * *`) + `scheduled-emails` (`* * * * *`) + `webinar-recordings` (`*/5`, fires at `:05`) — so `cert-issue`'s lock-acquire waited out `pool_timeout` and threw. It **paged** because `classifyPrismaError` didn't recognize the pool-timeout message, so the P1 catch (from the EDBHANDLEREXITED fix) re-threw it to the wrapper-uncaught alert. **Not** caused by the bulk-email jobification (zero bulk activity at the time), but that change does add future worker DB load, making the pool bump worthwhile. **Three fixes**: (1) **`cert-issue` poller `* * * * *` → `*/3 * * * *`** ([worker/jobs/cert-issue.ts](worker/jobs/cert-issue.ts)) — cert issuance is post-event and not latency-critical, so a ~3-min start is fine, and it cuts this job's idle lock-acquire polls + collisions with the every-minute `scheduled-emails` by 3×. Note: `cert-issue` does **no** cert work unless an operator created a `CertificateIssueRun` — the tick is a poller that's a near-no-op (lock acquire + one "any active runs?" query) when idle; the idle poll is what got starved at 06:05, *not* actual cert load. (2) **`classifyPrismaError` now classifies "Timed out fetching a new connection from the connection pool" / `P2024` as retryable** ([src/lib/db.ts](src/lib/db.ts)) → `withJobLock` catches it on the acquire and skips the tick gracefully (warn, retries next tick) instead of paging; same shape as the EDBHANDLEREXITED fix — we'd just missed this message. (3) **Pool bump (env, applied on the box — not in git):** `DATABASE_URL` gained `&connection_limit=10&pool_timeout=15` (pool 3→10, wait-before-P2024 10s→15s).
