Shared `.env` so **web + worker both widen** (web had the same tight default-3); safe through pgbouncer (multiplexes onto a small set of real Postgres conns; ~20 client conns total, well under the pooler ceiling). `pool_timeout` kept at **15 not 20** so the user-facing web side still fails reasonably fast. **Lever reference** (for next time): `connection_limit` = concurrency headroom — the *primary* fix, but bounded by what the DB/pooler can actually serve (a huge pool just runs more slow queries at once); `pool_timeout` = patience before P2024 — *secondary*; a long value masks under-provisioning and risks slow hangs, so **size the pool, keep the timeout modest**. **Tests**: +2 ([db-error-classifier.test.ts](__tests__/lib/db-error-classifier.test.ts) P2024 case; [advisory-lock.test.ts](__tests__/lib/advisory-lock.test.ts) P1 pool-timeout skip). Suite 1530 → 1532. Verified: tsc 0, eslint 0, vitest 1532/1532, build 0. Commit `e90c989` (code); the `.env` pool bump is operational. Also corrected the stale `connection_limit=1` guidance in [.env.example](.env.example).

- **Schedule/Agenda consistency pass (June 10, 2026)** — A review of the schedule/agenda area surfaced several cross-surface inconsistencies (the same concept validated or rendered differently across REST vs MCP vs dashboard vs public vs the in-app AI Agent). Shipped to `main` in commit `53c8c52` (deployed); package bumped to 0.4.6. **New shared helper** [src/lib/event-time.ts](src/lib/event-time.ts) — isomorphic (server + client, `Intl`-only, safe for `"use client"`) event-timezone helpers: `resolveTimezone` (defaults `Asia/Dubai`), `localDateInTz`, `isSessionWithinEventDates` (local-date comparison in the event TZ), `formatTimeInTz`, `formatDateInTz`, `tzLabel`. Single source of truth so session date-validation and public time rendering all agree. **Fixes:** **(1+7) REST session create+update timezone validation** — [sessions/route.ts](src/app/api/events/%5BeventId%5D/sessions/route.ts) POST + [[sessionId]/route.ts](src/app/api/events/%5BeventId%5D/sessions/%5BsessionId%5D/route.ts) PUT validated "within event dates" with `eventStart.setHours(0,0,0,0)` — i.e. the **server's** timezone (UTC on the box) — so an early-morning (e.g. 1am Dubai = previous UTC day) or late-night boundary session was wrongly rejected, while the MCP path (which used `Intl.DateTimeFormat` in the event TZ) accepted it. Both REST paths now use the shared `isSessionWithinEventDates` (event TZ) + an explicit `endTime > startTime` check, matching MCP. **(3) Dashboard agenda honorifics** — [agenda/page.tsx](src/app/%28dashboard%29/events/%5BeventId%5D/agenda/page.tsx) rendered raw `firstName lastName` and its API omitted `title`, so "Prof. Jane Doe" on public pages showed as "Jane Doe" in the dashboard agenda. Now uses `formatPersonName(title,…)` with `title` added to every session/topic speaker `select` in the sessions routes. **(2+4) Public agenda topics + roles** — the public agenda API ([public/.../agenda/route.ts](src/app/api/public/events/%5Bslug%5D/agenda/route.ts)) didn't `select` topics or session-speaker `role`, and the page's `SessionRow` never rendered them — so the talk-level agenda and Chairperson/Moderator/Panelist labels were invisible on the main public agenda (they showed on the dashboard + single-session page). Now fetched + rendered. The public **single-session** page ([session/[sessionId]/page.tsx](src/app/e/%5Bslug%5D/session/%5BsessionId%5D/page.tsx)) already fetched `role` but never displayed it — now shows a role badge. **(8) Public times in event timezone** — the public agenda, single-session page, and the registration-page agenda preview ([speakers-agenda-preview.tsx](src/components/public/speakers-agenda-preview.tsx)) rendered session times in the **viewer's** local TZ (`date-fns format(new Date(...))`). All three now render in the **event's** timezone via `formatTimeInTz` with a short TZ label (e.g. "11:00 PM GMT+4"), and the public agenda carries a "All times shown in event time (GMT+4)" note. (Two secondary "join opens at…" countdown timestamps on the session page still render viewer-local — intentionally deferred.) **(5) In-app AI Agent session tools** — `update_session`, `add_speaker_to_session`, `remove_speaker_from_session`, `replace_session_speakers`, and `list_live_sessions_now` had executors wired into `SESSION_EXECUTORS`/`TOOL_EXECUTOR_MAP` and were all registered on the MCP HTTP server, but were **missing from `SESSION_TOOL_DEFINITIONS`** — so the in-app agent at `/events/[id]/agent` couldn't discover or call them (n8n/MCP could). Added the 5 tool definitions. **(6) MCP `create_session` parity** — the MCP create executor silently dropped `capacity` and topic `abstractId` that the REST POST persists; both are now wired through the executor, the in-app tool definition, and the MCP registration ([register-mcp-tools.ts](src/lib/agent/register-mcp-tools.ts)). **Aligned + left as-is (confirmed consistent):** cascade deletes, `sortOrder` defaults/ordering, track name+color across surfaces. **Tests:** [__tests__/lib/event-time.test.ts](__tests__/lib/event-time.test.ts) — 9 cases pinning the boundary-day validation (late-night accepted, 1am-Dubai-previous-UTC-day accepted, next/prior day rejected) + formatting. Suite 1521 → 1530. Verified: tsc 0, eslint 0, vitest 1530/1530, build 0; helper logic sanity-checked against the boundary cases.

- **Bulk email immediate-send jobified (enqueue → jobId) + retry logging (June 9, 2026)** — The immediate bulk-send route [/emails/bulk](src/app/api/events/[eventId]/emails/bulk/route.ts) no longer runs `executeBulkEmail` **inline** (N emails + per-recipient agreement-PDF generation inside the HTTP request — unbounded, could time out on a large fan-out). It now **enqueues a `ScheduledEmail` with `scheduledFor = now` and returns 202 `{ jobId, status }`**; the existing scheduled-emails worker (every minute) drains it via the SAME `executeBulkEmail`, and the caller polls the existing Scheduled Emails list. "Send now" therefore means "sends within ~60s" — the request never blocks. Reuses existing job machinery (no new worker; reference patterns are `CertificateIssueRun` + `ScheduledEmail`). **Schema**: `ScheduledEmail.recipientIds String[] @default([])` (migration `20260609130000_add_scheduled_email_recipient_ids`, `ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS` → blue-green safe) so explicitly-selected-recipient sends survive the queue — the worker forwards `recipientIds` to `executeBulkEmail` (empty array → `undefined` → filter-based resolution at fire time). The route drops the inline user lookup (worker reconstructs organizer name+signature from `createdById`) and the at-send admin notification (the worker already emits "Scheduled Email Sent" on completion). **UI**: `useBulkEmail` return type → `{ success, message, queued, jobId, status }`; the bulk-email dialog needed **no change** (it already toasts `result.message` + closes on `result.success`; the message now reads "queued, sending within ~60s", and the send appears in the Scheduled Emails list to track PENDING→PROCESSING→SENT with counts). **MCP `send_bulk_email` still sends inline** (unchanged — jobifying it would change its JSON-RPC return contract for n8n/claude.ai; deferred). **Logging — closed two retry gaps**: `retryCount` is now threaded into the worker's `scheduled-email:sent` (info) + `scheduled-email:send-failed` (error) lines, and a successful manual retry emits `scheduled-email:retried` (info, was audit-only / invisible in `/logs`). So send counts (`total`/`successCount`/`failureCount`), per-recipient + whole-row failures, and retries are all visible in `/logs`. **Behavior change (user-visible)**: "Send now" is no longer instantaneous — queued + delivered within ~60s, tracked under Scheduled Emails. **Tests**: +11 — [scheduled-emails-worker.test.ts](__tests__/lib/scheduled-emails-worker.test.ts) (recipientIds + retryCount passthrough, SENT counts) + [bulk-email-enqueue.test.ts](__tests__/api/bulk-email-enqueue.test.ts) (202+jobId, recipientIds persisted, scheduledFor≈now, auth/denyReviewer/429/400/404 guards). Suite 1508 → 1519. Verified: tsc 0, eslint 0, vitest 1519/1519, build 0. Commit `69c5b7f`. **Doc fix**: corrected user-guide bulk-email rate limit 10 → 20/hr (the dashboard REST flow is 20; MCP `send_bulk_email` remains 10).

- **Worker DB-connection alert fix (P1+P2) + legacy cron cutover + P3 documented (June 9, 2026)** — Two prod alerts fired together — `worker:tick-wrapper-uncaught` (api) and a connector-level `Prisma error` (database) — both tracing to **one routine Supabase pooler dropout** (`EDBHANDLEREXITED` / `Error { kind: Closed }`) on the `webinar-recordings` worker tick. **Root cause**: the `pg_try_advisory_lock` acquire in [worker/lib/advisory-lock.ts](worker/lib/advisory-lock.ts) runs *outside* the job's own try/catch, so a transient connection-closed blip escaped to the scheduler's last-resort catch in [worker/index.ts](worker/index.ts) and paged — a self-healing event surfaced as a crash. Alert 2 is the same event from Prisma's `$on("error")` connector channel ([src/lib/db.ts](src/lib/db.ts)), which fires independently of whether the query promise is caught. **P1** — wrapped the lock-acquire so a *retryable* connection error (classified via the now-exported `classifyPrismaError`) becomes a quiet skip (`return null`, warn-level `worker:lock-acquire-transient-skip`) that retries next tick; non-retryable acquire errors still re-throw. **P2** — added a `DB connection closed` classifier pattern (`EDBHANDLEREXITED` / `kind: Closed` / `connection to database closed`, retryable) AND **gated the connector `$on("error")` log level on the `retryable` flag** (until now `retryable` was metadata that nothing consumed): retryable transients now log at `warn` (still in /logs + Sentry, but **below** the error threshold that fires the SES admin-alert page); non-retryable classified errors (auth, TLS) and unclassified errors stay at `error` and still page. Net effect: routine pooler dropouts stop paging, real DB problems still do, and nothing stops being logged. **Tests**: extended [__tests__/lib/db-error-classifier.test.ts](__tests__/lib/db-error-classifier.test.ts) (capture warn+error, pin the new category + the level-gating) and new [__tests__/lib/advisory-lock.test.ts](__tests__/lib/advisory-lock.test.ts) (acquire→run→unlock, contended skip, P1 transient-skip, non-retryable re-throw). Suite 1499 → 1508. Verified: tsc 0, eslint 0, vitest 1508/1508, `npm run build` 0. **Operational — legacy cron cutover (Phase 4 operational half, done early):** disabled the 5 `/api/cron/*` lines in the Mumbai `ubuntu` crontab (commented, not deleted; backed up to `/home/ubuntu/crontab.backup.2026-06-09.txt`; the 3 DR backup lines — `.env`/uploads/`dr-pg-dump.sh` — untouched), so the `ea-sys-worker` node-cron tier is now the **sole runner** for cert-issue / scheduled-emails / webinar-recordings / webinar-attendance / oauth-cleanup. Route shims stay in code as the rollback handle (revert = re-enable the crontab lines; full code deletion is the remaining Phase 4 step in [docs/WORKER_EXTRACTION_PLAN.md](docs/WORKER_EXTRACTION_PLAN.md)). Verified worker reliable as sole runner post-cutover (stable, `RestartCount=0`, all jobs firing on cadence, zero errors). **P3 (known limitation, NOT fixed — documented):** the worker's `pg_try_advisory_lock` is *session*-scoped, but the worker's Prisma client connects through the Supabase **transaction** pooler (port 6543, `pgbouncer=true`), where per-statement backend reassignment means the lock and its unlock can land on different backends — so the singleton guarantee does **not** actually hold across two concurrent runners. Harmless today (single worker, cron killed) but **must be fixed before running a 2nd worker** (e.g. Singapore DR failover). The durable fix = point the worker at `DIRECT_URL` (session mode, port 5432), which also removes the pooler-recycle that caused the original `EDBHANDLEREXITED`. Caveat block added to [worker/lib/advisory-lock.ts](worker/lib/advisory-lock.ts); the old "session-scoped auto-release" comment was actively misleading and is now corrected.

- **Survey — dashboard shareable link + configurable expiry + Preview fix (June 9, 2026)** — Added an organizer-generated, reusable survey link alongside the existing per-registration bulk-email invite, and fixed the long-broken Preview button. Shipped to `main` in commit `c347b50` (deployed). **Three capabilities:** (1) **Shareable link** — one reusable link the organizer generates from the Survey builder and posts anywhere (email signature, WhatsApp, a slide). Respondents **self-identify by their registered email**, so every response stays tied to a `Registration` — **no `SurveyResponse` schema change**, and the responses dashboard / CSV / aggregate are untouched (they already null-guard registration, and self-identify never produces a null one). (2) **Configurable expiry (3/5/7/10 days)** on both the shareable link and the bulk-email survey-invitation (which previously hardcoded a 7-day TTL). (3) **Preview fix** — the builder's Preview button linked to `?token=preview`, a fake token the public route rejected with *"This survey link is invalid or has already been used"* (the exact symptom an organizer hit). It now opens `?preview=1`, a non-saving preview mode (renders the questions, submit disabled, "responses are not saved" banner). **Storage**: `Event.surveyShareLink Json?` (additive column, migration `20260609120000_add_event_survey_share_link`, `ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS` → blue-green safe). Shape `{ token, expiresAt, createdAt, createdByUserId } | null`. Token is **plaintext** (like `Abstract.managementToken`) so the dashboard can re-display the URL; reaching the form still requires a valid registrant email to submit, so plaintext is acceptable. Lookup is **slug-scoped** (the public URL carries the slug) so no global token index is needed. **New lib** [src/lib/survey/share-link.ts](src/lib/survey/share-link.ts): `surveyExpiryDaysSchema` (the 3/5/7/10 contract, shared by the management route + the bulk-email schema), `generateShareToken`, `buildShareLinkRecord`, `readSurveyShareLink` (defensive JSON parse like `readSurveyConfig`), and `isShareLinkValid` — a **timing-safe** compare (`crypto.timingSafeEqual` with a length guard first so it never throws on a length mismatch; the token check runs BEFORE the expiry check). **Management API** [src/app/api/events/[eventId]/survey/share-link/route.ts](src/app/api/events/%5BeventId%5D/survey/share-link/route.ts): `POST` (generate/regenerate, `denyReviewer` + org-scoped + 20/hr rate-limited + audited; returns `{ url, expiresAt }`) and `DELETE` (disable → `Prisma.JsonNull`, idempotent). The builder reads the current link from the existing `GET /api/events/[eventId]` payload (the new column flows through automatically). **Public route** [src/app/api/public/events/[slug]/survey/route.ts](src/app/api/public/events/%5Bslug%5D/survey/route.ts): added a `?preview=1` GET branch (FIRST — config only, no token, no PII, no DB write) and a `?share=` GET branch (validates the share token + expiry, returns config with no prefill), plus a `?share` POST self-identify path (body `{ share, email, answers }`). Both submit paths now funnel through a shared `finalizeSubmission(req, registration, rawAnswers, deleteTokenHash)` helper so the **existing `?token=` per-registration path is byte-for-byte behavior-identical** (the only difference is the token path passes a hash to delete; the share path passes `null` because the link is reusable). The existing `public-survey-route` test still passes unchanged, confirming the refactor preserved behavior. Share-path registration resolution handles **email→multiple registrations** (prefer an incomplete one, else most-recent; scoped by event slug so no cross-event leak) and a **soft 60s IP dedup** as a secondary guard — the per-registration `@unique` stays the primary dedup; the window is deliberately short so distinct registrants behind one conference-WiFi NAT IP aren't false-blocked. **Bulk-email TTL** [src/lib/bulk-email.ts](src/lib/bulk-email.ts): the survey-invitation token mint now reads `filters.surveyExpiryDays ?? 7`. It rides inside `filters` (not a top-level param) specifically so **scheduled sends honor it too** — the worker reconstructs the send from the persisted `ScheduledEmail.filters` JSON, so a top-level param would have silently fallen back to 7 days on scheduled sends. **UI**: builder [survey/page.tsx](src/app/%28dashboard%29/events/%5BeventId%5D/survey/page.tsx) gains a "Shareable link" card (generate with a 3/5/7/10 expiry dropdown, copy, regenerate, disable) + the one-line Preview href fix; the public form [e/[slug]/survey/page.tsx](src/app/e/%5Bslug%5D/survey/page.tsx) gains preview mode (amber banner + disabled fields/submit) and share mode (a "registered email" step above the questions); the bulk-email dialog [bulk-email-dialog.tsx](src/components/bulk-email-dialog.tsx) gains the 3/5/7/10 "expires in" dropdown shown only for the survey-invitation type, threaded into `filters`. **Tests**: [__tests__/lib/survey-share-link.test.ts](__tests__/lib/survey-share-link.test.ts) — 13 cases covering the expiry enum, record building, and every `isShareLinkValid` branch (valid / none / mismatch / wrong-length-never-throws / empty / expired-at-boundary / token-checked-before-expiry). Suite 1486 → 1499. Verified: tsc 0, eslint 0, vitest 1499/1499, `npm run build` 0. **Note for operators**: a respondent's email must match a non-cancelled registration on that event, and the one-response-per-registration rule still applies (testing the same email twice shows the already-completed state — correct).

- **CloudWatch Logs — fourth observability path live (June 8, 2026)** — All Pino logs now ship from the Mumbai EC2 box to AWS CloudWatch Logs in `ap-south-1`. Joins Sentry (errors), SES admin-alert email (errors), `/logs` Postgres dashboard (everything), and `tail -f` on the host as the fourth + fifth parallel paths. Architecture: CloudWatch agent runs as a systemd service on the host, reads the same Pino-written log files at `/home/ubuntu/ea-sys/logs/{app,error}.log` (mounted as Docker volumes from both web + worker containers), ships them via the EC2 instance role to log groups `ea-sys/app` (30-day retention) and `ea-sys/error` (90-day retention). Chose **host-agent over Docker `awslogs` driver** to preserve `docker logs ea-sys-blue` for emergency SSH-debug, and **over a Pino-direct-to-CloudWatch transport** so the app stays AWS-agnostic + logs survive app crashes (file persists on disk regardless). Same source as the SystemLog Postgres table reads — one Pino write powers four readers. **Setup files**: [infra/cloudwatch/amazon-cloudwatch-agent.json](infra/cloudwatch/amazon-cloudwatch-agent.json) (agent config — schema-strict, no `_comment` fields allowed by the validator), [infra/cloudwatch/setup.sh](infra/cloudwatch/setup.sh) (idempotent install + ACL fix + systemctl enable, runs from `bash infra/cloudwatch/setup.sh` on the box), [infra/cloudwatch/README.md](infra/cloudwatch/README.md) (operator runbook with §1 architecture / §2 setup / §3 optional alarm pipeline / §4 troubleshooting / §5 layer comparison). **Two debug-cycle gotchas surfaced during initial deploy, both fixed in setup.sh**: (1) CloudWatch agent's JSON Schema validator rejects unknown properties — `_comment` fields I'd added for inline docs failed phase-1 validation with `Additional property _comment is not allowed`. Stripped to schema-only JSON; docs moved to README. (2) `cwagent` user can't read log files even though they're mode `0644` because `/home/ubuntu` is `0700` on Ubuntu default — world-readable files inside a non-traversable parent are functionally unreadable. Fix uses ACLs (`setfacl -m u:cwagent:rx /home/ubuntu /home/ubuntu/ea-sys /home/ubuntu/ea-sys/logs` + `setfacl -d -m u:cwagent:r /home/ubuntu/ea-sys/logs` for default ACL on rotated files). Surgical — doesn't loosen `/home/ubuntu` for other system users. **Setup script auto-installs `acl` package** if missing (Ubuntu LTS images usually ship it but the AMI on the Mumbai box didn't, surfaced during initial deploy). **Useful CloudWatch Insights queries**: `fields @timestamp, level, module, msg | filter level >= 50 | sort @timestamp desc | limit 50` (last 50 errors), `fields module | filter level >= 50 | stats count() by module | sort count desc` (error count by source), `fields @timestamp, msg, durationMs | filter msg like /cron:tick/ and durationMs > 100 | sort durationMs desc` (slowest cron ticks), `fields awsErrorName, to.0, subject | filter awsErrorName != "" | stats count() by awsErrorName` (email failures by AWS error code — the Jan 5 webinar `MessageRejected` would have surfaced here in seconds). **Cost**: ~50-200 MB/month log volume = well under $1/month at AWS pricing. **What's not done**: the optional alarm pipeline (SNS topic + email subscription + metric filter on `{ $.level >= 50 }` + alarm on "5 errors in 5 minutes") is fully documented in `infra/cloudwatch/README.md §3` but not executed — pick it up if the existing per-error SES admin-alert feels too noisy or you want an aggregate-rate signal. Operator one-time prereq: attach AWS-managed `CloudWatchAgentServerPolicy` to `ea-sys-mumbai-ec2-role` instance role.

- **Background worker tier — node-cron Node service alongside Next.js web (June 4, 2026)** — Cron-driven jobs (cert renderer, scheduled emails, webinar recordings + attendance, MCP OAuth cleanup) now run in a dedicated Node process in its own Docker container (`ea-sys-worker`) alongside the existing blue/green Next.js web containers on the same EC2 box. Sibling, not microservice — shares the same Postgres, same `.env`, same `public/uploads` volume, same `logs` volume, same Docker `web` network. Closes the "request/response shape mismatch + CPU isolation" gap I flagged in the earlier "would I still pick Next.js" reflection — workers no longer compete with dashboard latency on the same Node event loop. Plan-of-record at [docs/WORKER_EXTRACTION_PLAN.md](docs/WORKER_EXTRACTION_PLAN.md) covers the full architecture + 4-phase migration. **Phase 1** (`dcadc44`): extracted the bodies of 4 `/api/cron/*` route handlers into shared `runTick()` functions under `src/lib/{scheduled-emails,webinar-recordings,webinar-attendance,mcp-oauth-cleanup}-worker.ts` — pure refactor, behavior unchanged, routes became thin shims (auth + delegate). The cert worker (`src/lib/certificates/issue-worker.ts → tickAllRuns()`) was already in shape from earlier. **Phase 2** (`0350592`): built the worker process — 15 new files. `worker/index.ts` bootstraps a `node-cron` scheduler registering all 5 jobs at their natural cadences (cert-issue + scheduled-emails every minute, webinar-recordings every 5 min, webinar-attendance every 10 min, oauth-cleanup hourly at :00). Each `worker/jobs/*.ts` is a ~20-line shim wrapping the matching `runTick()` in `withJobLock(jobId, name, fn)` + try/catch. `worker/lib/advisory-lock.ts` uses `pg_try_advisory_lock(jobId)` for singleton enforcement — session-scoped, so a crashed worker auto-releases at connection close. `worker/lib/health-server.ts` exposes `GET /health` on port 3099 returning `{ok, uptimeSeconds, lastTickAt, shuttingDown}` for Docker's healthcheck. `worker/lib/shutdown.ts` traps SIGTERM/SIGINT, drains in-flight ticks with a 25s timeout (Docker grants 30s grace before SIGKILL), then `Prisma.$disconnect` + exit 0. **The advisory lock is the key safety property**: both the legacy `/api/cron/*` routes AND the worker drain the same job queues during the dual-write window (Phase 3); whichever path grabs the lock per tick does the work, the other politely skips with `worker:skip-tick-locked`. Same primitive also makes the Singapore DR fail-over case safe — Mumbai web + Mumbai worker + Singapore worker can all be up without double-processing. **Phase 2.5** (`8672b4f`): added two public-facing health endpoints — `/health` is a shorter alias for `/api/health` (same handler via re-export, matches what external monitors like Uptime Robot / Route 53 default to); `/worker/health` is a Next.js-side proxy to the worker container's internal `:3099/health` via Docker DNS (`ea-sys-worker:3099`). The worker's port 3099 is NOT published externally — this proxy is the only public surface for worker state. Returns 503 on unreachable/timeout (2s ceiling)/shutting-down. `WORKER_HEALTH_URL` env override for local dev. **Dockerfile.worker**: multi-stage (`node:24-slim` base), copies `src/` wholesale because worker libs transitively import other parts of `src/`; runtime is `npx tsx worker/index.ts` (tsx moved from devDeps to deps so production has it; no separate TS-compile step — tsx handles `tsconfig.json` paths directly so `@/lib/*` resolves at runtime). `docker-compose.prod.yml` gains the `ea-sys-worker` service: same `env_file`, same `public/uploads` + `logs` mounts as the web containers, healthcheck every 30s with 3-retry restart. **Worker logs flow through the same Pino logger as the web app** — the `apiLogger` writes to stdout (Docker captures) + `/app/logs/app.log` (mounted to `./logs` on host, shared with web container) + `SystemLog` Postgres table (the same table the dashboard's `/logs` viewer reads). So all worker activity is searchable from the dashboard with no SSH: open `/logs`, pick `source=database`, search `worker:` to filter. Useful log keys: `worker:started` (boot), `worker:tick-start` / `worker:tick-end` (debug-level per-tick), `worker:skip-tick-locked` (healthy lock-contention signal), `worker:tick-uncaught` (caught at the job's try/catch), `worker:tick-wrapper-uncaught` (caught at the scheduler wrapper — should be 0), `worker:shutdown-start` → `worker:shutdown-complete`, `worker:advisory-unlock-failed` (DB connection died before unlock; session-close cleanup will release anyway). **Decisions locked at plan-time**: Q1 same repo with new `worker/` folder + shared root `package.json` (over monorepo workspaces or separate repo — easier revert, no cross-repo coordination), Q2 `node-cron` for scheduling (over `bree` or BullMQ — minimal, no Redis dependency, job state already lives in Postgres tables), Q3 dual-write window ~1 week (over hard cut — easy rollback if worker has unforeseen issues). New deps: `node-cron@4.2.1`, `@types/node-cron`. `tsx` moved from devDeps to deps. Smoke-tested locally: `npx tsx worker/index.ts` boots, registers 5 schedules, `curl localhost:3099/health` returns 200 with the expected shape, SIGTERM triggers graceful shutdown logs. Verified across both phases: tsc + lint + 1357/1357 vitest + build clean. **Phase 3 is the watch window** — both paths fire in parallel for ~1 week; healthy state shows `worker:tick-end` keys at expected cadences AND occasional `worker:skip-tick-locked` AND `/worker/health` 200s with updating `lastTickAt` timestamps. **Phase 4 cut-over** scheduled ~June 11: remove the 5 cron lines from Mumbai crontab, delete the thin-shim route handlers in `src/app/api/cron/`, deploy. Worker becomes the only path. Rollback procedure documented in [docs/WORKER_EXTRACTION_PLAN.md §11](docs/WORKER_EXTRACTION_PLAN.md). Operator quick-reference at [worker/README.md](worker/README.md) covers all 3 healthcheck paths (public proxy, docker exec, docker inspect), all 3 log views (dashboard `/logs`, `docker logs`, file tail), and the "adding a new job" playbook.

- **Certificates — operator-feedback round + independent review (June 3, 2026)** — Four pieces of organizer feedback shipped behind a planning round, then an independent review-agent pass closed 4 HIGHs in-band. Commits `0c56c9a` (implementation, 11 files, +1264 LOC) → `1e9801a` (tests, +737 LOC, 24 unit + 8 e2e cases) → `58168b4` (4 HIGHs from the review). **The four features**: (1) **Canvas editor undo + Y-axis arrow nudge.** Commit-point undo (one step per drag-end / resize-end / add / delete / duplicate / textarea-focus / format change), Cmd/Ctrl+Z + Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+Z + Cmd/Ctrl+Y bindings on the editor wrapper (tabIndex=0, outline-none), stack depth 30 per-side, toolbar buttons mirror the shortcuts and disable on empty. Arrow nudge: Up/Down moves selected box Y by 1pt, Shift+Up/Down by 10pt, bounds-clamped, only when canvas is focused (not in a textarea), consecutive presses within 500ms coalesce into one undo step so holding the key doesn't fill the stack. Y-axis only per organizer's explicit request; X/W/H are direct-input via the side panel. (2) **`IssuedCertificate.lastResentAt` + `resendCount` columns.** Migration `20260603120000_add_certificate_resend_tracking` (additive). Distinct from existing `lastReprintedAt`/`reprintCount` — reprint re-renders the PDF, resend re-fires the delivery email reusing the existing pdfUrl. (3) **Resend route + listing route + IssuedCertificatesCard.** `GET /api/events/[eventId]/certificates/issued?registrationId=…` or `?speakerId=…` returns per-recipient cert rows (template name, serial, issuedAt, lastResentAt, resendCount, emailedAt from linked run item). `POST /api/events/[eventId]/certificates/issued/[certificateId]/resend` re-fires the delivery email reusing the existing pdfUrl + the cover-email snapshot from the original `CertificateIssueRun` row (replay fidelity — NOT the latest template defaults). Falls back to system default for legacy certs without a run snapshot. 30/hr/user rate limit. Bumps counter ATOMICALLY AFTER the SES send succeeds (failed sends do NOT poison the counter — next click is the same operation, not a misleading "second resend"). Refuses on revoked (409 CERT_REVOKED), un-rendered (409 PDF_NOT_RENDERED), and missing PDF (409 PDF_MISSING with the cross-machine local-storage hint). [src/components/certificates/issued-certificates-card.tsx](src/components/certificates/issued-certificates-card.tsx) mounts above the EmailLogCard on both the registration detail sheet (Activity tab) AND the speaker detail page (speaker page also gets an EmailLogCard for the first time as a bonus). Each cert row: type badge (ATTENDANCE blue, APPRECIATION amber), template name, serial (monospace), issued/sent dates, resend pill if `resendCount > 0`, Download + Resend buttons. Resend opens a confirm dialog labeled with recipient + previous-resend-history; on success toasts the **total** send count ("now sent N times total") so operators don't conflate "resent N times" with "this cert was only ever sent N times". (4) **EmailLogCard "Cert" pill.** Both the cron worker AND the new resend route thread `templateSlug: "certificate-delivery"` through `logContext`, so a small amber `<Award>` pill renders next to the subject on any cert-delivery row regardless of code path. **Independent review (in commit `58168b4`)** closed 4 HIGHs: **H1 atomic primary-query binding** — folded `eventId` into the resend route's `where` clause so a future refactor can't drop the cross-event-within-same-org guard (the GET list route already used this model; we now mirror). **H2 path-traversal + SSRF allowlist in `loadPdfBytes`** — local-path branch `path.resolve()` + assert prefix is `public/uploads/certificates/` (trailing sep so `certificates-evil/` can't slip past); remote branch must be https + hostname matches `*.supabase.co` allowlist. Each rejection now logs distinctly (`pdf-path-traversal`, `pdf-invalid-url`, `pdf-non-https`, `pdf-host-disallowed`, `pdf-fetch-failed`) so an engineer scanning `/logs` knows WHY a 409 PDF_MISSING fired without reading the error string. **H3 setState updater purity in undo/redo** — the previous `setUndoStack(stack => { setRedoStack(...); onChange(...); ... })` mutated other state + called the parent's onChange inside the updater; React 18+ StrictMode (default in Next 16) double-invokes updaters so the side effects fired twice per undo in dev, intermittently mis-syncing the redo stack. Restructured to read both stacks synchronously, set both, call onChange once — all in same tick (React batches the two setStates). **H4 toast wording** — `totalSent = resendCount + 1` so "now sent N times total" disambiguates against the row pill ("Resent N times") and what the EmailHistory shows (N+1 rows). **Tests**: 1352 → 1357 (+5 H1/H2 cases: cross-event 404, path-traversal `/uploads/../etc/passwd`, wrong-prefix `/uploads/photos/`, non-allowlisted host, supabase.co happy path). 8 e2e API-contract scenarios in `e2e/certificates-resend.spec.ts`. UI-level coverage of the resend button intentionally deferred until the e2e seed gains an `IssuedCertificate` row (today the seed doesn't issue certs because that requires the cron worker, which has its own unit suite). **Deferred review findings** (7 MEDIUMs + 7 LOWs) tracked in [docs/ROADMAP.md](docs/ROADMAP.md) §"Certificates — operator-feedback round, deferred review findings (June 3, 2026)" — none blocks deploy, each independently shippable, picked up when an operator hits a related issue. The most notable deferred ones: `abstractTitle` token not HTML-escaped in cert email body (pre-existing, inherited by resend route), confirm dialog state leak on Escape mid-mutation, `handleNudgeY` closure re-allocation while holding arrow key, EmailLogCard pill baseline misalignment. Decisions locked at plan-time: commit-point undo (not keystroke), Y-axis only (not X/Y), snapshot cover email from original run (not latest template), dedicated "Certificates" card placement (not inlined in Email History). Verified: tsc + lint + 1357/1357 vitest + build clean.

- **Disaster recovery — Singapore S3 bucket now mirrors uploads + env + Postgres dumps (June 3, 2026)** — Closed the last open DR gap from `docs/EC2_HARDENING.html` §"Gaps still open". Three independent backup streams now land in `s3://ea-sys-dr-singapore/` (customer-managed KMS encryption, S3 versioning on): `uploads/` (hourly mirror of `/home/ubuntu/ea-sys/public/uploads/`, RPO 60 min), `env/{YYYY-MM-DD}.env` (daily 21:00 UTC, RPO 24h, was already running), and now `db/{YYYY}/{MM}/{DD-HH}-mumbai.dump` (daily 23:00 UTC `pg_dump -Fc --schema=public`, RPO 24h — tunable to 12h by adding `11,` to the cron expression, scripts unchanged). S3 lifecycle: `db/` expires 30 days from creation; `uploads/` + `env/` kept indefinitely. **New scripts**: [scripts/dr-pg-dump.sh](scripts/dr-pg-dump.sh) — parses `DIRECT_URL` from `.env` without `source`-ing (defense against `.env`-as-shell), auto-installs `postgresql-client-17` idempotently on first run, sanity-checks dump size ≥ 100 KB (so silent pg_dump empty-file failures surface as exit 2), failure trap writes structured JSON log line + fires SES alert email (`alerts@meetingmindsexperts.com` → `krishna@meetingmindsdubai.com`) + cleans `/tmp` + propagates exit code, all config env-overridable for testability. [scripts/dr-restore-drill.sh](scripts/dr-restore-drill.sh) — quarterly drill (manual, 15 Jul/Oct/Jan/Apr), spins ephemeral `postgres:17` in Docker on port 55432, drops the auto-created `public` schema in scratch DB so the dump's own `CREATE SCHEMA public` doesn't collide on `pg_restore --exit-on-error`, downloads the latest dump from S3, `pg_restore --jobs=4 --exit-on-error`, then row counts on 9 critical tables (Event, Registration, IssuedCertificate, Payment, EmailLog, Speaker, Abstract, CertificateTemplate, AuditLog). **Three verified gotchas, all worth knowing about for the next operator**: (1) **Supabase is on PostgreSQL 17, not 15** — PG 17 isn't in Ubuntu Noble (24.04) default repos, needs the PGDG repo first; the scripts default `PG_VERSION=17` and `PG_IMAGE=postgres:17` accordingly, both env-overridable for future upgrades. (2) **`pg_dump --schema=public` is mandatory** — Supabase auto-creates platform schemas (`auth`, `storage`, `realtime`, `graphql_public`, `vault`, `pgsodium`, `_realtime`, `extensions`) referencing proprietary extensions like `supabase_vault` that vanilla `postgres:17` doesn't have; a full-schema dump fails to restore with `extension "supabase_vault" is not available`. EA-SYS uses none of those platform features (NextAuth not Supabase Auth, `STORAGE_PROVIDER=local` not Supabase Storage, no Realtime/GraphQL/Vault) so `--schema=public` captures everything we actually need AND keeps the dump portable to any vanilla PG 17 (RDS, Crunchy, fresh Supabase, the scratch Docker drill) — a real DR advantage vs being locked into Supabase as the only restore target. (3) **Scratch container needs `DROP SCHEMA public CASCADE` before `pg_restore`** — because `pg_dump --schema=public` includes its own `CREATE SCHEMA public` statement at the top, and fresh `postgres:17` auto-creates `public` at init, they collide on the very first statement; `dr-restore-drill.sh` drops public right after Postgres becomes ready. **IAM**: `DRBackupToSingapore` inline policy on `ea-sys-mumbai-ec2-role` grants `s3:PutObject` + `s3:GetObject` + `s3:ListBucket` on the bucket, `kms:Encrypt`/`kms:GenerateDataKey`/`kms:Decrypt` on the Singapore KMS key, and `ses:SendEmail`/`ses:SendRawEmail` constrained to the alerts sender address. **Documentation**: [infra/dr/README.md](infra/dr/README.md) is the operator runbook (one-time setup §1-§6 including read-path smoke test, monthly drill, surgical recovery §A-§E for partial losses, promotion runbook for full failover, post-incident return-to-Mumbai, known gaps, cost ~$0.20-0.50/mo for the DB backup line). [infra/dr/POSTGRES_BACKUP_PLAN.md](infra/dr/POSTGRES_BACKUP_PLAN.md) is the design history with decisions Q1-Q3 + §11 "First-run refinement" documenting the `--schema=public` discovery. Decisions locked in: Q1 30-day flat retention from each object's creation date, Q2 alerting = log file + SES email on failure (skipping CloudWatch alarm for v1), Q3 scope = all tables in `public` schema (include `SystemLog` + `EmailLog`, revisit at 6-month checkpoint if dumps exceed 1 GB). Open follow-ups in §7 "deferrals" with explicit re-eval triggers: Supabase PITR (cost $25-50/mo for seconds-precision rollback within 7d — worth it only if business need tightens past 24h RPO), cross-region read replica for sub-minute DB RTO, tiered retention (30d daily + 12w weekly + 12mo monthly), auto-run drill in CI. Verified end-to-end on Mumbai 2026-06-03: dump size 1.06 MB compressed (healthy for early-stage prod, well above 100 KB abort guard), duration ~4s, restore drill green with row counts on all 9 critical tables.

- **In-dashboard docs viewer — ADMIN + SUPER_ADMIN `/admin/docs` (June 3, 2026; access expanded to ADMIN on June 8, 2026)** — Every `.md` / `.html` in the repo is now browseable + searchable from the dashboard sidebar (BookOpen icon, role-gated). Source of truth = the repo files as of the deployed image. **Corrected Aug 11, 2026 (this said `scripts/deploy.sh`'s `git pull`, which does not exist):** the box never pulls source. The image is built on a GitHub runner and [Dockerfile](Dockerfile) lines 99-105 COPY `CLAUDE.md` / `README.md` / `CHANGELOG.md` / `docs/` / `infra/` into the runtime stage; the box only runs `docker compose pull`. **Consequence worth knowing: a docs-ONLY push never reaches prod.** The workflow's `paths-ignore` skips `**.md` / `docs/**`, so no image is built and `/admin/docs` keeps serving the previous image's copy until the next code deploy carries the docs along. `public/user-guide.html` is NOT ignored (it is an `.html` outside `docs/`), so a user-guide edit deploys on its own, and `paths-ignore` is evaluated per PUSH, so a mixed commit deploys everything in it. No DB writes, no Sanity, no in-browser editing — edits go through PR like normal code (planning round's explicit decision). Architecture: [src/lib/docs-fs.ts](src/lib/docs-fs.ts) filesystem walker exports `buildDocsTree()`, `readDocFile(path)`, `searchDocs(query)`. Security primitives baked in: extension allowlist (`.md`, `.html`, `.htm`), directory blocklist (`node_modules`, `.next`, `.git`, `.turbo`, `out`, `dist`, `build`, `coverage`, `playwright-report`, `test-results`, `.vercel`, plus `public/uploads/` as a hard block at the directory level), path-traversal guard via `resolveSafe()` (absolute path must stay within `process.cwd()`, nulls rejected, leading separators stripped, re-checked after symlink resolution), 1 MB per-file cap (anything bigger is a sign of something that shouldn't be in /docs), literal-substring search (NOT regex — protects against ReDoS from operator-typed patterns), 100-hit cap on search results. Three API routes ([src/app/api/admin/docs/tree/route.ts](src/app/api/admin/docs/tree/route.ts), [src/app/api/admin/docs/file/route.ts](src/app/api/admin/docs/file/route.ts), [src/app/api/admin/docs/search/route.ts](src/app/api/admin/docs/search/route.ts)) each re-check `role === "ADMIN" || role === "SUPER_ADMIN"` server-side (page-level guard is defense-in-depth, sidebar uses `adminOnly: true` flag). Search route has 60/hr/user rate limit. Page at [src/app/(dashboard)/admin/docs/page.tsx](src/app/%28dashboard%29/admin/docs/page.tsx): split layout, collapsible tree on left with auto-expand of ancestors when a deep-linked file is active (React 19's "store info from previous render" pattern, not `useEffect + setState`), content on right. Markdown → ReactMarkdown + remark-gfm with the same `prose` styling the help-chat uses but with `prose-code:bg-transparent prose-code:text-foreground` so inline code blends with the dashboard theme (no muted backgrounds, no white-on-dark). HTML → sandboxed iframe with `sandbox="allow-same-origin"` only (no `allow-scripts`), so the styled `docs/*.html` files (EC2_HARDENING, CERTIFICATES, user-guide) keep their original look without colliding with the dashboard theme AND any future supply-chain injection in a committed HTML file can't execute inside the dashboard origin. "Open in new tab" affordance for the full-screen styled HTML view. Default landing tries `infra/dr/README.md` (most useful "where do I start" doc for ops work), falls back to `docs/HANDOVER.md`, then `CLAUDE.md`. Debounced 300ms search (typing "registr" doesn't fire 7 requests), grouped results by file path with line + ~80-char context, max 5 hits shown per file with "+N more" tail. Copy-path button on every file header. Verified: tsc + lint + 1328/1328 vitest + build clean.

- **Certificates system — v3 PDF-overlay + multi-template + tag-driven Issue + cover-email editor + audit hardening (June 2, 2026)** — Major build over 12+ commits (`b226f16` → `425d979`). The v2 compose-from-assets cert renderer (banner + signatures + footer logos assembled by the platform) was replaced wholesale with a **PDF-overlay model**: the designer hands the organizer a finished cert PDF (or PNG/JPG that the upload route server-converts via `pdf-lib`'s `embedPng` / `embedJpg`), the canvas editor at [src/components/certificates/certificate-canvas-editor.tsx](src/components/certificates/certificate-canvas-editor.tsx) rasterizes page 1 via `pdfjs-dist` (self-hosted worker at `/pdfjs/pdf.worker.min.mjs`, copied by [scripts/copy-pdfjs-worker.mjs](scripts/copy-pdfjs-worker.mjs) at postinstall), and `react-rnd` handles drag + resize of text-box overlays. The renderer at [src/lib/certificates/render.ts](src/lib/certificates/render.ts) is ~250 LOC of pdf-lib code that loads the background PDF, embeds the 12 standard fonts on demand, and paints each text box with `mergeBody()` token substitution + alignment + the top-left ↔ bottom-left coordinate flip the editor's editor-Y → pdf-lib-Y conversion needs.

  **Cert types collapsed 4 → 2**: ATTENDANCE + APPRECIATION (was ATTENDANCE / PRESENTER / POSTER / CME). Migration `20260602110000_collapse_certificate_types_to_two` does the Postgres `ALTER TYPE RENAME` + swap + ALTER COLUMN dance (no live data — Phase C was shipped earlier the same day with zero issued certs). CME / accreditations stay as event-level data consumed via `{{cmeHours}}` / `{{accreditationBody}}` / `{{accreditationReference}}` tokens on either category's text boxes — not a separate cert type any more.

  **Multi-template per category**: replaced the `Event.settings.certificateTemplates` 2-slot JSON with a proper `CertificateTemplate` table (migration `20260602120000_certificate_template_table`). An event can have N templates per category — "Standard Attendance", "VIP Attendance", "Chairman Appreciation", etc. Each has its own backgroundPdfUrl, textBoxes, sortOrder, and (post-`32a3610`) optional `emailSubject` + `emailBody` cover-email defaults. `IssuedCertificate.certificateTemplateId` + `CertificateIssueRun.certificateTemplateId` FKs preserve audit-trail integrity (SetNull on delete; the API layer additionally blocks DELETE with 409 when any issued cert references the template).

  **One cert per recipient per category** invariant is enforced by `IssuedCertificate`'s dual `@@unique([eventId, type, registrationId|speakerId])` constraints, catching concurrent operator clicks + MCP retries that race past the application-level eligibility exclusion. Serials are category-scoped via `CertificateSerialCounter` (atomic upsert+increment under a `@@id([eventId, type])` PK).

  **Tag-driven manual Issue (no auto-eligibility)** — per the organizer's "no auto eligibility" call. The eligibility worker takes a `tag` parameter; ATTENDANCE template + tag X → registrations in event where `Attendee.tags` includes X (Registration→Attendee FK; tags live on Attendee), APPRECIATION template + tag X → speakers where `Speaker.tags` includes X (abstract submitters inherit `Speaker.tags` because submitters are persisted as Speaker rows with `Abstract.speakerId` as a required FK). The `/eligible` route has two modes via the same response shape — without `tag` it returns `availableTags: [{ tag, count }]` for the picker, with `tag` it returns the filtered recipient list. Issue route body requires `{templateId, tag, emailSubject, emailBody}`; the concurrent-run guard + tx are unified into a single `$transaction` (H5 fix from the audit) so two fast-clicks can't both pass the in-progress check.

  **Cover-email editor opens at Issue click** — Tiptap WYSIWYG dialog at [src/components/certificates/cert-email-editor-dialog.tsx](src/components/certificates/cert-email-editor-dialog.tsx), reused twice (once for per-template defaults from the Templates tab, once for per-run overrides from the Issue tab). 8 tokens total (recipientName, eventName, eventDateRange, venueLine, organizationName, certificateType, certificateSerial, plus abstractTitle on APPRECIATION which looks up the speaker's accepted abstract via Abstract FK, POSTER preferred). Token resolver split between client-safe constants (`src/lib/certificates/email-tokens.ts` — system defaults + spec) and server-only resolver (`src/lib/certificates/email-tokens-resolver.ts` — DB lookups + structured warn logs) because Turbopack tried to bundle the server-only Pino logger into the client when the page imported the constants. Snapshotted onto the run row at Issue confirm so a later template edit doesn't change in-flight emails. The send phase applies the per-event branding pipeline via `wrapWithBranding()` + `inlineCss()` — header image, footer HTML, footer image, sender override, CSS inlining all apply (H1 fix from the audit: pre this change the cert email bypassed the pipeline entirely).

  **Image upload conversion** — Upload route at [src/app/api/upload/pdf/route.ts](src/app/api/upload/pdf/route.ts) accepts PDF/JPG/PNG via magic-byte detection (`%PDF-`, `89 50 4E 47`, `FF D8 FF`); images get wrapped in a single-page PDF where page dims = image's intrinsic pixel dimensions as points, so downstream code only ever sees PDFs. 10 MB cap (was 5 MB; bumped because full-res PNG cert designs commonly land at 5-8 MB). The route validates `eventId` against a cuid regex BEFORE touching the filesystem (B1 from the audit: defense-in-depth against `../../media` traversal) AND verifies the event belongs to the caller's org via `db.event.findFirst` (H7 from the audit: cross-tenant upload-into-another-org's-directory is structurally impossible).

  **Issue lifecycle**: PENDING → RENDERING → AWAITING_REVIEW → SENDING → COMPLETED, with FAILED + CANCELLED branches. The AWAITING_REVIEW gate is the operator's spot-check before 300-5000 emails fan out. Cron worker drains 50 renders/tick + 25 emails/tick (SES-safe at 14/sec sustained), heartbeats `lastTickAt` so the stall detector reclaims runs stuck >10 min, per-item try/catch so one bad recipient can't kill a batch, and HARD-fails the run rather than fall back to a placeholder PDF if the template gets deleted mid-run (H4 from the audit). The design-approval gate was dropped — the PDF-overlay model makes the design tangible enough (canvas + Preview button) that a separate SUPER_ADMIN sign-off step is unwarranted.

  **MCP tools (5)**: `list_certificate_templates`, `create_certificate_template`, `update_certificate_template`, `delete_certificate_template`, `update_cme_settings`. All accept the cover-email defaults; tool definitions at [src/lib/agent/tools/certificates.ts](src/lib/agent/tools/certificates.ts), Zod params at [src/lib/agent/register-mcp-tools.ts](src/lib/agent/register-mcp-tools.ts). The Issue flow itself is NOT exposed via MCP — interactive email-confirmation step, operator-only.

  **Independent senior code review** caught 4 BLOCKERs + 8 HIGHs in the post-build pass; all blockers + 6 highs fixed in-band: B1 path-traversal + cross-tenant upload (cuid + org-bound check), B2 XSS in cert delivery email (escapeHtml on recipientName/eventName/orgName), B3 canvas PATCH spam (page-level 400ms debounce + optimistic React Query cache + flush on editor close — typing "Hello" was 5 server writes), B4 draft-wipe-on-window-focus (`JSON.stringify` deep-equal instead of object-reference comparison since React Query's `refetchOnWindowFocus: true` returns fresh objects), H2 silent-4xx logging sweep, H3 sortOrder race (transactional aggregate+create), H4 template-deleted-mid-run (fail run hard), H5 concurrent-run guard not transactional (moved findFirst into the same `$transaction` as the create), H6 package version bump for MCP cache invalidation, H8 no-org logging consistency. H1 (cert-email branding-pipeline bypass) landed in `32a3610` along with the cover-email editor.

  **User-facing docs**: full §18 added to [public/user-guide.html](public/user-guide.html) (operator-facing — picked up by the help chat at module init, no chat-code change needed); developer architecture at [docs/CERTIFICATES.md](docs/CERTIFICATES.md). MCP reference at [docs/MCP_REFERENCE.md](docs/MCP_REFERENCE.md) gained a Certificates section (now 70 tools). HANDOVER.md Recent Major Additions header updated. Help chat starter chips at [src/components/help-chat/help-chat-sheet.tsx](src/components/help-chat/help-chat-sheet.tsx) gained "How do I issue certificates after the event?" for SUPER_ADMIN / ADMIN / ORGANIZER roles.

  **Deploy story**: blue-green via `scripts/deploy.sh` — applies the migrations (additive: cert types collapse + template table + email-fields columns) before container swap. STORAGE_PROVIDER setting was an early-build false alarm and is currently unset (defaults to `local`, which is correct for EC2 — Phase C cert PDFs land in `public/uploads/certificates/issued/{runId}/{certId}.pdf`). Package bumped 0.3.9 → 0.4.0 (cert collapse) → 0.4.1 (image upload) → 0.4.2 (cover-email editor) → 0.4.3 (MCP cover-email fields). Verified: tsc clean, lint clean, 1328/1328 vitest, `npm run build` clean.

- **Help-chatbot (Sonnet 4.6, KB-grounded) — sidebar drawer (May 21, 2026)** — Read-only AI assistant accessible from the dashboard sidebar footer. Answers "how do I" questions from `public/user-guide.html` via Anthropic prompt-cached system prompt. **Distinct from the existing AI Agent** (which mutates event data via 65+ tools): this one only explains, can't act. Six-commit staged rollout (`c076aa0` → `b3a6bc4`), planned in [docs/HELP_CHATBOT.md](docs/HELP_CHATBOT.md). **Architecture**: new `src/lib/ai/` provider abstraction (`AiProvider` interface + Anthropic implementation + central model config — future vendor swaps are config flips, not rewrites; the existing AI Agent stays untouched and retrofits later as v1.1 work); `src/lib/help-chat/guide-loader.ts` (reads + strips HTML once at module init, security-tested removal of `<script>`/`<style>`/comment bodies); `src/lib/help-chat/system-prompt.ts` (two-block `SystemBlock[]`: cached stable instructions + guide + uncached role-aware tail — cache-prefix order matters and is unit-pinned); `POST /api/help-chat` with SSE streaming via the abstraction, per-user 50/hr rate limit, Zod-validated body, role-aware system prompt (SUPER_ADMIN / ADMIN / ORGANIZER / MEMBER / REVIEWER / SUBMITTER / REGISTRANT — MEMBER specifically warned to refer finance questions to admin per the Mecomed-sensitive RBAC policy); React drawer (`src/components/help-chat/help-chat-sheet.tsx`) on the `Sheet` primitive with typing-dots placeholder, ReactMarkdown + remark-gfm rendering matching the AI Agent's `prose` styling, localStorage persistence (`ea-sys:help-chat:v1:<userId>`, 40-msg cap, schema versioned); `HelpChatProvider` mounts the drawer once at the dashboard root and exposes `useHelpChatLauncher()` so the sidebar Help button opens it without prop-drilling. **Cost (measured vs planned)**: guide is ~12K tokens (planned 30K); warm-cache call ~$0.008 (planned $0.022); 1k Q/month ~$8 (planned $33). **Privacy posture**: Anthropic enterprise terms; logs metadata only (userId, role, token counts, latency) — message bodies NEVER logged. **Visual differentiation from AI Agent**: HelpCircle icon vs Sparkles; "Help Assistant" header vs "AI Agent"; muted drawer styling vs primary-tinted; explicit "for doing things on an event, use the AI Agent in Tools" prompt copy. **Tests**: +44 unit (11 Anthropic adapter — system block cache flag mapping, stream filtering, null-cache-token mapping, missing API key fail-fast; 12 stripHtml — script/style/comment body removal as security property, entity decoding, space-replace tag stripping; 21 system prompt — 2-block structure, refusal-pattern keywords pinned as safety harness, role-tail differentiation, name/org fallbacks). Suite 1237 → 1281. **E2E**: `e2e/help-chat.spec.ts` — hermetic with mocked SSE response (no real Anthropic in CI); pins UI shell (sidebar trigger, drawer opens, role-tailored starter chips, clear-chat hidden in empty state) + plumbing (fetch → SSE parse → markdown render → clear chat resets). Caveat: spec requires Playwright to spawn its own dev server (the saved port-drift memory about `PORT=3113`); reusing a locally-running dev server bound to the development DB will fail at login because the test users don't exist there — stop the dev server before `npm run test:e2e`. **Deferred to v1.1** (in [docs/HELP_CHATBOT.md](docs/HELP_CHATBOT.md) §17): retrofit existing AI Agent onto the `AiProvider` abstraction; provider-fallback for reliability; local Ollama as a privacy escape hatch; `👍/👎` feedback capture per assistant message; cross-device server-side conversation history; multi-language; public-guide widget; quote-style markdown subset trimming for tighter style control.

- **registration-detail-sheet.tsx staged refactor — A → E (May 20, 2026)** — The 2,174-line monolithic registration detail sheet went through a careful 5-commit staged refactor, each step independently revertable, each gated by tsc + lint + full vitest + build + Playwright regression. **Step A (`8ad760b`)** typed `useBillingAccounts` / `useBillingAccount` returns in `src/hooks/use-api.ts` (new `BillingAccountRow` / `BillingAccountDetail` interfaces mirroring the API response shape) → removed 3 `any[]` casts from the picker call sites. **Step B (`25b3299`)** extracted [src/app/(dashboard)/events/[eventId]/registrations/registration-edit-mapping.ts](src/app/%28dashboard%29/events/%5BeventId%5D/registrations/registration-edit-mapping.ts) — pure `toEditData(reg)` + `toServerPayload(editData, expectedUpdatedAt)` mappers + `RegistrationEditData` interface + `EMPTY_REGISTRATION_EDIT_DATA` defaults. The same ~30-field shape used to live inline three times in the sheet (initial useState defaults / `startEditing` populate / `saveEdits` payload assembly). Critical: the mappers preserve every null-vs-undefined-vs-trim normalization decision exactly — billing/tax/payer trim-to-null on save (deliberate clear), attendee free-text → undefined (PUT treats as "unchanged"), association/memberId/studentId → null (CAN clear), photo `?? null`, payer triplet atomicity (setting `billingAccountId=""` forces `payerReference=null + attendeeIsGuarantor=false`), `expectedUpdatedAt` is the W2-F8 optimistic-lock token. 14 unit tests pin every decision + the studentIdExpiry ISO parse + the `attendeeIsGuarantor ?? false` legacy-null path + a round-trip identity. Sheet **−99 lines**. **Step C (`9cdf002`)** introduced [src/lib/api-fetch.ts](src/lib/api-fetch.ts): `ApiError` (Error subclass with `status` + `code` + raw `data`) + `apiFetch` / `apiPostJson` / `apiPutJson` / `apiDelete` thin method helpers. The existing `fetchApi` in `use-api.ts` throws plain `Error(message)` which is fine for queries, but mutations sometimes need to branch on status + code (STALE_WRITE, BILLING_ACCOUNT_INACTIVE, CAPACITY_EXCEEDED). All 5 mutations in the sheet (update / check-in / send-email / delete / refund) collapsed from 8-line fetch+throw boilerplate to one-line arrow expressions; `updateRegistration.onError` uses `error instanceof ApiError` to branch on STALE_WRITE instead of manual error-shape casting. `apiPostJson` skips Content-Type when body is undefined (empty-body action routes like `/check-in`, `/refund`). +8 unit tests pin the helper. Sheet **−38 lines**. **Step D (`5e3d486`)** fixed the prop-sync. The previous `if (registration !== selectedRegistration && registration !== null)` compared the prop to **derived state** which (a) tripped React 19's setState-during-render rule and (b) had a latent **prop-revert race** — after a mutation's onSuccess updated `selectedRegistration` to the fresh server row, the stale parent prop diverged and the next render would silently revert the just-saved data. Replaced with React 19's canonical "Storing information from previous renders" pattern: a `prevRegistration` state snapshot is compared against the incoming prop; `setPrevRegistration` and the derived-state updates fire in the same render pass; sync runs ONLY when the prop actually changes. Diff +21/−4. **Step E (`64dc640`)** extracted 5 inline handlers near the existing `handlePreviewRegistrationEmail`: `handlePrintBadge` (was a 30-line inline async block with try/catch/finally + blob lifecycle + setTimeout cleanup), `handleDeleteClick`, `handleRefundClick`, `openEmailDialog(type)` (collapses 4 near-identical DropdownMenuItem onClicks), `handleConfirmSendEmail`. JSX call sites now read as one-liner `onClick={handleX}` expressions. **Cumulative**: sheet 2,174 → ~2,063 lines (~−110 net), **+22 unit tests** that didn't exist before, one latent bug squashed, type signatures tightened end-to-end. **F + G + H tracked in [docs/ROADMAP.md](docs/ROADMAP.md)** "registration-detail-sheet.tsx staged refactor remainder" with explicit trigger conditions for when to revisit each (F: only with H or under measured input lag; G: when file >3k lines or next feature touches >2 sections painfully; H: when a feature needs per-field control like autosave-on-blur). Verified post-step by running the 62-spec Playwright suite — 58 passed, 0 regressions from A–E (the 4 unrelated bulk-email failures pre-date these commits; git diff proved none of the 7 files touched appear in the bulk-email dialog import graph).

- **Per-event payer scoping — EventBillingAccount junction (May 20, 2026)** — The v1 ship (May 19) made `BillingAccount` org-scoped, which caused **picker overflow**: every active payer in the org appeared in every event's "Charge to" dropdown. Refactored to a many-to-many via junction so a payer must be **explicitly attached** to each event where it's available — same logical row, never duplicated across events. **Schema**: new `EventBillingAccount { id, eventId, billingAccountId, addedAt, addedByUserId, @@unique([eventId, billingAccountId]) }`; FKs Cascade from both ends (deleting either entity unlinks but doesn't delete the other; Registration→BillingAccount stays Restrict so existing assignments survive a detach). Migration `20260520120000_event_billing_account_junction` is additive + junction starts empty (v1 not yet deployed, no pairs to backfill). **API**: `GET /api/billing-accounts?eventId=…` filters via junction membership (org-bound at the event end too — a foreign eventId returns `[]`, no cross-tenant attachment leak); new idempotent `POST/DELETE /api/events/[eventId]/billing-accounts/[billingAccountId]` (denyReviewer+denyFinance, both ids org-bound before touching the junction). **Hooks**: `useBillingAccounts({ eventId })` threaded into Add Registration form + detail-sheet reassign picker — each event now sees only its attached payers. **Edge case**: detail-sheet Select shows a synthetic option `(no longer attached to this event)` when a registration's current payer was detached after assignment, so the value renders truthfully instead of going blank. **UI**: `BillingAccountsCard` (Settings → Billing) gained a clickable "Events" count column + a `CalendarDays` icon action → `EventsAttachmentDialog` with one checkbox per org event (attach/detach with idempotent fetch + toast + queryClient invalidation). Detail GET on `/api/billing-accounts/[id]` now returns `attachedEvents` alongside the registrations AR view. **View-mode UX fix (May 20, also `d939a20`)**: registration-detail-sheet Billing tab always shows a "Charge to:" status row in view mode ("Cleveland Clinic · attendee is guarantor · Ref PO-12345" or "Attendee — self-pay"), so organizers don't have to click Edit to see the current state. **Tests**: +10 new attach/detach cases (RBAC for MEMBER, IDOR org-binding on both ends, inactive-payer 400, upsert idempotency on POST, deleteMany idempotency on DELETE). Suite 1205 → 1215. tsc + lint + build clean. **Software-engineering name**: this is a **many-to-many association via a junction (associative / link / bridge) table** with **shared identity** — the BillingAccount is referenced by multiple Events through the junction, never duplicated. In DDD terms, BillingAccount is its own aggregate; the junction makes per-event availability an explicit relationship rather than ownership. Package unchanged at 0.3.7 (no MCP-visible tool surface change).

- **"Charge to another account" — third-party payer / BillingAccount (May 19, 2026)** — Doctors are often paid for by their hospital or by a pharma grant covering a specific HCP. New reusable org-scoped `BillingAccount` model (the payer) + `Registration.billingAccountId` / `payerReference` / `attendeeIsGuarantor`. **Orthogonal to `paymentStatus` by design** (the explicit anti-INCLUSIVE decision): money is still owed and the registration stays UNPAID/PENDING — this only redirects the invoice *bill-to* party and suppresses the attendee Pay-Now path. Distinct from `Event.settings.sponsors[]` (bulk pre-paid INCLUSIVE) and the `Registration.billing*` block (same payer, different address). Migration `20260519120000_add_billing_account` is purely additive (every existing reg defaults to self-pay). **Service**: [src/services/billing-account-service.ts](src/services/billing-account-service.ts) (create/update, soft-delete via `isActive`, `@@unique([organizationId,name])` dedupe → `DUPLICATE_NAME` with existing id in meta, errors-as-values, audit). **Registration wiring**: `registration-service.createRegistration` + REST POST + REST PUT + MCP `create_registration`/`update_registration` accept the three fields with org-scoped+active validation (new codes `BILLING_ACCOUNT_NOT_FOUND` / `BILLING_ACCOUNT_INACTIVE`); PUT/MCP `billingAccountId:null` reverts to self-pay (the fallback path). **Invoice/Quote PDF**: bill-to renders the payer (name/address/VAT) with the attendee dropped to a reference line + PO/grant ref ([src/lib/quote-pdf.ts](src/lib/quote-pdf.ts), [src/lib/invoice-pdf.ts](src/lib/invoice-pdf.ts), [src/lib/invoice-service.ts](src/lib/invoice-service.ts)). **Finance boundary**: `billingAccount`/`billingAccountId`/`payerReference`/`attendeeIsGuarantor` added to `FINANCIAL_KEYS` — MEMBER never sees who funds a doctor (Mecomed-sensitive); BillingAccount REST routes ([src/app/api/billing-accounts/route.ts](src/app/api/billing-accounts/route.ts) + `[billingAccountId]`) are `denyFinance`+`denyReviewer` gated, org-scoped. **UI**: `BillingAccountsCard` in Settings → Billing (CRUD + soft-delete + needs-review badge); payer picker + PO + guarantor on the full-page Add Registration form; reassign/guarantor/revert + "Billed to" pill on the registration detail sheet's finance-gated Billing tab. Package 0.3.6 → 0.3.7. **Tests**: +13 (billing-account-service, registration-service payer cases, finance redaction). Suite 1195 → 1205; tsc + lint + build clean. **Deferred to v1.1** (tracked in ROADMAP): public-registration "who pays" step (schema/route already carry `needsReview` for the dedupe flow), the quick-Add *dialog* picker (consistent with its existing pricingTier/sponsor gap), standalone `list/create_billing_account` MCP tools (payer mgmt is a Settings task; the agent assigns existing payers via the create/update params), registrations-list "Payer" column + CSV, AR aging by payer, VAT reverse-charge by payer taxNumber (v1 prints the number but does NOT change the rate — finance-correctness), consolidated invoicing, auto-revert-on-nonpayment cron.

- **Multi-agent audit remediation — 2 BLOCKERs + 4 HIGHs (May 18, 2026)** — A supervisor + 4 specialist review agents (React, Prisma, backend/RBAC, architecture) swept the codebase; the six findings verified against source were fixed in one batch. **(B1) Cross-tenant IDOR on event email templates** — [src/app/api/events/[eventId]/email-templates/[templateId]/route.ts](src/app/api/events/%5BeventId%5D/email-templates/%5BtemplateId%5D/route.ts) GET/PUT/DELETE/POST/PATCH resolved the template by `{ id, eventId }` (both from the URL) with **zero `organizationId` binding** — any authenticated user in any org could read/overwrite/reset/delete another org's templates or exfiltrate rendered content via POST `action:"test"`. All five handlers now bind the event to `session.user.organizationId` (404, not 403, to avoid enumeration) before touching the template, mirroring the sibling list route. **(B2) `soldCount` never released on cancel via MCP** — REST PUT decremented `TicketType.soldCount` on →CANCELLED and re-incremented on reactivate, but MCP `update_registration` only adjusted soldCount on ticket-type change and `bulk_update_registration_status` was a bare `updateMany` with none — so "cancel all unpaid registrations" via the agent/n8n silently inflated soldCount and the event **falsely reported sold-out, rejecting paying registrants**. Both MCP paths in [src/lib/agent/tools/registrations.ts](src/lib/agent/tools/registrations.ts) now mirror REST: single-update gets the four-case branch (becoming-cancelled→decrement / reactivating→capacity-guarded increment with `CAPACITY_EXCEEDED` / type-change / no-op) and bulk groups affected rows per ticket type inside a transaction (cancel→decrement, reactivate→increment; bulk reactivation may oversell but logs `registration:bulk-reactivate-oversold` rather than failing 200 rows — single-row still hard-blocks). **(H3) Registrations LIST finance leak** — [src/app/api/events/[eventId]/registrations/route.ts](src/app/api/events/%5BeventId%5D/registrations/route.ts) GET returned full `payments` (amount, cardLast4, receiptUrl, bank ref) + prices with no redaction while detail/tickets/event GETs redacted for MEMBER; now `redactFinancialFields` when `orgCtx.role` is a non-finance role (API-key auth, `role:null`, stays full — admin-equivalent, MEMBER can't mint keys). **(H4) Contacts write-guard bypass** — `contacts/route.ts`, `contacts/[contactId]/route.ts` (PUT+DELETE), `contacts/bulk-tags`, `contacts/import`, `contacts/[contactId]/email` used inline `ctx.role === "REVIEWER" || "SUBMITTER"`, letting **MEMBER + REGISTRANT write/delete org contacts**. All six sites now route through `denyReviewer({ user: { role: ctx.role ?? undefined } })` (single source of truth — blocks REVIEWER/SUBMITTER/REGISTRANT/MEMBER; API-key `role:null`→undefined passes as before). **(H5) PaymentStatus enum drift** — `ALL_PAYMENT_STATUSES` in [src/lib/agent/tools/_shared.ts](src/lib/agent/tools/_shared.ts) was a hand-list missing `INCLUSIVE`, so MCP `update_registration`/`bulk_update_registration_status` rejected INCLUSIVE as invalid and the sponsor-paid handling downstream was unreachable; now derived from `Object.values(PaymentStatus)` (the generated Prisma enum) so it cannot drift, and the local `PAYMENT_STATUSES` filter list in `registrations.ts` (was also missing UNASSIGNED+INCLUSIVE) collapsed to the same derived set. **(H6) `getNextSerialId` race** — [src/lib/registration-serial.ts](src/lib/registration-serial.ts) used `aggregate(_max: serialId) + 1`, which takes no row lock under Read Committed even in a transaction → concurrent registrations collided on `@@unique([eventId, serialId])` and the public register route mis-reported the P2002 as "You are already registered". Replaced with an atomic upsert+increment on a new `RegistrationSerialCounter` table (one row per event, PK `eventId`, `onDelete: Cascade`); migration `20260518120000_add_registration_serial_counter` is additive + backfills `lastSerial = MAX(serialId)` per event so it's blue-green safe (old container keeps MAX+1 against an untouched table; first new-code increment yields the same MAX+1; `@@unique` remains the net). **Tests**: +20 (auth-guards MEMBER/REGISTRANT/undefined cases; new `agent-payment-status-set`, `registration-serial`, `registration-cancel-soldcount`, `api/events/email-templates/idor`). Suite 1175 → 1195. Package 0.3.5 → 0.3.6 (MCP cache-invalidation hint — agent tool *behavior* changed). Verification: tsc + lint + 1195 vitest + build clean. **Corroborated-but-not-yet-fixed** (deferred, tracked): accommodation overbooking TOCTOU, registration DELETE deleting a shared Attendee, `PricingTier.soldCount` one-way leak on delete/bulk-type, Stripe post-payment invoice/email fire-and-forget with no reconciliation, registrant invoice/quote routes missing `denyFinance`, `refreshEventStats` lost-update, ~8 silent `safeParse`→400 sites, frontend silent failures (bulk-tag toast, registrant portal "no registrations" on fetch error), MCP finance boundary / OAuth role-snapshot, blue-green non-additive-migration guardrail. Doc drift noted: CLAUDE.md says `src/middleware.ts` (now `src/proxy.ts`, Next 16.1 rename) and "0 silent Invalid-input paths" (false) and stdio MCP "drifts" (stale — now shares `registerAllMcpTools()`).

- **Admin full pricing-tier control on manual add (May 18, 2026)** — The manual Add Registration full-page form ([src/app/(dashboard)/events/[eventId]/registrations/new/page.tsx](src/app/(dashboard)/events/%5BeventId%5D/registrations/new/page.tsx)) filtered the Pricing Tier picker to `isActive` tiers only, so organizers couldn't record a late registrant at a *closed* Early Bird rate as a courtesy. The backend (`registration-service.ts`) already only validated tier→ticket-type membership (no `isActive` requirement), so the restriction was a frontend-only artifact. Fix: `activeTiers` → `availableTiers` (drop the `.filter(isActive)`), POST guard validates against the full set, inactive tiers render as `Early Bird (inactive) — USD 400` so the admin picks informed, ticket-type Select hides the `- $X` suffix when the type has **any** tiers (the tier dropdown is the source of truth on this path). **Asymmetry preserved by design**: the public self-register path (`/api/public/events/[slug]/register`) still gates `isActive: true`. **The add-registration *dialog* has no tier picker** (the full-page form is the only tier-selection surface); its `isActive` price-suffix check is correctly scoped and unchanged. **Accepted tradeoffs, documented in a block comment at [src/services/registration-service.ts](src/services/registration-service.ts) tier-validation** (organizer decision — leave as-is, don't re-add the restriction): (1) the manual path bumps only `ticketType.soldCount`, never `PricingTier.soldCount`, so a manually-assigned (esp. closed) tier does **not** consume that tier's inventory and is never blocked by its quantity/closed cap — intentional, a courtesy seat must not burn a real paid Early Bird seat; consequence is `PricingTier.soldCount` under-counts vs actual rows, so the "Registrations by Tier" dashboard tile (counts rows, not soldCount — correct) is authoritative and anything reporting off `PricingTier.soldCount` directly will diverge; (2) tier is now an explicit assignment, not a proxy for "registered during that sales window" — an Early Bird row may have a `createdAt` after Early Bird closed, so finance reconciliation must treat tier as stated, not derived from registration date / `salesEnd`; (3) only ticket-type membership is enforced, not "the right tier within that type" — the field is as accurate as the admin's click. **All reporting verified accurate**: dashboard tile, list "Tier" column, CSV export, and `computeRegistrationFinancials` (subtotal = `pricingTier?.price ?? ticketType?.price`) all resolve the tier by id with no `isActive` gate, so a courtesy-rate registration is correctly named, counted, and priced. Verification: tsc + lint + build clean, 1175/1175 unit tests passing. Commit `434a45e` (feature) + this doc/comment follow-up.

- **Workflow tiles on Communications page (May 14, 2026)** — The 4-filter intersection model added in the previous round was technically powerful but cognitively heavy. Flipped to a **tiles + escape hatch** layout: each audience card (Registrations, Speakers) now opens with a grid of one-click workflow tiles at the top, with the existing dropdown filter grid moved into a collapsed `<details>Advanced filters</details>` block. **Speakers tiles** (6): Send Invitations (status=INVITED → invitation), Chase Agreements (CONFIRMED + unsigned → agreement), Brief Moderators (sessionRole=MODERATOR → custom), Brief Chairpersons (sessionRole=CHAIRPERSON → custom), Active Faculty (CONFIRMED + signed + hasSession → custom), Reinvite Declined (DECLINED → invitation). **Registrations tiles** (4): Chase Unpaid (CONFIRMED + UNPAID → custom), Welcome Paid (CONFIRMED + PAID/COMPLIMENTARY/INCLUSIVE → confirmation), Pre-event Reminder (CONFIRMED → reminder), Cancelled Re-engagement (CANCELLED → custom). Each tile shows a live recipient count (disabled at 0). Tile click bypasses the page-level filter state entirely (so an in-progress Advanced composition isn't clobbered), pushes filter combo + email type straight to the dialog. **Backend untouched** — tiles are pure frontend pre-set over `executeBulkEmail`. **New dialog prop** `defaultEmailType?: string` on [src/components/bulk-email-dialog.tsx](src/components/bulk-email-dialog.tsx) honored only on the closed → open transition, via React's "store info from previous render" pattern (set-during-render guarded by prev-value state) — `useEffect + setState` is banned under React 19's `react-hooks/set-state-in-effect`. **Welcome Paid caveat**: dialog payload supports one `paymentStatus` at a time so the tile narrows to PAID on send; matching predicate stays broad (PAID/COMPLIMENTARY/INCLUSIVE) so the count is accurate; sending to COMPLIMENTARY / INCLUSIVE separately needs Advanced filters. **Deferred**: organizer-saved tiles via `Event.settings.savedSegments[]`, tiles for Abstracts / Reviewers, multi-value `paymentStatus IN (...)` filter, audit `triggerLabel` field. Verification: tsc + lint + build clean, 1152/1152 unit tests passing.

- **Registration Type picker — drop misleading "- $0" suffix (May 14, 2026)** — On the Add Registration full-page form and dialog, the Registration Type Select rendered "Allied Health - $0" / "Physician - $0" etc. because when a type uses pricing tiers the base `TicketType.price` is typically 0 (real prices live on the tiers). The `$0` suffix read as "this is free" when the actual price comes from the Pricing Tier picker to the right. Rule: TicketType has active tiers → show just the name (Pricing Tier dropdown is the source of truth); no tiers + price > 0 → keep `Name - $X`; no tiers + price = 0 → just the name (same misleading-$0 cleanup for free / non-tier types). Applied to both surfaces ([src/app/(dashboard)/events/[eventId]/registrations/new/page.tsx:193](src/app/(dashboard)/events/%5BeventId%5D/registrations/new/page.tsx#L193) + [src/app/(dashboard)/events/[eventId]/registrations/add-registration-dialog.tsx:163](src/app/(dashboard)/events/%5BeventId%5D/registrations/add-registration-dialog.tsx#L163)). Public registration page handles tier-aware pricing in its own way and is unaffected. Shared `registration-type-select` doesn't render prices and is unaffected. Commit `af25e74`.

- **Communications page filters expansion (May 14, 2026)** — Two-part fix bringing the Communications page audience cards closer to parity with the registrations list page and what the bulk-email backend already supported. **Registrations card 2 → 3 filters**: added **Registration Status** dropdown (All / Pending / Confirmed / Checked In / Cancelled with live counts) at [src/app/(dashboard)/events/[eventId]/communications/page.tsx](src/app/(dashboard)/events/%5BeventId%5D/communications/page.tsx). Pure UI wiring — backend already accepted `filters.status` ([src/lib/bulk-email.ts:331-339](src/lib/bulk-email.ts#L331-L339)) but the Communications page was hard-coding `activeStatusFilter` to `undefined` on the registrations branch of `openEmailDialog`, so the filter was only usable from the speakers card or the registrations list page. **Speakers card 1 → 4 filters**: three new dimensions, all three-state dropdowns with live counts. (a) **Agreement** — All / Signed / Unsigned, drives the canonical "send the agreement to everyone who hasn't signed yet" workflow, mirrors the existing MCP `list_speaker_agreements` filter. (b) **Has Session** — All / Has Session / No Session, separates active faculty (presentation guidelines, AV setup) from backup invitees. (c) **Session Role** — All / Speaker / Moderator / Chairperson / Panelist, targets role-specific briefings in a single bulk send instead of four manual ones. `sessionRole` implies "has session" naturally via the same `SessionSpeaker` join, so the filters combine freely without conditional UI. **Backend** ([src/lib/bulk-email.ts](src/lib/bulk-email.ts)): `BulkEmailFilters` type + Zod schema gain `agreementSigned: "signed" | "unsigned"`, `hasSession: "yes" | "no"`, `sessionRole: SessionRole`. Speakers `where` extension uses `agreementAcceptedAt: null` / `{ not: null }` and `sessions: { some/none: ... }`. **Speakers GET API** ([src/app/api/events/[eventId]/speakers/route.ts](src/app/api/events/%5BeventId%5D/speakers/route.ts)) adds `sessions: { select: { role: true } }` to the existing include — reuses the same SessionSpeaker join Prisma was already doing for `_count.sessions`, so the page filter counts stay accurate client-side. **Dialog** ([src/components/bulk-email-dialog.tsx](src/components/bulk-email-dialog.tsx)) gains three optional pass-through props (`agreementSignedFilter`, `hasSessionFilter`, `sessionRoleFilter`) threaded into the POST `filters` payload (speakers-recipient only, "all" skipped), plus three recap lines in the dialog's "Filtered by …" summary.
